INTRODUCTION
Dear learner, you are welcome to this section which discusses the foundation 
of language (speech sounds). You will be introduced to the concepts of vowels 
and consonants of your language of study and how speech sounds are described 
(parametre). It will focus on where the speech sounds occur in words of a Ghanaian 
language. For example, where vowels and consonants can occur in a word of a 
Ghanaian language such as initial position, medial position, or final position of 
a word. Again, Dear learner you will be introduced to the distribution of vowels 
and consonants in their language, aiding them to form meaningful words and 
facilitate effective speaking and reading in the language. This section is essential 
for learners not only in the context of Ghanaian language studies but also to 
establish links with related subjects such as English and other languages. This 
section equips you with foundational knowledge and functional understanding 
of speech sounds and their role in language learning. In summary, you should be 
able to identify, explain, produce, and label vowel charts and consonant tables of 
your language of study.
After this section, you should be able to:
1. Describe the vowels of a Ghanaian language using the right parameters 
(e.g., lip posture, tongue height and part of the tongue).
2. Describe the consonants of the Ghanaian language using the right 
parameters (e.g., voicing, place of articulation and manner of articulation).
3. Explain the distribution of vowels of the Ghanaian language (e.g., word 
initial, medial and final).
4. Explain the distribution of consonants of the Ghanaian language (e.g., 
word initial, medial and final).

Key ideas
	 Production refers to the making or saying of a speech sound in language. 
Speech sound is a sound used in the formation of words for human 
communication. The production of speech sound involves obstruction 
which is the interruption of free flow of air during production of speech 
sounds. Sounds are distributed in languages and this refers to the place 
or position in a word where a sound can appear. Sound involves airflow 
which is a mass movement of air that is meant for the production of 
speech sounds. Another term for it is airstream.
TYPES OF SPEECH SOUNDS
Speech sounds can be grouped into two main types, namely vowels and consonants. 
It is the combination of these two types of sounds that produces words. In other 
words, all words are made up of individual speech sounds. For examples, the word 
pan consists of three individual speech sounds, that is, /p/, /a/, /n/. The sound /a/ 
is a vowel, whereas the sounds /p/ and /n/ are consonants. In the following topics 
we discuss both vowels and consonants focusing on how each is produced in a 
Ghanaian language.
The concept of vowel
The concept vowel refers as a speech sound in which production there is a little or 
no obstruction of the flow of air in the oral cavity. In other words, a speech sound 
which when being produced the air is not obstructed or it is minimally obstructed 
in the oral cavity is referred to as a vowel. Since in their production there is no 
or very little obstruction of airflow, vowels are comparatively heard louder when 
they are produced. V owels are very important part of words. There cannot be a 
word without a vowel or vowel-like sound. This important role vowel plays in a 
word will later on in your second year be discussed when we are talking about 
the syllable.
Description of vowels
Dear learner, in describing vowels of a Ghanaian language, there are certain 
properties we use. These properties are often termed parametres. Parametres 
simply refer to the characteristics that a vowel possesses. The main parametres

used in describing vowels are the tongue height, lip posture, and part of the tongue 
used during the production of the vowel sound. In addition to the three, there 
is a fourth parameter called advancement of the tongue root in some Ghanaian 
languages such as Akan. Let us begin the discussions of these parametres.
Lip position/posture:
The parametre lip posture is used to determine the position your lips assume 
when you are producing a vowel. So, at this level, the lips assume two main 
postures or positions, namely rounded or unrounded. That is, whether the lips are 
rounded or they are not rounded when a vowel sound is being produced. Based 
on this posture of the lips, we can divide vowels of a Ghanaian language into two, 
namely ‘rounded’ and ‘spread/unrounded.’ Some examples of rounded vowels 
are /u, o, ɔ/. examples of unrounded vowels, on the other hand, are /i, e, a/.
Activity
At this point, produce rounded and unrounded/spread vowels of your Ghanaian 
language of study.
Tongue height/Height of the tongue:
This refers to the position of the tongue in reference to the root of the mouth when 
producing vowel sounds. It is assumed that when we are producing vowels, the 
mouth opens when we drop the jaw. This can be high, mid, or low. When we 
drop our jaws to the lowest possible position, the vowels produced in this way are 
referred to as low vowels. Examples of low vowel is /a/, and in some Ghanaian 
languages [æ]. When we open our mouth wide enough but not as low as when 
producing low vowels, then the vowels we produced are termed mid vowels. 
Some examples of mid vowels in a Ghanaian language are /e, o/. In producing 
high vowels, on the other hand, the mouth is significantly opened but not as wide 
as mid vowels, thereby allowing enough air to flow through the oral cavity. Some 
examples of high vowels in a Ghanaian language are /i, u/.
Activity
Begin practicing the production of vowels in your language of study focusing 
on how high or how low you raise your jaws or open your mouth.

Part of the tongue:
This parametre refers to the area of the tongue where the vowel sound is produced. 
It is assumed that when we are producing vowels, some parts of the tongue 
move. We cannot easily feel this movement though. Three parts of the tongue 
are assumed to be involved when a vowel sounds is being produced. These parts 
are the front part, middle part, and back part. Based on that, the parametre gives 
us three classes of vowels, namely front, mid, and back vowels. In producing 
front vowels, it is the front part of the tongue that moves. Some examples of front 
vowels of a Ghanaian language are /i, e, ɛ/. For the production of mid vowels, 
the middle of the tongue is assumed to move. Therefore, the following vowel is 
an example of a mid-vowel: /a/. For back vowels, on the other hand, as the name 
suggests, it is the back of the tongue that is involved in their production. Some 
examples of back vowels of a Ghanaian language are: /u, o, ɔ/.
Activity
Practice how to produce vowels of your language of study with focus on the 
part of the tongue.
Having finished discussing the main parametres we use in describing vowels of 
a Ghanaian language, there is a fourth parametre as mentioned earlier in this 
sub-strand which is not common among Ghanaian languages. This parametre is 
advancement of the tongue.
Advancement of the tongue root (ATR): (Please, dis-cuss only if applicable in your language)
This parametre, which is prominent in a few Ghanaian languages including Akan, 
Dagbani, etc. It is used to determine the position the tongue root assumes when a 
vowel is being produced. By this parametre, we try to find out if there is tension 
or pressure on the tongue or not during production of vowels. When a vowel is 
produced with pressure on the tongue thereby causing the tongue root to draw 
back, we say that vowel is produced with Advanced Tongue Root (ATR) i.e. 
(+ATR) vowels. When vowels are produced with the tongue root in its natural 
neutral position, we label those vowels are Unadvanced Tongue Root i.e. (-ATR) 
vowels. Some examples of (+ATR) vowels are: /i, e, u, o/, and examples of (-ATR) 
vowels are /ɪ, ɛ, ɔ/.

Having discussed the nature of vowel sounds and the parametres used in describing 
the vowel sounds of your language, we now focus our attention on the production 
of consonants.
The concept of consonant
As was mentioned earlier in the section, consonant is another type of speech 
sounds apart from vowel. The concept consonant refers to a speech sound in 
which during production the breath, which we have termed airflow, is at least 
obstructed. Based on this explanation, we can contrast vowel and consonant by 
saying that while in the production of vowel there is very minimal or no obstruction 
of airflow, there is significant obstruction of airflow when producing consonants. 
We combined vowels and consonants form a word.

Consonant Distribution
The concept consonant distribution simply refers to the position in a word where a consonant 
can occur in a particular Ghanaian language. A consonant that occurs at the beginning of a 
word is referred to as word initial consonant. When a consonant occurs at the middle of a word, 
we refer to it as word medial consonant. When a consonant occurs at the end of a word, we 
refer to refer to it as word final consonant. Let us note that some consonants can occur in all 
positions of a word. For example, in some Ghanaian languages, the consonant /m/ can occur in 
the three positions in a word.
In the following activities, we will consider consonants of a Ghanaian language 
and the position the consonants can occur in a word.

ORAL CONVERSATION
Conversation/Communication in Context
INTRODUCTION
This section discusses identification of key ideas in texts and discourse. It 
always gives information on specific ideas or knowledge to the reader or hearer. 
The information given may come from all perspectives such as education, 
industrialisation, mining among others. It may also indicate some cultural values 
such as respect, tolerance and patience. Identifying key ideas gives you a better 
understanding of the discourse. It also enhances your critical thinking skills and 
interpretation abilities. There are types of reading techniques namely skimming 
and scanning and the application of any of the type enables you to get the right 
information demanded at any time. Knowledge of the types is therefore essential 
in our everyday life. The concept of oral interpretation will also be discussed. We 
shall discuss the skills needed for effective interpretation. Interpretation plays 
important roles in facilitating communication across language barriers.
After this section, you should be able to:
• Identify key ideas from appropriate discourse. E.g., cultural values 
(respect, kindness, tolerance and others), education, child trafficking, 
environment, industrialisation in Ghana, mining, GESI etc.,
• Discuss ideas and relevant opinions from selected discourse. E.g., 
cultural values (respect, kindness, tolerance and others), education, 
child trafficking, environment, industrialisation in Ghana, mining, GESI, 
STEM, etc.
Key Ideas
Key ideas are the main messages that is relevant in any discourse. Some 
of the key ideas may center on cultural values such as respect, kindness, 
tolerance, patience, etc. In any discourse you can share relevant opinions 
on any discourse appropriately and interpret any discourse in your own 
understanding.

 The main points you shared with your peers are known to as key ideas. Key ideas 
are the essential ideas that the author or speaker wants to give to the reader or hearer/
listener respectively. The ideas may include the claims, the reasons, conclusions, 
definitions, classifications, comparisons, evaluations, recommendations, etc. Key 
ideas can be expressed explicitly or implicitly.
For you to identify the key ideas in discourse there is the need for you to understand 
the main concepts, arguments, and the points made. Note that the discourse 
could deal with any topic such as mining, teenage pregnancy, natural disaster, 
educational issues among others. It must also be pointed out that it could also 
come in a text form, video or picture or all the forms mentioned.
In summary, my dear learner to identify the key ideas in a discourse which may be 
written or oral or visual, you may need to answer the following questions
• Find who or what the passage discusses: Does this passage discuss a person, 
group of people or an entity?
• Ask when the event took place: Does the information contain a reference to 
time?
• Find where the event took place: Does the text name a place?
• Ask why the event took place: Do you find a reason or explanation for 
something that happened?
• Ask how the event took place: Does this information indicate a method or a 
theory?
NB: In a text, key ideas are sometimes italicised, boldened, or underlined. You 
can also find it in the topic sentence.
What is discourse
Generally, discourse refers to communication, conversation or discussion between 
individuals or groups either in spoken form or written form. It involves the 
exchange of ideas, opinions and information. Note that the definition of discourse 
could be defined also from different angles such as linguistics, social science and 
philosophy. The general meaning is appropriate for us. Go online to read the other 
definitions to broaden your knowledge.

Key ideas
Skimming is going through a text rapidly to get the general information in 
the text while scanning involves looking for a specific information in a text. 
Scanning is a process of reading in which your eyes quickly run through a 
piece of text to find a piece of relevant information. Scanning and skimming 
are two different concepts of reading.
TYPES OF READING
There are types of reading skill or technique namely skimming, scanning, 
intensive reading and extensive reading. Dear learner, in this lesson you shall 
learn skimming and scanning techniques of reading.
Skimming
Skimming is a reading technique used to quickly identify the main ideas or key 
points in a text. It is the action of reading something quickly so as to note only the 
important points. Basically, skimming is reading rapidly in order to get a general 
overview of the material read. It is used to find specific facts in texts. It involves 
glancing over the material, focusing on headings, subheadings, bold text and key 
phrases to get a general understanding of the content. Skimming is useful when; 
time is limited, looking for specific information, you want to get an overview 
before reading in-depth and you are dealing with a large amount of text. Below 
are the skimming types.

1. Preview: An opportunity to view something before it is acquired or becomes 
generally available. Preview is done in an effort to learn about the ideas 
presented and the structure of their development.
2. Overview: Used to sample the reading material more thoroughly. A general 
review or summary of a subject.
3. Review: The review is done to re-familiarise yourself with the material 
you have previously read thoroughly or skimmed. A formal assessment of 
something with the intention of instituting a change if necessary.
Learner, in skimming, you can follow these steps
i. Read the title
ii. Read the headings and sub-headings as well as topic sentences in each 
paragraph
iii. Look for important information such as date, names and unusual words.
iv. Read the conclusion

In summary you have learnt skimming and the steps as well as the types of 
skimming which you can apply. Dear learner, let us examine what is scanning.
Scanning
Scanning is reading rapidly in order to find facts without reading everything. 
Scanning helps you locate a particular fact while skimming tells you what general 
information is within a section.
Scanning involves looking for a specific information in a text. It can also be said 
to be a process of reading in which your eyes quickly run through a piece of text 
to find a piece of relevant information. In scanning the reader looks for a piece 
of specific information. An example of scanning is searching for the meaning 
of a word in a dictionary. Scanning helps the reader to locate particular facts in 
an entire text quickly. Students often use scanning when solving their reading 
comprehension questions.
It is important to know the purpose for scanning. You should know what you are 
searching for, eg title of a book, a website, a reference material, a particular word 
or phrase and a particular story you want to read etc. You should know how the 
material is structures either alphabetically, non-alphabetically, chronologically, 
by category, by titles /headings, by textual sense, by numbers among others.

Scanning helps a learner to read more and to develop love for reading.
When to scan
1. Scan before reading
2. Scan a number of questions to identify the one which you are most 
comfortable answering
3. When searching for particular information such as date, keywords etc.
The following shows how to do scanning after getting overview of a text and 
identifying the sections of the text you want to read.
1. Start scanning the text by moving your eyes and fingers quickly over it
2. When you have identified the information, word or the phrase you are 
searching for, read the information surrounding the word carefully
3. When you identified the information that requires attention, you read it 
thoroughly slowly.

Oral Interpretation and Translation
After this section, you should be able to:
Discuss oral interpretation focusing on effective listening, encoding and 
decoding,
Key Ideas
Oral interpretation is reframing the meaning of a speech most often orally 
into another language. The original language is the source language and the 
language in which it is rendered is the target language. In oral interpretation 
you must note the cultural differences and be accurate in giving the meaning 
of what you are to render in the language orally.
INTERPRETATION
Interpretation is listening to a message in one language and rendering it orally 
in another language maintaining the original meaning, tone and context. It 
is the stylistic representation of a creative work or dramatic role. It is the act 
of explaining, reframing, or otherwise showing your own understanding of 
something. In interpretation you first have to understand the text or the piece 
given to you and then explain in your own words. In broader terms it is rendering 
a spoken or signed message into another spoken or signed language preserving 
the register and meaning of the source language content.
Dear learner, it must be noted that before you can do any interpretation, you must 
be well versed in the source and target language. Interpretation can be performed 
either simultaneously or consecutively between users of different languages.
Dear learner, know that in interpreting you do not embellish or over-exaggerate. 
State the ideas clearly. In interpreting you need to listen carefully, decode and 
encode as they serve as the process of communication and interpreting.

SECTION 3  
Yetumi de oyikyerɛ, akontabude anaa edin nkyerɛkyerɛmu bata ho. Ɛho nhwɛso 
no mu bi ne pɛn, nhoma, pɛnsere, ofi, dan, apataa, ɛpo, atumpan,gyaade, sekan.
Edin a yenhu
Eyi yɛ nsɛmfua a ɛda nsusui bi ana ade bi a yɛmfa yɛn ani nhu adi. Eyi gyina hɔ ma nneɛma bi 
a yenhu ana yɛsɔ mu nso a ɛnyɛ yie. Ɛtaa kyerɛkyerɛ nkatede, nsusui ne atenka. Eyi ho nhwɛso 
no mu bi ne anigye, ɔdɔ, awerɛhow, yawdi, nokware, nyansa, ne nea ɛkeka ho.
Edin a yehu
Eyi yɛ edin a yɛde ma nneɛma a yehu na yɛsɔ mu nso a ɛyɛ yie. Eyinom yɛ nneɛma a atwa yɛn 
ho ahyia wɔ asase yi so a yehu. Eyi ho nhwɛso no mu bi ne ɔpon, mpa, dɔte, sankuw, twene, 
ɔson ne nea ɛkeka ho.

iii. Fa edin ahorow a wohuii no mu biara yɛ ɔkasamu tiawa sɛ ebia, Me

Me kurom gua mu mpasatuw
Beae bi wɔ me kurom a ɛhɔ yɛ bagyabagya a yɛfrɛ hɔ guam. Ɛhɔ yɛ anigyebea 
hyia a ebinom tontɔn nneɛma ahorow na ebinom nso tɔ. Wubetumi anya nneɛma 
bi te sɛ nnuaba ahorow ne atosode, afade, nkuaba ne nneɛma ahorow a yɛde di 
dwuma wɔ efie nyinaa bi wɔ hɔ.
Nnawɔtwe awiei biara no me ne m’abusuafo kɔ guam hɔ kodi gua. Sɛ yɛreyɛ adu 
hɔ a, mete sɛ adetɔnfo rebɔ wɔn aguadetɔn ho dawuru ne adetɔfo nso a wɔnenam 
guam no mu bagyabagya redi gua nea ɛyɛ den.
Ade a midi kan huu wɔ guam hɔ yɛ nnuaba ne atosode a wɔahyehyɛ no fɛfɛɛfɛ wɔ 
mpata ahorow mu. Nneɛma no mu bi nso ne akutu a ɛyɛ dɛ yie, kwadu a abere, ne 
borɔfere a agyegye a ɛyɛ fɛ. Nnɔbae foforo a na wɔde aba guam no mu ho hwa no 
gyegye guam hɔ nyinaa na ɛmaa me ho pere me sɛ mɛkɔ akɔtotɔ emu nea ɛyɛ me 
akɔnnɔ no bi.
Bio, yɛkɔnenam sotɔɔ ahorow a wɔtɔn afade ne nneɛma ahorow nso mu. Mihuu 
hyɛɛte a ɛyɛ fɛ yie, sekɛte ne mpomporanne ahorow a ɛyɛ fɛ yie. M’ani gye sɛ 
mɛhwehwɛ mpaboa ahorow a wɔahyehyɛ no mu ahu nea mɛtɔ de akɔka nea mewɔ 
dedaw no ho.
Yɛkɔɔ so ara kyinkyin guam hɔ no, yɛkɔ huu sotɔɔ ahorow a na wɔtotɔn nkuaba ne 
kɔnmade ahorow fɛfɛ bi. Afei nso na nneɛma a yɛde gyegye mmofra agoru ahorow 
bi te sɛ, baalu, tɔe(tsoobi) ne nea ɛkeka ho nyinaa wɔ hɔ. Sɛnea na mmofra binom 
ani agye nneɛma a wɔde di agoru ahorow a na wɔahyehyɛ wɔ guam hɔ no ho yɛ 
me anika kɛkɛ.
Ne korakora no,yɛkɔduu beae a wɔtotɔn nneɛma a wɔde di adwuma ahorow wɔ 
efie. Aha yi no, na yehu nkukuw ne sereba ahorow a yɛnoanoa mu wɔ gyaade ne 
samina ahorow a yɛde si nneɛma ne nneɛma ahorow a yɛde siesie yɛn afi mu. Me 
maame tɔ ade bi a yehia a, me nso magye asoa.
Yɛbɛtoa yɛn adesua a ɛfa edin ahorow no so.

Edin a ɛkyerɛ kuw
Eyi nso yɛ edin a egyina hɔ ma kuw bi. Ekuw no betumi ayɛ nneɛma, mmoa ana nnipa. Eyi ho 
nhwɛso no mu bi ne kankyee, esa, saka, duru, dɔm, asafo, sukuu, abusua,kurow ne nea ɛkeka 
ho. Edin a ɛkyerɛ kuw biara yɛ baakofo a ɛmfa ho sɛ egyina hɔ ma nnipa, nneɛma ana mmoa 
ahorow bi.
Dwumadi 3
Montena baanu baanu na wɔmpɛ edin a ɛkyerɛ kuw ho nhwɛso anum anum 
nka nea yɛabobɔ dedaw no ho. Ma wɔne wɔn mfɛfo nkyɛ wɔn mmuae ahorow 
no.
Hwɛ ɔkasamu ahorow a ɛwɔ fam ha yi, na kyerɛ edin ahorow a wɔasensan ase

iv. Yɛpɛ nsu ntoa no.
v. Onipa a ɔnoa aduan ma me no de srade papa ankasa na ɛto keeki no.
vi. Mmarahyɛbeguafo dodow sɛn na wɔn ho behia ansa na wɔatumi ahyɛ 
mmara bi?
vii. Mmofra dodow no ara pɛ nufusu gye Yaw.
viii. Wɔde ntwoma na ayɛ kuku no mu dodow no ara.
ix. Dansoaa ne Safoah tumi bɔ asanku.
x. Ɔbrɛ dodow nti, medii twɔkoleti adaka baako.
Ne tiawatwam ne sɛ, yetumi kyekyɛ edin ahorow mu kɔ akuw ahorow akɛse abien mu a ɛnonom 
ne edin a yetumi kan ne nea yentumi nkan. Edin a yetumi kan yɛ edin a yetumi kan no mmiako 
mmiako ana yɛde akontabude toto ho a, ɛyɛ yie (sɛ ebia. P ɛn, atade, pɛnsere, siksbɔtɔ, papa, 
kyinii, amango, akutu,ne nea ɛkeka ho. Edin yentumi nkan yɛ edin a yɛde ma biribi yɛkan no 
mmiako mmiako a ɛnyɛ yie ana yɛde akontabude toto ho a, ɛnyɛ yi. Ɛho nhwɛso no mu bi ne 
ngo, ɔmo, nsu, amanebɔ ne nea ɛkeka ho. Ahwiede ne edin a yentumi nkan.

Edin nkyerɛkyerɛmu yeinom kasa fa nnipa ana nneɛma bi dodow ho. Akontabude

bi dodow pɔtee ho. Hwɛ nhwɛso a edidi so yi:

Sukyerɛ nkyerɛkyerɛmu yɛ nkyerɛkyerɛmu a ɛka birirbi fa edin bi su ana ne tebea

SECTION 3  
Dɛn ne adeyɛ?
Dɛn na woyɛɛ no anɔpa yi? Kyerɛwkyerɛw nea woyɛe no nyinaa.
Dɛn na wususuw fa nneɛma ahorow a wosua wɔ sukuu no mu ho? Kyerɛwkyerɛw 
wo nsusui no nyinaa.
Hyɛ no nso sɛ wo ne w’afɛfo bɛkyɛ wo nsusui ahorow no.
Adeyɛ asɛmfua ana nsɛmfua a ɛkyerɛ nea obi ɔyɛfo bi reyɛ. Adeyɛ san tumi yɛ 
asɛmfua ana nsɛmfua a ɛkyerɛ tebea a ɔyɛfo bi wom. (se ebia; so, nyini, hua, di, 
dɔ, si, som, hwɛ, hu ne nea ɛkeka ho).
Adeyɛ tumi ba ɔkasamu a ɛwɔ ɔyɛtia ana enni ɔyɛtia mu.Yetumi kyekyɛ adeyɛ mu 
nya f-ɔyɛtia, amfa-ɔyɛtia ne fa-ɔyɛtia abien.
Fa-ɔyɛtia
Fa-ɔyɛtia yɛ adeyɛ a ɛfa edin a edi dwuma sɛ ɔyɛtia di n’akyi wɔ ɔkasamu mu.Eyi 
ho nhwɛso no mu bi ne noa, nom, ka, saw, di, kyerɛw, boroo ne nea ɛkeka hoƐho 
nhwɛso no bi na yɛde ayɛ ɔkasamu wɔ fam ha yi:
1. Ɔkyerɛkyerɛfo no noaa ɔmo.
2. Adesuafo no saa nsu.
3. Kofi ne Adwoa di fufu.
4. Abofra no tɔɔ nnuaba.
5. Akwantufo no foroo kaa no.
Nsɛmfua a yɛakyeakyea no wɔ ɔkasamu no mu nyinaa yɛ fa-ɔyɛtia. Ɔyɛtia ahorow 
no nyinaa ba adeyɛ akyi. Nhwɛso 1 mu no, ɔyɛtia a ɛwom no ne ɔmo, ɛnna nhwɛso 
(5) mu no, ɔyɛtia a ɛwɔ mu no ne kaa .
Amfa-ɔyɛtia
Eyi nso yɛ adeyɛ a edin a edi n’akyi no nni dwuma sɛ ɔyɛtia-saa adeyɛ yi nhia 
ɔyɛtia ansa na ntease yi ada adi wɔ ɔkasamu mu. Asɛmfua ana nsɛmfua tumi di 
saa adeyɛ yi akyi no taa yɛ ɔkyerɛfo ana adeyɛ boafo. Saa adeyɛ yi ho nhwɛso no

Ɔkyerɛfo yɛ asɛmfua ana nsɛmfua a ɛkyerɛkyerɛ adeyɛ mu wɔ ɔkasamu mu. 
Ɔkyerɛfo tumi san kyerɛkyerɛ ɔkyerɛfo foforo mu. Dwen sɛnea wosi nantew kɔɔ 
sukuu nnɛ no ho, na ɛyɛ brɛoo,ntɛm ana ntɛmntɛm? Ebetumi aba sɛ wonantewee 
ntɛmntɛm kɔɔ sukuu. Asɛmfua ntɛmntɛm no kyerɛ sɛnea wosi nantew kɔɔ sukuu 
fae ne saa nti, ɛyɛ ɔkyerɛfo. Ɔkyerɛfo nkyekyɛmu ahorow no gyina sɛnea esi 
kyerɛkyerɛ mu no so. Nkyekyɛmu ahorow no ne: yɛbea kyerɛfo, beae kyerɛfo, 
bere kyerɛfo, dodow kyerɛfo, anoɔden kyerɛfo, ampayɛ/akyinnegye kyerɛfo.
Yɛbea kyerɛfo
Saa ɔkyerɛfo yi kyerɛkyerɛ ɔkwan a ɔyɛfo no fa so yɛ biribi ana sɛnea dwumadi 
bi si kɔ so fa mu. Ɛho nhwɛso na edidi so yi:
1. Osuani no nantewee ntɛmntɛm kɔɔ sukuu.
2. Bɔɔlobɔfo no bɔɔ bɔɔlo no brɛoo.
3.  Adwontofo no too dwom no bɔkɔɔ.
4. Anomaa no tuu ɔhareso.
Beae kyerɛfo
Beae kyerɛfo ka biribi fa beae a dwumadi kɔ so ana ɔyɛfo yɛ biribi ho. Ɛho nhwɛso 
no mu bi na edidi so yi:
1. Adesuafo no gyinagyina adiwo.
2. Kwasi ne Asɛmpa reda wɔ aborosan no so.
3. Adesuafo no toto nkrataa gugu baabiara.
4. Akosua Frempong fi Aburi.

Bere Kyerɛfo
Bere Kyerɛfo nso ka biribi fa bere pɔtee a dwumadi bi kɔ so ana bere pɔtee bi a 
ɔyɛfo bi yɛ biribi ho. Ɛho nhwɛso wɔ ɔkasamu mu na edidi so yi:
1. Adesuafo no kyerɛww sɔhwɛ no nnɛra.
2. Nnɛ yebedi yɛn awiabere aduan wɔ adwuma mu.
3. Yɛbɛyɛ yɛn nhyiamu anɔpa nnɔnkron.
Dodow kyerɛfo
Eyi nso kyerɛ mpɛn dodow a dwumadi bi kɔ so ana mpɛn dodow a ɔyɛfo bi 
reyɛ adwuma bi. Saa ɔkyerɛfo yi tumi di ɔkasamu anim ana akyi nanso ɔkyerɛfo 
ahorow no mu kakra bi na etumi di ɔkasamu anim/kan, mfinimfini ana akyi. 
Dodow kyerɛfo nhwɛso no mu bi ne afeafe, mprenu, mprɛnsa, prɛkopɛ, da, bere 
biara, nnawɔtwe-nnawɔtwe, da biara ne nea ɛkeka ho. Ɛho nhwɛso no mu bi na 
edidi so yi;
1. Wɔhyɛ fa afeafe.
2. Da biara yedidi.
3. Yɛnkɔɔ hɔ da.
4. Wɔhyɛ mmofra nkuran sɛ wɔntwitwiw wɔn se bere biara.
5. Meba ha nnawɔtwe-nnawɔtwe.
Ɔkasamu a ɛwowɔ soro hɔ no mu no, dodow kyerɛfo a ɛwowɔ mu nonom ne 
afeafe, da biara, da, bere biara ɛnna nnawɔtwe-nnawɔtwe . Nhwɛso (2) mu 
no, ɔkyerɛfo Da biara di ɔkasamu no anim. Nhwɛso (5) mu no nso, ɔkyerɛfo 
nnawɔtwe-nnawɔtwe di ɔkasamu no akyi.
Anoɔden kyerɛfo
Saa ɔkyerɛfo yi yɛ asɛmfua ana nsɛmfua a ɛkyerɛkyerɛ adeyɛ ana ɔkyerɛfo foforo 
bi mu de kyerɛ sɛnea dwumadi bi ano den si te anaa sɛnea ɔyɛfo bi dwumadi ano 
si te. Ɛho nhwɛsono mu bi ne yie, pa ara, dwerebee, sɛ, dodo, defedefe ne nea 
ɛkeka ho. Ɛho nhwɛso no mu bi na edidi so wɔ fam hɔ no:
1. Maame no kasa dodo.
2. Wɔpraa ɔdan no mu yie.
3. Na ne mmɔdenmmɔ no sɔ ani sɛ.
4. Abeawa no yɛɛ Agya Fosu defedefe.

Saa ɔfa yi kasa fa Akuapem Twi kyerɛwbea ho mmara ho. Yɛbɛkyerɛkyerɛ 
Akuapem Twi kyerɛwbea ho mmara a ɛfa edin, adeyɛ, edinnsiananmu ne edin 
nkyerɛkyerɛmu ho mu. Yebedi kan akyerɛkyerɛ kyerɛwbea ho mmara a ɛfa edin

nkyerɛkyerɛmu, adeyɛ ne ɔkyerɛfo ho. Eyi bɛboa wo ama woahu ɔkwan a yɛfa so 
de edin, edinnsiananmu, edin nkyerɛkyerɛmu ne ɔkyerɛfo di dwuma wɔ Akuapem 
Twi kasa mu. Yebetumi de saa kyerɛwbea ho mmara yi adi dwuma wɔ borɔfo 
kasa mu nso.
Adesua yi bɛkɔ awiei no, na wutumi:
1. Gyina edin ne dinnsiananmu ho mmara so kyerɛw ɔkasamu ahorow.
2. Gyina edin nkyerɛkyerɛmu ho mmara so kyerɛw ɔkasamu ahorow.
3. Gyina adeyɛ ne ɔkyerɛfo ho mmara so kyerɛw ɔkasamu ahorow.

• Edin di dwuma sɛ ɔyɛfo, ɔgyefo, edin nkyerɛkyerɛmu ne edin kasasin ti.

ɛrekyerɛkyerɛ mu no akyi wɔ Akuapem Twi kasa mu.

Ghana kasa ahorow no, dinnsiananmu di dwuma sɛ:
a. ɔyɛfo wɔ ɔkasamu mu. 
 Nhwɛso:
i. Mekɔɔ sukuu.
ii. Dabiara, yɛhwɛ sini.
iii. Wɔsere kwakwakwa.
b. Dinnsiananmu tumi san di dwuma sɛ ɔyɛtia wɔ ɔkasamu mu (ɔyɛtia anaa 
ogyefo). 
 Nhwɛso:
i. Kwasi huu no. (Ɔyɛtia).
ii. Ama de kyerɛwdua maa wɔn. (Ɔgyefo).
iii. Anima maa yɛn mpaboa bi. (Ɔgyefo)
iv. Ɔkyerɛkyeyrɛni no somaa mo (Ɔyɛtia).
c. Bio, Ghana kasa ahorow bi mu no, yɛkyerɛw dinnsiananmu a edi dwuma 
sɛ ɔyɛfo no ne adeyɛ a ɛtoa ne so no bom sɛ asɛmfua biako (Sɛ ebia., Ga, 
Akuapem Twi).
Dwumadi
1. Kyerɛkyerɛ din mu na ma ho nhwɛso du anaa nea ɛboro saa. Wo ne wo 
mfɛfo nkae no nkyɛ wo mmuae no.
2. Montena baanu baanu mfa nkyerɛw edin dwumadi ahorow no. Momfa 
kuw biako nka mo de no ho na mo mpɛnsɛmpɛnsɛm dwumadi no mu.
3. Kyerɛkyerɛ dinnsiananmu na ma ho nhwɛso du anaa nea ɛboro saa. Wo 
ne wo mfɛfo nkae no nkyɛ wo mmuae no.
a. Kenkan abasɛm a ɛwɔ fam hɔ no na momfa nhwehwɛ edin ne 
edinnsiananmu ahorow a ɛwowom.
b. Fa edin a wuhui no mu anum yɛ ɔkasamu mmɔho. Kae sɛ wo ne 
wo mfɛfo bɛkyɛ wo mmuae no.
c. Fa dinnsiananmu a wuhui no mu abiɛsa yɛ ɔkasamu. Kae sɛ wo 
ne wo mfɛfo bɛkyɛ mmuae no.

Nkraman
Wiase nnipa nyinaa nim sɛ, nkraman yɛ mmoa a yɛde wɔn gyegye yɛn ani. 
Wɔgu mu ahorow esiane wɔn su, wɔn bɔbea ne wɔn ahosu nti. Wɔyɛ mmoa bi 
a wɔwɔ nan anan a wɔfiri mpataku abusuakuw a na wɔte wuram no mu. Bere a 
yɛn nananom hyɛɛ ase yɛnn mpataku yi de wɔn yɛɛ aha no, wɔn ani begyee nnipa 
ho ma wɔkaa wɔn ho bɛnn nnipa. Wɔyɛ mmoa bi a wɔwɔ nkatede a wotumi de 
hu nnipa nneyɛe te sɛ ɔdɔ, ɔtan ne ahunahuna na wɔda ho suban adi kyerɛ nnipa 
biara sɛnea ne nneyɛe te pɛpɛɛpɛ. Ne nyinaa mu no, nkraman yɛ mmoa bi a wɔte 
pampan pa ara. Wɔsan nso yɛ mmoa a wɔte dede ahorow a ɛmfa ho sɛ ano yɛ den 
anaa ɛyɛ mmerɛw. Ade a ɛma nkraman som bo pa ara ne sɛ, wutumi tete wɔn ma 
wotumi di dwuma ahorow. Yɛwɔ nkraman a wotumi kyerɛ anifurafo kwan da 
biara ɛnna nkraman a wɔwɔ atenka sononko no nso tumi kyekyere nnipa a wɔn 
werɛ aho no werɛ. Wɔsan tumi de nkraman hwehwɛ gye afoforo nkwa na wotumi 
te pampan a mfiri mpo ntumi nte. Nnepa ahorow a nkraman tumi da no adi kyerɛ 
nnipa yi nyinaa akyi no, wɔn nkwanna nna sua a wɔanyin ara na bɛyɛ mfe du (10) 
kosi dunum (15) Wɔn som papa nti nnipa gye nkraman tom sɛ wɔn abusua wɔ 
wiase afanaa nyinaa.
Dwumadi
1. Kyerɛkyerɛ dwuma a nsɛmfua a yɛasan ase no mu biara redi wɔ ɔkasamu 
yi mu biara mu. Fa wo mmuae no toto wo mfɛfo de ho.
a. Adesuafo a wɔaben no tuu kwan nnera.
b. Mede sika manee Frempomaa wɔ Kade.
c. Ɔkyerɛkyerɛfo no kyerɛw kyerɛwpon mono no so.
d. Wɔfii hɔ kɔɔ Navrongo.
e. Ɔkwantuni no tɔɔ paano brɛɛ no.
7
MMƆAKYIRI NSƐMMISA
1. Fa w’ankasa nsɛmfua kyerɛkyerɛ edin a edi dwuma sɛ nkyerɛkyerɛmu 
mu. Ma eyi ho nhwɛso abien na wo ne wo mfɛfo nkyɛ adwen wɔ ho.
2. Wo kyerɛkyerɛni de abasɛm a mfomso wowom bɛma wo. Kenkan 
abasɛm a wo kyerɛkyerɛni de bɛma wo no na fa hwehwɛ mfomso a 
ɛwowom no.
3. Kyerɛkyerɛ dinnsiananmu dwumadi a ɛyɛ ɔyɛtia ne ɔgyefo no mu wɔ 
Akuapem Twi mu.
 Fa toto ɔkasa foforo bi a wunim anna wobɛpɛ sɛ wubesua ho.
4. Ma edin a edi dwuma sɛ edin kasasin ti ho nhwɛso anum wɔ ɔkasamu 
mu wɔ Akuapem Twi mu. Wo ne wo mfɛfo nkyɛ adwenkyerɛ.
5. Montena baanu baanu na monkyerɛw ɔkasamu ahorow du a 
edinnsiananmu a ɛwowɔ mu no redi dwuma sɛ ɔyɛfo. Fa toto Ghana 
kasa ahorow no ho na wo ne wo mfɛfo nkyɛ adwenkyerɛ no.

Woadi kan asua edin nkyerɛkyerɛmu ho ade pɛn. Montena akuwakuw na momfa 
edin nkyerɛkyerɛmu a mode bɛkyerɛkyerɛ nea edidi so yi biara mu nyɛɛ ɔkasamu 
abiɛsa abiɛsa.

b. W’adamfo pa
c. Wo sukuu mu
d. W’abusua

Ɔkasamu (b) mu nso, nsɛmfua teatea tenten kyerɛkyerɛ abarimaa no abɔsu.

ɔkwan a yɛfa so de edin nkyerɛkyerɛmu di dwuma wɔ ɔkasamu mu da nso wɔ

Edin nkyerɛkyerɛmu wɔ Akuapem Twi mu:
1. ɛkyerɛkyerɛ edin mu wɔ ɔkasamu mu. 
 Nhwɛso:

b. Mihuu efie kɛse bi.
2. Edin nkyerɛkyerɛmu no ba wɔ din a ɛrekyerɛkyerɛ mu no akyi pɛɛ. 
 Nhwɛso:
a. Akuapem Twi mu no, Efie tuntum no abu.
b. Ɔbea tumtum bi aba ha.

MMƆAKYIRI NSƐMMISA
1. Kenkan abasɛm yi na fa hwehwɛ edin nkyerɛkyerɛmu du a ɛwom.
 Nnipa bebree na wɔahu nsunsuanso a yɛn nneyɛe renya wɔ yɛn atenae 
so. Ɛsɛ te sɛ, yɛma yɛn atenae ho bammɔ ho hia yɛn pa ara kyɛn biribiara. 
Nanso, nnipa kakra bi na wɔwɔ nimde wɔ ɔkwan a yɛfa so bɔ yɛn atenae 
ho ban ho. Ɛnam ɛmfa-me- ho su a ɛwɔ yɛn mu no so rema yɛn atenae 
no sɛe da biara. Nhwɛso, nwura a yɛtoto gu basabasa, galamsee ne 
nnuabubu basabasa ne nea ɛkeka ho. Sɛ yɛannyae saa nneyɛe bɔne yi a, 
bere bi bɛba a, nkyirimma bedi amia wɔ yɛn nneyɛe bɔne ho nsunsuanso 
mu. Ɛyɛ me ne wo asɛde sɛ yɛbɛyɛ yɛn afam de abɔ yɛn atenae no ho 
ban. Ɛyɛ yɛn asodi kɛse sɛ yɛde nhyehyɛe papa begu akwan mu de abɔ 
ɔdomankoma agyapade a ɔde ama yɛn no ho ban. Yɛn nneyɛe bɔne so 
nsunsuanso wɔ yɛn atenae so no mu bi ne nsuyiri, nnɔbae a yentumi 
nnya no dodow ne nea ɛkeka ho.
2. Fa edin nkyerɛkyerɛmu a woahu no yɛ ɔkasamu kuntann ahorow du.

ADESUA NO MU NSƐNTITIRIW
Sɛ wode adeyɛ ne ɔkyerɛfo reyɛ ɔkasamu wɔ Ghana kasa ahorow mu no gyina 
mmara ahorow so. Saa mmara ahorow yi boa ma ɔkasamu no mu da hɔ, na ɛnam 
so ma ɔkenkanfo no nya emu ntease a ɛfata. Sɛ wode kyerɛwbea ho mmara no di 
dwuma wɔ Ghana kasa ahorow no mu a, ɛboa ma yetumi kyerɛw ɔkasamu a emu 
da hɔ fann wɔ ɔkasa a woresua no mu.
Adeyɛ
Ansa na yɛbɛkɔ adeyɛ ho mmara so no, ma yɛnkaekae yɛn ho mfa adeyɛ asekyerɛ 
ho. Hwɛ nhwɛso a ɛwɔ fam hɔ no. Nsɛmfua a wɔayeyɛ no tuntumm no nyinaa yɛ 
adeyɛ.
1. Okuafo no dɔw n’asase no so afe biara.
2. Mmofra no nantew kɔ sukuu Fida biara.
3. Yɛhuruwhuruw anɔpa biara de tenetene yɛn apɔw mu.
Adeyɛ yɛ asɛmfua, nsɛmfua anaa ɔkasasin a ɛkyerɛ dwumadi a ɛrekɔ so anaa 
tebea a biribi wɔ mu. Adeyɛ taa di nkasae anim wɔ ɔkasamu mu. Ne tiaatwa mu 
no adeyɛ taa yɛ nkasae ti wɔ ɔkasamu mu.
Ɔkwan a yɛfa so de adeyɛ di dwuma wɔ ɔkasamu mu
Ɔkwan a yɛfa so de adeyɛ di dwuma wɔ ɔkasamu mu da nso wɔ Ghana kasa 
ahorow mu. Mmara no mu bi na edidi so yi:
1. Adeyɛ kyerɛ dwuma a ɔyɛfo bi redi wɔ ɔkasamu mu. 
 Nhwɛso:
a. Ɔkraman no po wɔ ɔkwan no ano.
 Ɔkasamu yi mu no, adeyɛ po no kyerɛ ade a ɔyɛfo (ɔkraman no) reyɛ wɔ 
kwan no ano.
b. Adesuafo no nantew kɔ sukuu anɔpa biara.
 Ɔkasamu yi mu no, adeyɛ nantew no kyerɛ ɔyɛfo (adesuafo no) no anɔpa 
biara.
2. Adeyɛ kyerɛ su a ɔyɛfo no wom wɔ ɔkasamu no mu. 
 Nhwɛso:
a. Amoako so pa ara.

Ɔkasamu yi mu no, adeyɛ so no kyerɛ su anaa tebea a ɔyɛfo (Amoako) wɔ

Ɔkyerɛfo yɛ asɛmfua anaa ɔkyerɛfo kasasin a ɛkyerɛkyerɛ adeyɛ mu ana ɔkyerɛfo 
foforo a egyina hɔ ma beae, bere, anoɔden ne nea ɛkeka ho. Ɔkyerɛ ho nhwɛso

1. Wɔbaa ha. (beae kyerɛfo)
2. Adu ne Asare baa ha anɔpa nnɔnson. (bere kyerɛfo)
3. Abeawa no yɛɛ ɔpanyin no defedefe. (anoɔaden kyerɛfo)
Ɔkyerɛfo a ɛwowɔ ɔkasamu a ɛwɔ soro hɔ no mu nonom ne ha, anɔpa nnɔnson 
ne defedefe.
Ɔkyerɛfo Dwumadi
Ɔkwan a yɛfa so de ɔkyerɛfo di dwuma wɔ ɔkasamu mu da nso wɔ Ghana kasa 
ahorow no mu.
Mmara no mu bi na edidi so yi:
1. Ɔkyerɛfo tumi di dwuma sɛ ɔkyerɛfo kasa in ti.
 Nhwɛso:
a. Mmarima no kasa dodo pa ara.
b. Agoru kɔɔ awiei ntɛmso.
 Ɔkyerɛfo dodo ne ntɛmso di dwuma sɛ ɔkyerɛfo kasasin, wɔ bere koro 
no ara mu no, edi dwuma sɛ ɔkyerɛfo kasasin no ti.
2. Wɔtumi nso kyerɛkyerɛ ɔkyerɛfo foforo mu.
 Nhwɛso:
a. Abofra kasa ntɛmntɛm pa ara.
b. Ɔkraman no didi dodo sɛ.
 Ɔkasamu ahorow a ɛwɔ soro hɔ no mu no, ɔkyerɛfo pa ara kyerɛkyerɛ 
ɔkyerɛfo ntɛmntɛm mu, saa ara nso na ɔkyerɛfo sɛ nso kyerɛkyerɛ 
ɔkyerɛfo dodow mu.

NNIANIM
Saa ɔfa yi kasa fa susukyerɛw ahorow no ho. Ɛnyɛ Akuapem Twi kasa mu nko na 
susukyerɛw ho nimde hia na mmom, ɛho hia wɔ adesua ahorow bi te sɛ Borɔfo 
kasa ne Abakɔsɛm sua mu nso.
Adesua yi bɛkɔ awiei no, na wutumi:
1. Kyerɛw amannebɔ susukyerɛw
2. Kyerɛw susukyerɛw susukyerɛw
3. Kyerɛw akwankyerɛ susukyerɛw
Adwempɔw Ahorow
• Susukyerɛw yɛ bere a onipa bi fa akyerɛw kwan so da ne tirimpɔw adi fa 
asɛntitiriw bi ho.
• Wubesua biribi afa suskyerɛw ahorow abiɛsa ho:
o Amannebɔ susukyerɛw yɛ ɔkwan a yɛnam akyerɛw so bɔ amanne fa 
asɛm bi a asi ho.
o Sukyerɛ susukyerɛw yɛ susukyerɛw a yɛkyerɛw fa ade bi ho de 
kyerɛkyerɛ sɛnea dekode no su si te pɔtee. Sɛ ebia: ade bi, onipa, 
beae, osuahu, atenka tebea ne nea ɛkeka ho.
o Akwankyerɛ susukyerɛw nso yɛ bere a yɛnam akyerɛw so kyerɛkyerɛ 
ɔkwan a yɛfa so yɛ biribi pɔtee. Ɛkyerɛkyerɛ kwan anaa nimde pɔtee 
a yɛfa so di dwuma bi anaa yɛ biribi.
• Susukyerɛw ahorow no mu biara wɔ nhyehyɛe sononko bi a ɛda emu 
biara adi.

ADESUA MU NSƐNTITIRIW 
Yɛaka saa atifiasɛm yi afa ahorow no bi ho asɛm wɔ adesua a atwam no bi mu. 
Wokae nea yɛka faa Asɛntitiriw Nnyinaso kasamu ho no? Dɛn ne nkyerɛkyerɛmu 
kasamu?
Sɛ wo ne wo mfɛfo kyɛ adwen wie a, kyerɛw w’ankasa wo nkyerɛkyerɛmu.
Afei, fa wo mmuae no toto nkyerɛkyerɛmu a ɛwɔ fam ha no ho.
Asɛntitiriw Nnyinaso Kasamu
Asɛntitiriw Nnyinaso Kasamu yɛ ɔkasamu a ɛde asɛntitiriw a ɛwɔ kasapɛn no mu 
to gua. Ɛnna nkyerɛkyerɛmu kasamu nso yɛ ɔkasamu a ɛkyerɛkyerɛ Asɛntitiriw 
Nnyinaso Kasamu no mu.
Osusukyerɛw
Ansa na wubetumi akyerɛw susukyerɛw no, wohia emu nimde amapa. Ɛsɛ sɛ 
wutumi hyehyɛ adwen ahorow no yie wɔ kasapɛn biara mu. Yebetumi ayɛ eyi wɔ 
bere a yɛrehyehyɛ anaa yɛrekeka adwen ahorow a ɛsesɛ no abobom wɔ nnidiso 
nnidiso kwan so wɔ bere a yɛde adansedide mfonini, ntotoho ne nea ɛkeka ho redi 
dwuma.
Susykyerɛ yɛ bere a onipa fa akyerɛw kwan so da ne tirimpɔw adi fa asɛntitiriw 
bi ho. Susukyerɛw biara de asɛmpɔw bi to gua.
Susukyerɛw ahorow abiɛsa na yɛbɛka ho asɛm. Nea yebedi kan aka ho asɛm no 
ne Amannebɔ Susukyerɛw.
Amannebɔ Sususkyerɛw
Amannebɔ Susukyerɛw yɛ ɔkwan a yɛnam akyerɛw so bɔ amanne fa asɛm bi  ase 
ho. Amannebɔ susukyerɛw mu nsɛm tumi yɛ bɔsrɛmka anaa biribi a asi pɔtee. 
Amannebɔ suskyerɛw mu no, yɛhyehyɛ nsɛm no nnidiso nnidiso kwan so na yɛtaa 
de edinnsiananmu akuw a edi kan (me, yɛn) na edi dwuma wɔ n’akyerɛw mu.
Wɔde twam kabea, adwen mu mfonini ne kasasu ahorow na ɛkyerɛw Amannebɔ 
susukyerɛw mu dodow no ara de twe akenkanfo adwen.
Amannebɔ susukyerɛw atifiasɛm ho nhwɛso:
• Kyerɛw abasɛm fa da a edi kan a wokɔɔ sukuu ho.
• Sɛnea midii akwamma a etwaa mu no.

Sukyerɛ susukyerɛw nhyehyɛe
Sukyerɛ susukyerɛw nhyehyɛe te sɛ amannebɔ susukyerɛw nhyehyɛe no ara.
i. Nnianim: Ɛsɛ sɛ nnianim no da nea ɔkyerɛwfo no rebɛkasa afa ho no 
adi. Nsɛm a ɛtwe akenkanfo adwen kɔ sukyerɛ susukyerɛw no so bi te sɛ 
ampɛmmuae asɛmmisa ho hia wɔ ha pa ara.
ii. Asɛm no Ankasa:  Aha na yɛkyerɛkyerɛ adwempɔw ahorow no mu. Ɛsɛ 
sɛ Asɛntitiriw Nnyinaso Kasamu boa ma adwempɔw no mu da hɔ fann na 
atumi atwe akenkanfo no adwen aba dwumadi no so. Ɛsɛ sɛ yɛde kasapɛn 
foforo di dwuma wɔ bere a yɛreda adwempɔw foforo adi.
iii. Awiei: San kyerɛw susukyerɛw no nnyinaso anaa ne botae a wokaa ho asɛm 
wɔ nnianim hɔ no ne adwempɔw ahorow a ɛda adi wɔ asɛm no ankasa bom 
wɔ ha.
Sukyerɛ susukyerɛw ho nhwɛso ahorow
• Kyerɛkyerɛ sini a wopɛ ne hwɛ pa ara mu.
• Kyerɛkyerɛ sɛnea ahofadi ne atɛn tenenee si te mu.
• Kyerɛkyerɛ sɛnea nhoma bi a w’ani gye ho pa ara si te.
• Kyerɛkyerɛ sɛnea ɔkwan a edi kan a wutu kɔɔ amanɔne si te,
• Kyerɛkyerɛ sɛnea w’adamfo a wopɛ n’asɛm pa ara si te.

Akwankyerɛ Susukyerɛw
Akwankyerɛ Susukyerɛw da nimde foforo adi fa atifiasɛm bi ho kyerɛ ɔkenkanfo no. 
Ɛboa ma ɔkenkanfo no nya ntease a emu dɔw, nkyerɛasekann anaa nkyerɛkyerɛmu

Akwan Ahorow A Yɛfa So kyerɛw Akwankyerɛ Susukyerɛw
Sɛ wubetumi akyerɛw akwankyerɛ susukyerɛw amapa a, ɛho hia sɛ wubenya not 
wobenya ntease a emu dɔw wɔ atifiasɛm a wɔde ama wo no ho.
Akwankyerɛ Susukyerɛw atifiasɛm ho nhwɛso ahorow;
1. Kyerɛkyerɛ ɔkwan a yɛfa so nwene kɛntɛn
2. Kyerɛkyerɛ ɔkwan a wɔfa so yi akannifo wɔ wo sukuu mu
3. Nkwan a w’adamfo bi pɛ pa ara ne abɛkwan nanso onnim yɛ. Kyerɛkyerɛ 
no sɛnea yesi yɛ no.
4. ɔkwan bɛn so na yesi yɛ afuw?
5. W’adamfo bi pɛ sɛ ɔbɛsra wo wɔ wo sukuu mu. Kyerɛ no kwan.
 Worekyerɛw akwankyerɛ susukyerɛw a,ɛho behia sɛ wobedi saa atrapoe 
ahorow yi so;
a. Kenkan asɛmmisa anaa atifiasɛm no yie.
b. San kenkan nimde a woasua afa akwankyerɛ susukyerɛw ho no mu. Sɛ 
wonte biribi ase a, bisa wo kyerɛkyerɛfo na ɔnkyerɛkyerɛ mu yie nkyerɛ 
wo. Wubetumi nso ayɛ nhwehwɛmu afa atifiasɛm no ho wɔ abɛɛfo 
ntontanfidi so anaa nneɛma ahorow mu de apɛ ho nimde.
c. Kyekye dwumadi no mu nketenkete sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a wubenya mu ntease 
yie.
d. Yɛ wo susukyerɛw no ho nhyehyɛe amapa (hwɛ nea ɛwɔ fam hɔ no.) .
e. Kyerɛw ɔkasamu a ɛyɛ akwankyerɛ susukyerɛw no fapem no na hyehyɛ 
wo nnianim no yie fa hyɛ wo dwumadi no ase.

akwankyerɛ susukyerɛw no wie a, kyerɛ emu nea ɛho hia pa ara a ɛbɛboa wo ama

Akwankyerɛ susukyerɛw nhyehyɛe ahorow
Akwankyerɛ susukyerɛw ho nhyehyɛe ahorow na edidi so yi:
i. Nnianim: Di kan kyerɛw w’atifiasɛm no ne ɔkasamu a ɛyɛ akwankyerɛ 
susukyerɛw no fapem no na fa bɔ nea worebɛka ho asɛm no tɔfa.
ii. Asɛm no Ankasa: Eyi taa yɛ kasapɛn abiɛsa nanso etumi boro saa wɔ 
bere a wo susukyerɛw no ware pa ara. Aha na wokyerɛkyerɛ wo nsɛm, 
adwen ahorow anaa atifiasɛm no mu yie. Ɛsɛ sɛ kasapɛn biara kyerɛkyerɛ 
adwempɔw koro pɛ mu. Eyi bɛboa ama wo susukyerɛw no mu ada fann. Ɛho 
hia sɛ twaka bɛda kasapɛn biara ne ɔkasamu a ɛyɛ akwankyerɛ susukyerɛw 
no fapem a ɛwɔ nnianim kasapɛn no ntam.
iii. Awiei: Akwankyerɛ susukyerɛw awiei no bɔ atifiasɛm mpɛnsɛmpɛnsɛmu 
no ho nyinaa bɔ tɔfa. Eyi yɛ ɔkwan a yɛfa so de akwankyerɛ susukyerɛw 
dwumadi no nyinaa ba awiei. Ɛbɔ nkyerɛkyerɛmu ahorow a ɔkasamu a ɛyɛ 
akwankyerɛ susukyerɛw no fapem no de to gua ne kasapɛn ahorow a ɛwɔ 
asɛm no ankasa mu no tɔfa.
Kenkan abasɛm no na montena baanu baanu mpɛnsɛmpɛnsɛm akwankyerɛ 
susukyerɛw su mu.

NNIANIM
Saa ɔfa yi da Ghana mmusuakuw ahorow no abosomdin no adi wɔ bere a worehwɛ 
wɔn abɔse wɔ w’amammerɛ mu. Ɛbɛboa wo ama woahu nea enti ne abosomdin 
ahorow no so mfaso. Saa adesua yi bɛboa ama woate din to ase na ama wode nnidi 
a ɛsɛ fata ama Ghana amammerɛ ne amanne ahorow no. Ɔfa yi san kasa fa ɔkwan a 
yɛfa so pagyaw mmabunu kɔ wɔn mpanyin mfe so (Bragoru). Mpɛnsɛmpɛnsɛmu 
yi bɛhwɛ nneyɛe ahorow a ɛda adi wɔ: ansa na wɔbɛgoru bra, bragoru no ankasa 
ɛnna bragoru no akyi dwumadi ahorow a ɛkɔ so wɔ w’amammerɛ ne afoforo de 
mu wɔ Ghana,Wobɛsan asua mfaso a ɛwɔ bragoru so ma asakyima, n’abusuafo 
ne ne kuromfo nyinaa.Ɛsɛ sɛ wutumi kyerɛ nneɛma a ɛsesɛ ne nea ɛda nso wɔ 
ɔkwan a wɔfa so pagyaw mmabun kɔ wɔn mpanyin mfe so wɔ Ghana mmusuakuw 
amammerɛ ahorow no mu.
Adesua yi bɛkɔ awiei no, na wutumi:
• Na yɛasua abosomdin, wɔn abɔse ne wɔn dwumadi.
• Na wutumi pɛnsɛmpɛnsɛm kwan ahorow a wɔfa so de ɔbabun bi kɔ ne 
mpanyin mfe (bragoru; Ansa na wɔbɛgoru bra, bragoru no ankasa ɛnna 
bragoru no akyi dwumadi ahorow)
• Na wutumi yɛ ntotoho fa akwan ahorow a wɔfa so goru bra wɔ Ghana 
mmusuwkuw ahorow no mu no.
Adwempɔw ahorow
• Abosomdin ahorow no abɔse gyina ɔbosom pɔtee bi so.
• Ayɔnkofa amapa da abosom ne wim atumfo no ntam.
• Wɔda wɔn abakɔsɛm adi kyerɛ wɔn a wɔsom wɔn no.

ABOSOMDIN
Wɔde edin ahorow bi to yɛn so esian twaka a ɛda yɛne wim atumfo bi ntam nti. 
Wɔfrɛ saa edin ahorow yi se abosomdin. Ansa na wobesua biribi afa abosomdin 
ho no, ɛsɛ sɛ wote asɛmfua abosom asekyerɛ ase yiye.
DƐn ne ɔbosom?
Abosom yɛ ahonhom a wɔtumi yɛ mmea anaa mmarimma. Wɔyɛ ewiem atumfo 
a nnipa a wɔwɔ gyidi bi sɛ biribiara a ɛbɛkɔ so wɔ wɔn asetena mu no, ɛyɛ ade a 
abosom no betumi ayɛ ho biribi nti na wɔsom wɔn. Saa abosom yi wɔ honhom mu 
tumi kɛse. Yɛtaa de ɔsom mu gyidi ne emu nnwuma ahorow no gyina hɔ ma wɔn 
abosom. Saa ahonhom yi tumi yɛ mmea anaa mmarimma. Ɔsom mu ahonhom a 
wɔyɛ mmarimma no mu bi ne Zeus, Apollo, Athena, Aphrodite, Artemis, ne nea 
wɔkeka ho. Ghanaman yi mu, mantam anaa abusuakuw biara wɔ abosom a wɔgye 
wɔn di. Abosom a woagye din pa ara wɔ Ghanaman yi mu no na edidi so yi:
i. Ga: Dantu, Nae, Klote, La Kpa, ne wɔn a wɔkeka ho.
ii. Akan: Kune, Tegare, Nyamaa, Antoa, ne wɔn a wɔkeka ho.
iii. Dagomba: Tambo, ne wɔn a wɔkeka ho.
Abosom a wɔagye din pa ara bɛn na wɔwɔ wo kurom?
Abosomdin Ahorow
Wɔgyina gyidi ne ɔsom ahorow so na ɛde abosomdin to nnipa binom. Abosomdin 
yɛ edin pɔtee bi a abusua, kurow, ɔsom anaa nnipakuwbi de to wɔn ho ɛnam 
twaka a ɛda wɔne abosom no ntam nti.
Abosomdin ahorow no ho nhwɛso
Nea edidi so yi yɛ Abosomdin ahorow a ɛwɔ Ghanaman mu:
1. Ewefo mmusuakuw no mu biako a ɛde Anlo a ɛwɔ Firaw Mantam mu no 
som bosom bi a wɔfrɛ no ‘Afa’ a ɛkyerɛ sɛ ofi onyame hɔ na ɔsan yɛ Abakan 
ma anyame ‘Bokɔ’ no din de ‘Amuzu’.

2. Akanfo mu nso, wɔde abosomnini ne abosombere din gyina hɔ ma nna 
ahorow no. Ɛnam yei nti ɛda a yɛde wo obi no tumi nya nsunsuanso wɔ ne

Bobɔ abosomdin ahorow a ɛwɔ soro hɔ no mmiako mmiako. Ma wo kyerɛkyerɛni

Abosomdin ahorow abɔse
Abosomdin ahorow no da nso fi ɔsom ahorow mu a egyina wɔn a wɔto edin no 
gyidi ne wɔn amammerɛ so. Sɛ ebia, Ewefo mu no, wɔn abosomdin abɔse ne 
Yeʋe (Agradaa Nyame), Akanfo nso nya wɔn abosomdin fi asuo ahorow mu ɛnna 
Dangmefo nso nya wɔn abosomdin fi Ɔbɔade Nyame hɔ ne nea ɛkeka ho.
Wunim din no abɔse?
Nea enti a wɔto abosomdin
Wɔgyina nneɛma ahorow so na ɛto abosomdin. Wɔto nnipa abosomdin de kyerɛ 
dwuma a ɔbosom no di anaa ne tumi. Ebi nso gyina mmoa bi a wɔnya fii ɔbosom 
no hɔ so ɛnna ebi nso da nnipakuw bi amammerɛ so ana sɛnea ɔbosom bi si te. 
Bio, awarefo bi nnya awo a wɔkɔ abosom nkyɛn kɔpɛ mmoa. Wɔhyɛ bɔ wɔde 
wɔn ba na ɛto ɔbosom no de di wɔn bɔhyɛ no so.
Abosomdin to ho mfaso
Abosomdinto so wɔ nsunsuanso kɛse wɔ nnipa ahorow a wɔsom wɔn no abrabɔ 
so.
Mfaso ahorow a wɔn a wokura abosomdin no nya wɔ wɔn din no so na edidi so yi:
1. Yɛdehyɛ wɔn nso. Abosomdin boa ma yehu bosom pɔtee a obi som no ne 
beae a onipa no fi.
2. Ɛkyerɛ twaka a ɛda onipa bi ne ɔbosom no ntam.
3.  Abosomdinto boa ma amammerɛ ne ɔsom ase tim ne nea ɛkeka ho.
4. Ɛda awofo no gyidi a wɔwɔ wɔ ɔbosom no mu adi.
5. Abosomdinto boa ma nea okura abosomdin no nya ahoɔden, ahobammɔ ne 
honhom mu tumi.

Nsakrae a ɛda adi wɔ mmeawa nipadua mu
Nsakrae a ɛda adi wɔ mmeawa nipadua mu no bi na edidi so yi:
• Wɔn sisi akyi trɛw
• Wɔn aserɛ yɛ akɛse
• Wɔn to nso yeyɛ akɛse nkorowakorowa
• Wɔbu wɔn nsa a edi kan
• Wɔn nufo yeyɛ akɛse
• Nhwi fu wɔ wɔn bea so ne wɔn mmɔtoam.
Nsakrae a ɛda adi wɔ mmarimaa nipadua mu
Nsakrae a ɛda adi wɔ mmarimaa nipadua mu no bi na edidi so yi:
• Wɔn tadua ne wɔn hwoa yeyɛ akɛse.
• Nhwi fu wɔ wɔn tadua so ne wɔn mmɔtoam.
• Wɔn koko ne wɔn mmati yeyɛ akɛse
• Wɔn honam mu ntini nso mu yɛ den
• Wɔn nnɛ mu yɛ du
• Wɔyɛ tenten
• Wɔfu abɔgyesɛ
Saa nsakrae ahorow yi kyerɛ abrabɔ mu kankɔ bi a yɛfrɛ no Bragoru.

nhenepa ne mpomporanne ahorow siesie wɔn ho fɛfɛɛfɛ.

yiyi wɔn mpokua ne wɔn honam akwaa no so de da no adi ma mmarima

Bragoru no akyi dwumadi
• Bragoru no akyi no, mmeawa a wapagya wɔn kɔ wɔn mpanyin mfe so no ne 
wɔn abusuafo ne wɔn nnamfonom kyinkyin kurow no mu kɔdeda ɔmanfo

Mfonini 6.3. Eyi kyerɛ mmeawa a wɔagoru wɔn bra 
awie a wɔde kente asiesie wɔn ho. (bragoru)
Bragoru Ntotoho: Nsonsonoe a ɛda bragoru dwumadi ahorow 
a ɛwɔ Ghanaman yi mmusuakuw mu.
Sɛ yɛde dwumadi ahorow a ɛsesɛ no to nkyɛn a, yɛwɔ dwumadi ahorow no bi nso 
wɔ hɔ a ɛda nso fi afoforo ho. Saa dwumadi no bi na edidi so yi.
Ewefo
1. Sɛ wɔde nnawɔtwe anaa bosome bɛyɛ bragoru dwumadi bi gyina nnipa anaa 
botae a ɛtaa akyi no so.
2. Wɔde mmeawa a wɔagoru wɔn bra no kɔtena afikyiri ma wɔn nnamfonom 
begoru de gyegye wɔn ani wɔ bere a wɔte afikyiri hɔ no.
3. Bragoro dwumadi no mu no’ kesua a wɔde ma wɔn di no gyina hɔ ma awoɔ.
Krɔbɔfo
1. Krɔbɔfo yɛ Dipo ma wɔn mmeawa wɔ bere a wɔn bosombere Nene Kloweki 
soma ma wɔde ato gua sɛ obiara a ne ba aso sɛ yɛgoru no bra no mfa no 
mmra. Wɔde nnanum na edi saa dwuma yi wɔ Ogyefo bosome no mu.
2. Ansa na bragoru no ankasa bɛkɔ so no, awofo ahorow de wɔn mmammea 
no kɔkyerɛ wɔn abusua akɔmfo a wɔhwɛ yɛ ‘Dipo’ no.
3.  Bragoru ankasa dwumadi mu no, akɔmfo gu nsa, yɛ nyankomade ahorow 
san yi mmeawa no ti ho nhwi na wɔde wɔn atena bɔnhoma so ne nea ɛkeka 
ho.

Nkranfo
1. Nkranfo nso yɛ Otofo de ma wɔn mmammea wɔ bere a wɔanyini.
Akanfo
1. Akanfo nso de nnawɔtwe na edi saa dwuma yi wɔ bere a wɔhyɛ ase Dwowda 
anaa Benada.
2. Ansa na wɔbɛgoru bra no, wɔde mmeawa no kɔ ɔhemmea hɔ ma no yɛ 
honhom ne honam mu nhwehwɛmu fa wɔn ho de hwɛ sɛ wɔyɛ mmaabunu 
anaa wɔnnyenyem nso.
Ɔkwan bɛn so na Akuapemfo si goru wɔn mmammea bra?
Ɔkwan a yɛfa so goru mmarimaa bra
Ɔkwan a yɛfa so goru mmarimaa bra no nyɛ ade a ɛtaa kɔ so wɔ Ghanaman mu 
mmusuakuw ahorow no amammerɛ mu. Mmusuakuw kakra a wɔdi saa dwuma yi 
bi ne Ewefo a wɔfrɛ saa amammerɛ ne amanne no “Tudedeasi”. Sissalafo nso frɛ 
no Baala, Nkranfo nso frɛ no Plamatsemɔ/Butrumwɔɔ/Deŋtuwoo ɛnna Vaglafo 
nso frɛ no Pella. Bra a wɔgoru ma mmarimaa no ntaa nyɛ aguabɔ ase dwumadi. 
Nhwɛso, Ewefo mu no, otu a wɔde ma abarimaa a wɔregoru no bra no wɔfrɛ no 
‘Tudedeasi’. Ɛsɛ sɛ ɔde saa otu yi bɔ n’abusuafo ho ban na ɔsan nso de yɛ ha.
Akwan ahorow a wɔfa so di saa dwuma ahorow yi na edidi so yi;
1. Wɔde abarimaa no kosie baabi
2. Wɔkyerɛkyerɛ no biribi fa mmarimayɛ, asɛde ne mpam agodi ho
3. Wɔpagya mmarimaa no kɔ wɔn mpanyin mu
4. Wɔhyɛ wɔn den wɔ honhom ne honam mu
5. Wɔkyerɛkyerɛ wɔn amammerɛ ne amanne nso
Akwan ahorow a wɔfa so di saa dwuma yi da nso wɔ mmusuakuw ahorow bi de 
ho wɔ Ghanaman mu ha.
Bragoru So Mfaso
1. Wɔde pagyaw mmabunu kɔ mpanyin mu.
2. Wɔnam so nya nimde ahorow de bɔ wɔn bra.
3. Wɔde kyerɛ sɛ ɔbabunu bi aso aware.
4. Wɔde siesie mmabunu wɔ honhom ne honam mu ma aware.
5. Wɔde kyerɛkyerɛ mmeawa ne mmarimaa no subanpa ne abrabɔpa.
6. Wɔde kyerɛkyerɛ mmabunu no wɔn amammerɛ ne wɔn amanne.
7. Wɔnam so de si mmabunu abrabɔ bɔne ne subammɔne ano kwan.

NNIANIM
Saa ɔfa yi da Akanfo amammu nhyehyɛe a ɛwɔ Ghana ha no adi. Ɛpɛnsɛmpɛnsɛm 
Akanfo amammu nhyehyɛe no mu biara dwumadi ne wɔn so mfaso mu. Saa 
ɔfa yi hwɛ sɛ wobenya nimde ne ntease afa Akanfo amammu nhyehyɛe ho wɔ 
Akuapem amammere mu. Wobenya dwuma ahorow a Akanfo ahemfo no di ne 
wɔn dwumadi no so mfaso wɔ ɔman no mpuntu ne ɔmanfo no yiedi ho wɔ wo 
mpɔtam.
Adesua no bɛkɔ awiei no, na adesuafo no tumi:
i. Kyerɛkyerɛ Akanfo Amammu Nhyehyɛe no mu (Agya, abusuapanyin, 
odikuro)
ii Kyerɛkyerɛ Akanfo amammu nhyehyɛe no mu (ɔhene, ahemfo nketewa, 
asihenefo ne nea ɛkeka ho.)
Adwempɔw Ahorow
• Agya no ne abusua a wodi agyade no ti. (Aha yi no, wɔto anaa kɔ agya 
abusua mu).
• Abusua a wodi ɛnade fa mu no, ɔbea (ɛna) betumi ayɛ abusua no ti.
• Abusua tenten no ti ne adikurofo a wɔhwɛ yɛn mpɔtam-mpɔtam na abusua 
mpanyimfo ahorow na wɔka bom paw wɔn.

ƆFA 7 AMAMMERE NE AMAMMU
AKANFO AMAMMU
Sua Akanfo amammu nhyehyɛe no (Agya, abusuapanyin, odikuro).
Akanfo Amammu
Akanfo Amammu yɛ amammu nhyehyɛe a egyina ɔmanfo no suahunu ne wɔn 
amammere so. Akanfo amammu ahorow a ɛwɔ Ghana mpɔtam ahorow no mu yɛ 
nnidiso nnidiso. Saa nhyehyɛe yi da nso wɔ mmusuakuw ahorow no mu nanso 
nkurow no mu dodow no ara nhyehyɛe yɛ adekoro.
Akanfo amammu nhyehyɛe wɔ mmusuakuw mu
Ɔman Ghana ha yi no, asɛmfua ‘abusua’ asekyerɛ tumi yɛ abusua ketewa a emu 
nnipa no ne agya, ɛna ne mma anaasɛ abusua tenten a emu nnipa no ne abusua 
ketewa no mu nnipa nkae bi te sɛ nananom, wɔfanom, sewaanom, anuanom 
ne wɔn a wɔkeka ho. Eyi kyerɛ sɛ, Akanfo amammu nhyehyɛe wɔ abusua mu 
no, yenya agya, abusuapanyin, odikuro, ahemfo, ahemfo nketewa, asihene ne 
ɔmanhene ne wɔn a wɔkeka ho.
Dwumadi
Sɛn na Akanfo amammere nhyehyɛe no si te wɔ wo fi? Hena ne abusua ketewa 
no ti? Hena ne abusua tenten no ti? Woka abusua bi ho?
Adwumayɛmu Nhyehyɛe Pon Ɛyɛ mfoni a ɛda adwumakuw bi mu dwumadi 
ahorow no nhyehyɛe adi. Ɛkyerɛ nnidiso nnidiso nkitahodi kwan a ɛda adwuma 
no mu mpanyimfo ne adwumayɛfo no ntam.
Akanfo amammu nhyehyɛe a ɛwɔ fie mfoni na ɛwɔ ase ha yi;
Mfonini 7.1: Akanfo Amammu nhyehyɛe a ɛwɔ fie ho mfoni

ƆFA 7 AMAMMERE NE AMAMMU
1. Odikuro: Abusua tenten yɛ abusua a nnipa ahorow a wɔwɔ mu no hu 
wɔn ho sɛ wɔwɔ ayɔnkofa wɔ aware anaa mogya mu no tena bom. Eyi yɛ 
mmusuakuw ahorow a wɔn nyinaa kura abusuadin biako, nana biako na 
wɔn nyinaa ka bom som ɔkannifo biako. Wɔkura esu, anisoadehu ne apɛde 
koro. Onipa a saa nnipakuw yi kabom yi no sɛ wɔn kannifo no na wɔfrɛ no 
Odikuro. Susudua a wogyina so yi obi sɛ odikuro no da nso firi nkurow 
ahorow no mu. Mmusuakuw no bi mu no, mmusuakuw no mu mpanyimfo 
na wɔka bom yi odikuro afei binom nso wɔ hɔ a, saa adedi yi bɛyɛ awo 
ntoatoa so.
2. Abusuapanyin: Abusuapanyin yɛ onipa a abusua mu no ayi no sɛ wɔn 
kannifo. Wɔn dwumadi titiriw ne sɛ wɔbɛhwɛ abusua no so na waboa ayi 
abusua no mu ɔhaw ahorow afiri hɔ. Ɛsɛ sɛ wɔda akanni su ahorow adi. 
Mpɛn pii no, ɔbarima na wɔtaa yi no sɛ abusuapanyin.
3. Agya: Agya no ne abusua ketewa a n’ankasa ka ho bi, ne yere ne ne mma 
no ti. Agya no na ɔyɛ abusua no apɛde ma wɔn.
Dwumadi
 Sɛ yɛhwɛ Akanfo amammu nhyehyɛe mfoni no fi soro a, eyi nom mu hena 
na ne tumi so pa ara: odikuro, Abusuapanyin anaa Agya?
Kyerɛkyerɛ Akanfo amammu nhyehyɛe nnidiso no mu tiawa.
Akanfo amammu nhyehyɛe dwumadi no ho 
mfaso

d. ɔbɔ abusua no nsaase ho ban.
e. Ɔno na ɔhwɛ abusua no adedi so wɔ awo ntoatoaso nyinaa mu.
2. Abusuapanyin
 Abusuapanyin dwumadi ahorow:
a. Ɔbɔ abusua no ho ban

Akanfo Amammu Nhyehyɛe
Akanfo amammu nhyehyɛe na edidi so yi;
1. Ɔmanhene
2. Ahemfo nketewa/Feku Tiri
3. Ahemmea
4. Asiahene
Afoforo a wɔka Akanfo amammu akannifo a wɔka wɔn a wɔwɔ soro hɔ no ho bi 
ne Akwansrahene, apofofohene, odikuro, abusuapanyin ne nea ɛkeka ho.
1. Ɔmanhene: Amanhene yɛ akannifo ma nnipakuw ana mmusuakuw bi. Wɔn 
na wɔn tumi so pa ara wɔ Akannifo amammu nhyehyɛe no mu. Nkuro binom 
so no, saa diberɛ yi gyina adedi a efiri ɛna ana agya fam so. Ɔmanhene biara 
wɔ n’abodin Nhwɛso, Ewefo de ne Fiagã, Akanfo de ne Osagyefo ɛnna 
Dagombafo de ne Yaa-Naa ne nea ɛkeka ho.
 Ɔmanhene dwumadi ahorow:
a. Ɔhwɛ nkurow nketewa ne akɛse so.
b. ɔhwɛ aguabɔ ahorow so
c. ɔhwɛ ɔman no nsaase nyinaa so.
d. ɔhwɛ siesie ntawantawa a ɛwɔ ɔman no mu
e. ɔhyɛ mmara ma ne manfo hwɛ ma wodi so.
f. Ɔhwɛ ma kankɔ ne mpuntu kɔ so wɔ ne mpɔtam.
g. Ɔhwɛ ma asomdwoe ba ne man mma no ntam.
h. Ɔhwɛ ma nkabom ba ɔman no mu ɛnna afei nso osi ne manfo no ananmu 
wɔ amanhene aguabɔ ase.
2. Ahemfo nketewa/Feku Tiri: Ahemfo nketewa yɛ ahemfo a wɔhyɛ 
ɔmanhene ase pɛɛ. Wodi wɔn hene anaa tumi wɔ nkurow nketewa anaa 
nkurow mmiako mmiako so. Wɔnam awo ntoatoaso so na edi saa dibere yi.
7
ƆFA 7 AMAMMERE NE AMAMMU
 Ahemfo nketewa dwumadi ahorow:
a. Wɔyɛ ɔmanhehe ananmusifo.
b. Wɔhwɛ ma ɔmanfo nya ahobammɔ san di mmara so.
c. Wɔhwɛ siesie ntawantawa a ɛwɔ wɔn mpɔtam.
d. Ɔhwɛ ma asomdwoe ba ɔman no mu.
e. Ɔhwɛ nkonnwafi so.
3. Ahemea: Wohu ahemea sɛ wɔyɛ honhom mu akannifo ma mmea a wɔwɔ 
wɔn mpɔtam ɛnna wɔsan nso kora ɔman abakɔsɛm. Wɔn dwumadi titiriw 
pa ara ne sɛ wɔhwɛ mmea a wɔwɔ wɔn kurom no so. Mmusuakuw a wɔdi 
ɛnade no, ɛyɛ Ahemmea no na wɔyi obi ma odi hene. Wotumi yi obi ma ɔno 
nso bɛyɛ ɔhemmea hyɛ wɔn ase.
 Ahemmea dwumadi ahorow:
a. Wɔyɛ nnwuma ahorow de boa ahemfo no wɔ Akanfo amammu nhyehyɛe 
no mu.
b. Wɔhwɛ siesie ntawantawa a ɛda mmea ntam.
c. Wɔbɔ mmea yiedi ho ban.
d. Wɔbɔ ne kurow no abakɔsɛm ho ban.
4. Asiahene: Asiahene yɛ nnipa anaa nnipakuw bi a wɔhwɛ yi obi wɔ 
adehyebusua mu ma no di ɔhene wɔ bere a wɔn mu biara ntumi nni ɔhene. 
Saa nnipakuw yi hyia fa adwene wɔ onipa a adedi adu ne so no ho.
 Asiahene dwumadi ahorow:
a. Wɔn na woyi onipa a adu ne so
b. Ɔno na ɔhwɛ yɛ amanne wɔ bere a ɔhene bi kɔ akuraa
c. Wɔn na wɔhwɛ ma wɔtu ɔhene bi ade so
d. Wɔn na wɔda ɔhene foforo adi kyerɛ atenankonnwa ne ɔmanfo.
e. Wɔyɛ afotufo ma ɔhene.

MMƆAKYIRI NSƐMMISA
1. Hena na ɔyɛ w’abusua ketewa no ti?
2. Kyerɛkyerɛ dwumadi abien (2) a wohwehwɛ sɛ w’agya anaa wo papa 
bɛyɛ a yɛanka ho asɛm wɔ nhoma yi mu.
3. Kenkan abasɛm a ɛwɔ fam hɔ no na gyina so yɛ dwumadi nhyehyɛe 
mfonini pon ma Akanfo amammu nhyehyɛe ma saa mpɔtam no 
(Ɔmanhene /ɔhene, ahemfo nketewa, asiahene). Fa nhwɛso a wuhu 
wɔ akenkan no mu fa Akanfo amammu nhyehyɛe a ɛwɔ afi mu no di 
dwuma.
Abasɛm ‘A’
Ghana Akanfo amammu nhyehyɛe
Ansa na ka-bi-ma-menka-bi amammu rebɛba no, na Akanfo amammu wɔ 
Ghanaman mu ha dedaw. Saa amammu nhyehyɛe yi gyina nnidiso nnidiso 
kwan a wɔahyehyɛ ahemfo ne mpanyin so. Mpɔtam anaa nkuraase mu no, 
ɔhene ne ne mpanyimfo bi te sɛ asiahene, na wodi kurow no so yɛ nhyehyɛe 
ma kurow no. Na wogyina wɔn nimde, mfe ne wɔn osuahunu so na wɔde yiyi 
saa mpanyimfo no. Yɛyi nkuraase si nkyɛn a, amanhene na wodi nkurow akɛse 
a nkuraase nkurase bebibree hyehyɛ ase. Wɔn na wɔhwɛ siesie ntawantawa 
ma asomdwoe ba ɔman no mu. Ahemfo a wɔyɛ atenankonnwa no na wɔtu 
Ɔmanhene fo ma ɔyɛ nhyehyɛe a ɛbɛma ɔman no atu mpɔn. Ɔmanhene no na 
wodi Akanfo amammu nnidiso nnidiso hyenhyɛe no kan. Ɔmanhene no na 
ɔman no mu tumi nyinaa hyɛ ne nsa. Na Akanfo amammu nhyehyɛe no gye 
dodow- amammu, nnidi a yɛde ma mpanyimfo tom.
4. Pɛnsɛmpɛnsɛm Akanfo amammu nhyehyɛe ahorow no dwumadi ne so 
mfaso abiɛsa (3) ma ɔman no mu.

AKUAPEM TWI KASADWINI
Ano Kasadwini ne Akyerɛw Kasadwini
NNIANIM
Saa ɔfa yi kasa fa Akuapem Twi Ano ne Akyerɛw kasadwini ho. Wobesua biribi 
afa nsagu/apae. ho wɔ Ano Kasadwini mu. Wobɛsan asua biribi afa so mfaso ne 
sɛnea wosi yɛ no no ho. Yɛbɛboa wo ama woakyerɛkyerɛ w’adwene afa nea enti 
a nsagu/apaeyi ho hia ma wo nkurɔfo. Saa ɔfa yi ho behia ama wo, sɛ woresua 
Akuapem Twi a ɛne adesua bi te sɛ Ɔsom ahorow ho adesua wɔ twaka yi. Ɔfa yi 
bɛma woanya nimde a ɛho hia a ɛbɛma w’ani agye w’wámammere ne afoforo de 
ho. Saa ɔfa yi bɛboa ama woahu biribi afa Nsui ho. Yɛbɛma woakenkan nneɛma 
afa Nsui ho. Yɛbɛyɛ mpɛnsɛmpɛnsɛmu afa Nsui so mfaso ho. Bio, saa ɔfa yi 
bɛma woanya nimde afa Abasɛm su ahorow no ho ,sɛ ebia agoromma, nsɛntitiriw, 
nhyehyɛe, ɔkasafo ɛnne ne nea ɛkeka ho.
Saa ɔfa yi bɛkɔ awiei no na wutumi:
• Kyerɛ Nsagu/Apaeyi nhyehyɛe wɔ Akuapem Twi mu (ɔfrɛ, amannebɔ, ne 
nhyira)
• Pɛnsɛmpɛnsɛm nsui mu. (dwumadi ne so mfaso).
• Pɛnsɛmpɛnsɛm Abasɛm su ahorow no mu (nhwɛso, agoromma, asɛntitiriw, 
nhyehyɛe, sibiabere, ɔkasafo ɛnne ne nea ɛkeka ho).
• Kenkan abasɛm bi na kyerɛ w’adwen fa ho. (Nhoma no din, asɛntitiriw, 
nsɛmfua dwumadi, kasasu ahorow, ne nea ɛkeka ho.)
Adwempɔw ahorow
• Nsagu/Apaeyi yɛ nananom kwan a wɔfa so bɔ mpae.
• Nsagu/Apaeyi kura nhyehyɛe ahorow wɔ ne dwumadi mu.Ɔfrɛ, amannebɔ, 
ne nhyira ne nnome.
• Asɛntitiriw no ne abasɛm no nnyinaso.

ƆFA 8 KASADWINI

ahorow a ɛwɔ abasɛm  no.

• Ɔkasafo nne yɛ ɛnne pɔtee a yɛte no wɔ abasɛm bi kyerɛw mu.
• Nsui da ɔbra kanko no mu biako dwumadi adi, ɛnna yehu sɛ obi ahwere 
ne ho nipa bi, yɛde srɛ ade, yɛde da atenka sononko bi adi, ne nea ɛkeka 
ho.
NSAGU/MPAEYI
Yɛbɛyɛ mpɛnsɛmpɛnsɛmu afa nsagu/mpaeyi mu nkyekyɛmu afa abiɛsa a ɛyɛ ne 
nhyehyɛe no ho. Nsagu/Apaeyi nhyehyɛe nonom ne ɔfrɛ, amannebɔ ɛnna nhyira 
ne nnome.
Dɛn ne Nsagu/Apaeyi?
Nsagu/mpaeyi ne sɛ worehwie nsa (nsaden) anaa ahwiede bi ama nananom 
nsamanfo anaa ahonhom. Ɛyɛ ɔkwan a yɛfa so de yɛn abisade to nananom anim wɔ 
Abosonsom mu. Ayim-Aboagye (1993: 165, 1996:9) ka se, ɛyɛ adeyɛ bi a wɔde 
nsu anaa nsaden gu fam de frɛ nananom de bisa wɔn nkyɛn mmoa. Mmeae bi wɔ 
hɔ a, wɔde nneɛma bi te sɛ ɔmo tumi gu nsa/yi apae. Nsagu/Apaeyi di akoten pa 
ara yie wɔ Abibiman mu. Wɔnam nsagu/apaeyi so frɛ nananom nsamanfo a wɔdi 
akoten wɔ yɛn asetena mu ma wɔba yɛn aguabɔ biara ase. Ɛyɛ Abusuapanyin, 
Ahemfo anaasɛ mpanyimfo binom na wɔgu nsa anaasɛ wɔyi mpae wɔ aguabɔ 
ahorow bi te sɛ abadinto, awaregye, afahyɛ, ahensi ne nea ɛkeka ho ase Akanman 
mu wɔ Ghanaman mu ha.

Nsagu/Apaeyi Nhyehyɛe
Nsagu/Mpaeyi nhyehyɛe nonom ne ɔfrɛ, amannebɔ ɛnna Nhyira ne Nnome.
Ɔfrɛ
Ɔfrɛ yɛ bere a nsagufo/mpaeyifo no bobɔ nananom nsamanfo ne ahonhom nkae 
no din mmiako mmiako de to nsa frɛ wɔn. Nsagufo no di kan bɔ Tweaduapɔn din 
na afei ɔde Asase Yaa, abosom nketewa na afei wafrɛ nananom nsamanfo. Ɔfrɛ 
a ɛwɔ nsagu/mpaeyi mu no yɛ ɔkwan a wɔfa so bɔ Twaeduapɔn anaa ahonhom 
nkae no pon mu de bɔ wɔn amanne fa dwumadi a ɛrekɔ so no ho. Nhwɛso, Ɔfrɛ 
ho nhwɛso a ɛwɔ Akuapem Twi mu:
Tweaduapɔn Kwame yɛkyerɛ wo nsa na yɛma wo nsa!
Asase Yaa, wo nsa ni!
Asubosom ne nnuabosom mo nsa nie.
Nananom nsamanfo , mommegye nsa nom..
Ahum ne aham mo nso mo nsa ni! .
Amannebɔ
Amannebɔ a ɛwɔ nsagu/mpaeyi mu no da botae pɔtee nti a wɔregu nsa anaa wɔreyi 
mpae no .Eyi betumi ayɛ adesrɛ anaa aseda. Aha yi no, nsagufo no de botae pɔtee 
nti a wɔrefrɛ ahonhom no wɔ dwumadi no mu no to gua. Aha na nsagufo no srɛ 
ahobammɔ fi wɔn hɔ.
Awiei
Nsagu anaa mpaeyi fa eyi mu na nsagufo no da nananom nsamanfo ase anaa ɔhyɛ 
wɔn bɔ sɛ, sɛ wɔyɛ biribi ma wɔn a wɔde biribi bɛda wɔn ase. Nsagufo no srɛ 
nnome fi nananom abosomfo nkyɛn de ma wɔn atamfo Nsagufo no san srɛ nhyira 
fi nananom abosomfo hɔ de ma wɔn adɔfo ne wɔn a wɔreyɛ biribi pa de boa ɔman 
no. Eduru bere bi nso a wɔyi mmusu de dwira ɔman no ho wɔ nhyira ne nnome 
mu. Mfoni a ɛwɔ fam ha no yɛ nsagu/apaeyi ho nhwɛso.

NSUI
Nnwennweneho asɛmmisa: Sɛ wohwere w’abusuani bi a, atenka bɛn na wonya?
Dɛn ne Nsui?
 Nsui yɛ nneyɛe a obi da no adi anaa awerɛhodwom a obi to wɔ bere a ne ho nipa 
bi awu anaa wakae ne ho nipa bi a wawu dedaw. Yehu nsui sɛ ɛyɛ anwensɛm fa 
bi. Eyi kyerɛ sɛ, nsui yɛ anwensɛm a yɛde moma owufo bi. Nsui yɛ ade a yɛyɛ de 
gya owufo bi kwan wɔ bere a ɔrefi ateasefo asase so akɔ ɔman foforo so.
Nsui dwumadi
Abibiman mu ha no, yɛde nsui di dwuma ahorow pii. Nsui dwumadi no mu bi na 
edidi so yi;
1. Wɔde gyam owufo no.
2. Wɔde gya owufo no kwan.
3. Wɔde to nkra .
4. Yɛde srɛ ade ma owufo no
5. Ɛda ayɔnkofa a ɛwɔ yɛn ne owufo no ntam.
Nsui so mfaso
Nsui so mfaso na edidi so wɔ fam hɔ no;
1. Yɛde hyɛ owufo no anuonyam.
2. Ɛka ateasefo ne awufo bom.
3. Ɛma yehu sɛ obi ahwere ne ho nipa bi.
4. Yɛde to ana.
5. Yɛde bue kwan ma owufo no kɔ nseɛdo.

ƆFA 8 KASADWINI
ABASƐM SU AHOROW
Abasɛm/Ayɛsɛm
Abasɛm/Ayɛsɛm yɛ akyerɛw kasadwini no mu biako. Ɛyɛ kyerɛwsɛm a edi kasa 
mmara nhyehyɛe so. Abasɛm di ɔkasa mmara ne ne nhyehyɛe so. Ne nhyehyɛe no 
nte sɛ dwom. Wɔnam so de nimde, dwene ne atosɛm ma wɔn akenkanfo.
DWUMADI 8.11
Kyerɛkyerɛ senea wosi te abasɛm ase na fa toto adesuafo nkae no de ho.
Abasɛm su ahorow
1. Agoromma: Wɔyɛ nipa, mmoa anaa biribiara a wɔde wɔn di dwuma wɔ 
kasawini dwumadi mu. Abasɛm no gyina twaka a ɛda agoromma ahorow 
no ntam. Agoromma ho hi yie wɔ abasɛm papa biara mu na mmom, otiban 
no wɔ nsunsuanso amapa wɔ abasɛm no nhyehyɛe so. Otiban no ne agoroba 
titiriw a ɔwɔ abasɛm no mu ɛnna ɔkotiafo no nso ne agoroba bi a ɔko tia 
otiban na ɔsan nso de ɔhaw pii ba abasɛm no nhyehyɛe no mu. Agoroba 
-a-ɔnsesa-ne-su: Eyi yɛ agoruba ketewa a ɔnsesa ne su wɔ abasɛm mu ɛnna 
Agoroba-a-ɔsesa-ne-su nso yɛ agoroba ketewa a otumi sesa ne su tebea 
ahorow mu wɔ abasɛm mu.
2. Asɛntitiriw: Eyi yɛ asɛm pɔtee a abasɛm bi de to gua anaa kasa fa ho sɛ ebia 
boasetɔ, setie, ɔdɔ koroyɛ, nkabom, adwumaden, anigye ne nea ɛkeka ho. 
Abasɛm tumi nya asɛntitiriw nkorabata a ɛboa ma asɛntitiriw no ankasa wie 
mudi.
3. Sibeabere: Eyi boa ma yehu ade a abasɛm no kasa fa ho. Ɛka biribi fa bere 
ne beae a abasɛm bi mu dwumadi ahorow kɔ so sɛ ebia (asetena mu nsɛm, 
abakɔsɛm, amammere ne amanne anaa atenae bi). Sibeabere taa kasa fa 
bere, beae, wim nsakrae, asetena mu nsɛm ne nea ɛkeka ho a abasɛm no bi 
kɔ so mu.
4.  Nhyehyɛe: Eyi yɛ nnidiso nnidso kwan a wɔfa so hyehyɛ abasɛm bi mu 
dwumadi ahorow. Ɛda adwempɔw ne nneyɛe a ɛwɔ abasɛm no mu adi. 
Ɛkasa fa akansi, apereapere ne ɔhaw ahorow ho. Etumi yɛ biribi a ekowie 
yie, ɛkɔ so tɔɔtenn anaasɛ ɛnkɔwie yie sɛnea anka na wɔhwehwɛ no no.
5. Ɔkasafo nne: Eyi yɛ beae a ɔkenkanfo no gyina hu nea abasɛm no nyinaa 
kasa fa ho. Ɛsan da ɔkasafo nne a ogyina so de kyerɛw abasɛm no adi.

ƆFA 8 KASADWINI
Ebetumi ayɛ ɔkasafo a odi kan (ɔkasafo no ka abasɛm no ho.) anaa ɔkasafo 
nne a ɛto so abien.Wɔkyerɛw abasɛm no fa agoromma bi ho a ɔkasafo no 
nka ho bi.) Dinnsiananmu a wɔde di dwuma wɔ ɔkasafo nne a edi kan mu 
no ne “me” yɛn”afei ɔkasafo nne a ɛto so abien nso dinnsiananmu ne ‘ɔno’ 
‘ne’ ne ‘wɔn’.
6. Tebea: Eyi yɛ atenka a ɔkyerɛwfo bi nam ne dwumadi so de n’akenkanfo 
kɔ mu. Wɔnam mfoniyɛ, asetena mu nsɛm, nneɛma ahorow ,adwempɔw, 
dwumadi ahorow ne nea ɛkeka ho so na ɛde tebea no to gua wɔ abasɛm no 
nhyehyɛe mu. Ebetumi ayɛ awerɛhosɛm, nkunimdi, anigye, anidaso anaa 
owu.
Dwumadi 8.12
Wo ne wo yɔnko mpɛnsɛmpɛnsɛm su anan (4) mu tiawa. Fa wo mmuae no to 
adesuafo nkae no anim.
Dwumadi 8.13
Ma wo kyerɛkyerɛfo mma wo abasɛm nhoma bi na wo ne wo yɔnko nkenkan 
na mo mpɛnsɛmpɛnsɛm ne su ahorow no mu. Fa nhoma no mu nsɛm no bi foa 
wo mmue no so. Wo ne wo yɔnko nkyɛ adwene wɔ wo mmuae no ho.

INTRODUCTION
This section discusses identification of key ideas in texts and discourse. It 
always gives information on specific ideas or knowledge to the reader or hearer. 
The information given may come from all perspectives such as education, 
industrialisation, mining among others. It may also indicate some cultural values 
such as respect, tolerance and patience. Identifying key ideas gives you a better 
understanding of the discourse. It also enhances your critical thinking skills and 
interpretation abilities. There are types of reading techniques namely skimming 
and scanning and the application of any of the type enables you to get the right 
information demanded at any time. Knowledge of the types is therefore essential 
in our everyday life. The concept of oral interpretation will also be discussed. We 
shall discuss the skills needed for effective interpretation. Interpretation plays 
important roles in facilitating communication across language barriers.
By the end of this you will be able to
• Identify key ideas from appropriate discourse. E.g., cultural values 
(respect, kindness, tolerance and others), education, child trafficking, 
environment, industrialisation in Ghana, mining, GESI etc.,
• Discuss ideas and relevant opinions from selected discourse. E.g., 
cultural values (respect, kindness, tolerance and others), education, 
child trafficking, environment, industrialisation in Ghana, mining, GESI, 
STEM, etc.

Key Ideas
 Key ideas are the main messages that is relevant in any discourse. Some 
of the key ideas may center on cultural values such as respect, kindness, 
tolerance, patience, etc. In any discourse you can share relevant opinions 
on any discourse appropriately and interpret any discourse in your own 
understanding.
KEY IDEA
Dear learner, before leaving home for your present school, what are the main 
points from the conversation you had with your parent/guardian? Share with 
peers.
The main points you shared with your peers are known to as key ideas. Key ideas 
are the essential ideas that the author or speaker wants to give to the reader or hearer/
listener respectively. The ideas may include the claims, the reasons, conclusions, 
definitions, classifications, comparisons, evaluations, recommendations, etc. Key 
ideas can be expressed explicitly or implicitly.
For you to identify the key ideas in discourse there is the need for you to 
understand the main concepts, arguments, and the points made. Note that the 
discourse could deal with any topic such as mining, teenage pregnancy, natural 
disaster, educational issues among others. It must also be pointed out that it could 
also come in a text form, video or picture or all the forms mentioned.
In summary, my dear learner to identify the key ideas in a discourse which may 
be written or oral or visual, you may need to answer the following questions
• Find who or what the passage discusses: Does this passage discuss a 
person, group of people or an entity?
• Ask when the event took place: Does the information contain a reference to 
time?
• Find where the event took place: Does the text name a place?
• Ask why the event took place: Do you find a reason or explanation for 
something that happened?
• Ask how the event took place: Does this information indicate a method or 
a theory?

individuals or groups either in spoken form or written form. It involves the 
exchange of ideas, opinions and information. Note that the definition of discourse 
could be defined also from different angles such as linguistics, social science and 
philosophy. The general meaning is appropriate for us. Go online to read the other 
definitions to broaden your knowledge.

Reading
By the end of the sub-strand you should be able to:
i. Discuss skimming using preview, overview and review.
ii. Discuss scanning using the strategies (e.g., movement of eyes or finger, 
locating words and phrases)
iii. Apply skimming and scanning to extract information or ideas from texts
Key ideas
 Skimming is going through a text rapidly to get the general information 
in the text while scanning involves looking for a specific information in 
a text. Scanning is a process of reading in which your eyes quickly run 
through a piece of text to find a piece of relevant information. Scanning 
and skimming are two different concepts of reading.
Types of reading
There are types of reading skill or technique namely skimming, scanning, 
intensive reading and extensive reading. Dear learner, in this lesson you shall 
learn skimming and scanning techniques of reading.
Skimming
Skimming is a reading technique used to quickly identify the main ideas or key 
points in a text. It is the action of reading something quickly so as to note only the 
important points. Basically, skimming is reading rapidly in order to get a general 
overview of the material read. It is used to find specific facts in texts. It involves 
glancing over the material, focusing on headings, subheadings, bold text and key 
phrases to get a general understanding of the content. Skimming is useful when; 
time is limited, looking for specific information, you want to get an overview 
before reading in-depth and you are dealing with a large amount of text. Below 
are the skimming types.
8

1. Preview: An opportunity to view something before it is acquired or becomes 
generally available. Preview is done in an effort to learn about the ideas 
presented and the structure of their development.
2. Overview: Used to sample the reading material more thoroughly. A general 
review or summary of a subject.
3. Review: The review is done to re-familiarise yourself with the material 
you have previously read thoroughly or skimmed. A formal assessment of 
something with the intention of instituting a change if necessary.
Learner, in skimming, you can follow these steps
i. Read the title
ii. Read the headings and sub-headings as well as topic sentences in each 
paragraph
iii. Look for important information such as date, names and unusual words.
iv. Read the conclusion

In summary you have learnt skimming and the steps as well as the types of 
skimming which you can apply. Dear learner, let us examine what is scanning.
Scanning
Scanning is reading rapidly in order to find facts without reading everything. 
Scanning helps you locate a particular fact while skimming tells you what general 
information is within a section.
 Scanning involves looking for a specific information in a text. It can also be said 
to be a process of reading in which your eyes quickly run through a piece of text 
to find a piece of relevant information. In scanning the reader looks for a piece 
of specific information. An example of scanning is searching for the meaning 
of a word in a dictionary. Scanning helps the reader to locate particular facts in 
an entire text quickly. Students often use scanning when solving their reading 
comprehension questions.
It is important to know the purpose for scanning. You should know what you are 
searching for, eg title of a book, a website, a reference material, a particular word 
or phrase and a particular story you want to read etc. You should know how the 
material is structures either alphabetically, non-alphabetically, chronologically, 
by category, by titles /headings, by textual sense, by numbers among others.
Scanning helps a learner to read more and to develop love for reading.

When to scan
1. Scan before reading
2. Scan a number of questions to identify the one which you are most 
comfortable answering
3. When searching for particular information such as date, keywords etc.
The following shows how to do scanning after getting overview of a text and 
identifying the sections of the text you want to read.
1. Start scanning the text by moving your eyes and fingers quickly over it
2. When you have identified the information, word or the phrase you are 
searching for, read the information surrounding the word carefully
3. When you identified the information that requires attention, you read it 
thoroughly slowly.

LANGUAGE USAGE
Oral Interpretation and translation
By the end of the sub-strand the learner should be able to:
Discuss oral interpretation focusing on effective listening, encoding and 
decoding,
Key Ideas
 Oral interpretation is reframing the meaning of a speech most often orally 
into another language. The original language is the source language 
and the language in which it is rendered is the target language. In oral 
interpretation you must note the cultural differences and be accurate in 
giving the meaning of what you are to render in the language orally.
INTERPRETATION
Interpretation is listening to a message in one language and rendering it orally 
in another language maintaining the original meaning, tone and context. It 
is the stylistic representation of a creative work or dramatic role. It is the act 
of explaining, reframing, or otherwise showing your own understanding of 
something. In interpretation you first have to understand the text or the piece 
given to you and then explain in your own words. In broader terms it is rendering 
a spoken or signed message into another spoken or signed language preserving 
the register and meaning of the source language content.
Dear learner, it must be noted that before you can do any interpretation, you must 
be well versed in the source and target language. Interpretation can be performed 
either simultaneously or consecutively between users of different languages.
Dear learner, know that in interpreting you do not embellish or over-exaggerate. 
State the ideas clearly. In interpreting you need to listen carefully, decode and 
encode as they serve as the process of communication and interpreting.

Ɛdeɛn ne adeyɛ?
Ɛdeɛn na woyɛɛ no anɔpa yi? Twerɛtwerɛ deɛ woyɛeɛ no nyinaa.
Ɛdeɛn na wosusu fa nneɛma ahodoɔ a wosua wɔ wo sukuu mu no ho? Twerɛtwerɛ

Hyɛ no nso sɛ, wo ne wáfɛfoɔ bɛkyɛ wo nsusuiɛ ahodoɔ no.
Adeyɛ yɛ asɛmfua anaa nsɛmfua a ɛkyerɛ deɛ ɔyɛfoɔ bi reyɛ. Adeyɛ san tumi 
yɛ asɛmfua anaa nsɛmfua a ɛkyerɛ tebea a ɔyɛfoɔ bi wom (sɛ ebia; tu, so, ware, 
nyini, hua, di, dɔ, si, som, hwɛ, hunu, pɛ, ne deɛ ɛkeka ho).
Adeyɛ tumi ba ɔkasamu mu a ɛwɔ ɔyɛtia anaa ɛnni ɔyɛtia mu. Yɛtumi kyekyɛ 
adeyɛ mu nya fa-ɔyɛtia, amfa-ɔyɛtia ne fa-ɔyɛtia mmienu.
Fa-ɔyɛtia
Fa-ɔyɛtia yɛ adeyɛ a ɛfa edin a ɛdi dwuma sɛ ɔyɛtia di nákyi wɔ ɔkasamu mu. Yei 
ho nhwɛsoɔ no mu bi ne noa, nom, ka, sa, di, twerɛ, boro, ne deɛ ɛkeka ho. Ɛho 
nhwɛsoɔ no bi na yɛde ayɛ ɔkasamu wɔ fam ha yi:
1. Ɔkyerɛkyerɛfoɔ no noaa ɛmo.
2. Adesuafoɔ no saa nsuo.
3. Kofi ne Adwoa di fufuo.
4. Akwadaa tɔɔ nnuaba.
5. Akwantufoɔ no foroo kaa no.
Nsɛmfua a yɛakyeakyea no wɔ ɔkasamu no mu nyinaa yɛ fa-ɔyɛtia. Ɔyɛtia ahodoɔ 
no nyinaa ba adeyɛ no akyi. Nhwɛsoɔ 1 mu no, ɔyɛtia a ɛwom no ne ɛmo, ɛnna 
nhwɛsoɔ (5) mu no, ɔyɛtia a ɛwɔ mu no ne kaa.
Amfa-ɔyɛtia
Yei nso yɛ adeyɛ a edin a ɛdi nákyi no nni dwuma sɛ ɔyɛtia – saa adeyɛ yi nhia 
ɔyɛtia ansa na nteaseɛ ada adi wɔ ɔkasamu mu. Asɛmfua anaa nsɛmfua a ɛdi saa 
adeyɛ yi akyi no taa yɛ ɔkyerɛfoɔ anaa adeyɛ boafoɔ. Saa adeyɛ yi ho nhwɛsoɔ no 
mu bi ne firi, kɔ, te, nante, su, wu, da, didi, kasa, sa, hram, nyini, ne deɛ ɛkeka ho. 
Ɛho nhwɛsoɔ no mu bi na ɛwɔ fam ha yi:
1. Abarimaa no hram anɔpa biara.

Ɛdeɛn ne Ɔkyerɛfoɔ?
Hwɛ mfonini a ɛwɔ fam hɔ no. Sɛn na wɔresi tu mmirika no? Ɛyɛ ɛda no mu ɛberɛ 
bɛn? Beaeɛ bɛn na dwumadie no rekɔ soɔ? Adɛn nti na saa dwumadie no rekɔ 
soɔ?
Ɔkyerɛfoɔ yɛ asɛmfua anaa nsɛmfua a ɛkyerɛkyerɛ adeyɛ mu wɔ ɔkasamu mu. 
Ɔkyerɛfoɔ tumi san kyerɛkyerɛ ɔkyerɛfoɔ foforɔ mu. Dwene sɛdeɛ wosi nante kɔɔ 
sukuu ɛnnɛ no ho, na ɛyɛ brɛɛ, ntɛm anaa ntɛmntɛm? Ɛbɛtumi aba sɛ wonantee 
ntɛmntɛm kɔɔ sukuu. Asɛmfua ntɛmntɛm no kyerɛ sɛdeɛ wosi nante kɔɔ sukuu 
faeɛ ne saa nti, ɛyɛ ɔkyerɛfoɔ. Ɔkyerɛfoɔ nkyekyɛmu ahodoɔ no gyina sɛdeɛ ɛsi 
kyerɛkyerɛ adeyɛ a ɛkyerɛkyerɛ mu no so. Nkyekyɛmu ahodoɔ nonom ne: yɛbea 
kyerɛfoɔ, beaeɛ kyerɛfoɔ, ɛberɛ kyerɛfoɔ, dodoɔ kyerɛfoɔ, anoɔden kyerɛfoɔ ne 
ampayɛ/akyinnyegyeɛ kyerɛfoɔ.
Yɛbea kyerɛfoɔ
Saa ɔkyerɛfoɔ yi kyerɛkyerɛ ɛkwan a ɔyɛfoɔ no fa so yɛ biribi anaa sɛdeɛ dwumadie 
bi si kɔ so fa mu. Ɛho nhwɛsoɔ na ɛdidi soɔ yi:
1. Osuani no nantee ntɛmntɛm kɔɔ sukuu.
2. Bɔɔlobɔfoɔ no bɔɔ bɔɔlo no brɛɛ.
3. Adwontofoɔ no too dwom no bɔkɔɔ.
4. Anomaa no tuu ɔhareso.

Beaeɛ kyerɛfoɔ
Beaeɛ kyerɛfoɔ ka biribi fa beaeɛ pɔtee a dwumadie bi kɔ so anaa ɔyɛfoɔ bi yɛ 
biribi ho. Ɛho nhwɛsoɔ no mu bi na ɛdidi soɔ yi:
1. Adesuafoɔ no gyinagyina abɔnten.
2. Kwasi ne Adwoa Badu reda wɔ aborosan no so.
3. Adesuafoɔ no toto nkrataa gugu baabiara.
4. Adwoa Badu firi Asankragwa.
Ɛberɛ kyerɛfoɔ
Ɛberɛ kyerɛfoɔ nso ka biribi fa ɛberɛ pɔtee a dwumadie bi kɔ so anaa ɛberɛ pɔtee 
bi a ɔyɛfoɔ bi yɛ biribi ho. Ɛho nhwɛsoɔ wɔ ɔkasamu mu na ɛdidi soɔ yi:
1. Adesuafoɔ no twerɛɛ sɔhwɛ no nnora.
2. Ɛnnɛ, yɛbɛdi yɛn awiaberɛ aduane wɔ adwuma mu.
3. Yɛbɛyɛ nhyiamu anɔpa nnɔnkron.
Dodoɔ kyerɛfoɔ
Yei nso kyerɛ mpɛn dodoɔ a dwumadie bi kɔ soɔ anaa mpɛn dodoɔ a ɔyɛfoɔ bi yɛ 
adwuma bi. Saa ɔkyerɛfoɔ yi tumi di ɔkasamu anim anaa akyi nanso ɔkyerɛfoɔ 
ahodoɔ no mu kakra bi na ɛtumi di ɔkasamu anim, mfimfini anaa akyire. Dodoɔ 
kyerɛfoɔ ho nhwɛsoɔ no mu bi ne afeafe, mprenu, mprɛnsa, prɛkopɛ, da, ɛberɛ 
biara, nnawɔtwe-nnawɔtwe, da biara ne deɛ ɛkeka ho. Ɛho nhwɛsoɔ no mu bi na 
ɛdidi soɔ yi:
1. Wɔhyɛ fa afeafe.
2. Da biara, yɛdidi
3. Yɛnkɔɔ hɔ da.
4. Wɔhyɛ nkwadaa nkuran sɛ wɔntwitwi wɔn se ɛberɛ biara.
5. Meba ha nnawɔtwe-nnawɔtwe.
Ɔkasamu a ɛwowɔ ɛsoro hɔ no mu no, dodoɔ kyerɛfoɔ a ɛwowɔ mu nonom ne 
afeafe, da biara, da, ɛberɛ biara ɛnna nnawɔtwe-nnawɔtwe. Nhwɛsoɔ (2) mu 
no, ɔkyerɛfoɔ Da biara di ɔkasamu no anim. Nhwɛsoɔ (5) mu no nso, ɔkyerɛfoɔ 
nnawɔtwe-nnawɔtwe di ɔkasamu no akyi.

Ɔfa A: Adeyɛ
1. Nsonsonoeɛ bɛn na ɛda adeyɛ a ɛkyerɛ dwumadie ne deɛ ɛkyerɛ tebea 
ntam?
2. Hwehwɛ adeyɛ a ɛwɔ abasɛm a ɛwɔ fam hɔ no mu nyinaa na fa wo 
mmuaeɛ no toto wáfɛfoɔ deɛ ho:
 Mekɔɔ mpoano no, metuu mmirika, mehuriiɛ ɛnna mesaa wɔ ɛpo 
asorɔkyeɛ no mu. Owia no bɔɔ pa ara maa me ho woeɛ na me ho sisii 
me ho so. Meboroo ɛpo nsuo no bobɔɔ bi guiɛ, ɛnna medii agorɔ wom 
wɔ berɛ a na mede anigyeɛ renwenwene. Asunoma no tu faa ewiem, na 
wɔsu bɔɔ wɔn ntaban mu papapapa. Meboaboaa mpoano anwea ano 
maa ɛyɛɛ esie tenten na mede mpoano aboɔ ne nwatonturowa siesiee 
ho fɛfɛɛfɛ. Ɛda no kɔɔ nánim no, metuu mpasa de faa ɛpo no ano na 
mehunuu nneɛma bi a na asuma a me werɛ remfiri ɛho asɛm da biara 
da.
3. Kyekyɛ adeyɛ a wohunuu wɔ abasɛm a ɛwɔ ɛsoro hɔ no mu kɔ adeyɛ 
akuo mmiɛnsa a woasua ho adeɛ no mu.
Ɔfa B: Ɔkyerɛfoɔ
1. Twerɛ dwuma ahodoɔ bi a wotaa di no da biara na kyerɛkyerɛ ɛkwan 
a wofa so di no, ɛberɛ korɔ pɔtee a wodi no, beaeɛ pɔtee a wodi no ne 
sɛnti a wodi saa dwuma ahodoɔ no kyerɛ wáfɛfoɔ.
2. Twerɛ ɔkyerɛfoɔ ahodoɔ a wáfɛfoɔ de dii dwuma no na kyekyɛ mu kɔ 
ɔkyerɛfoɔ akuo no mu.
3. Fa nsɛmfua bɛyɛ aduonum (50) twerɛ abasɛm fa ewiem nsakraeɛ ne 
nnipa a wɔtete wo mpɔtam hɔ no ho. Fa ɔkyerɛfoɔ edu (10) anaa deɛ 
ɛboro saa di dwuma wɔ wábasɛm no mu.
