MI GBAMI 8 MASU
Saneyo Nyatsɔɔ He Nihi
Seneyo nyatsɔɔ
Saneyo nyatsɔɔ piɛɛ masu ngmangmɛɛ ɔmɛ a he. E ji saneyo ngmangmɛɛ nɛ kɔɔ 
ni sɛɛmi ngɛ demi kɛ gbi he. Saneyo nyatsɔɔ ngmami nyɛɛɔ animosa ngmami kɛ e 
tumi glɛ ɔ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. E nyɛɛ we gbi ɔ nya tomi kɛ pɛmi nɔ. A kɛ jeɔ yi mi tomihi, 
juɛmihi kɛ nyaziahi kpo kɛ haa e kanelɔ.
Ni tsumi 8.11
Moo ngɔ mo nitsɛ o nihi a sisi numi kɛ tsɔɔ saneyo nyatsɔɔ nya nɛ o ngɔ o 
heto ɔ kɛ to nyɛ tsu mi bi ɔmɛ a nɔ ɔ he.
Nihi nɛ ngɛ saneyo nyatsɔɔ mi
Sukpojelɔ: E ji adesa, lohwe aloo nɔ ko nɛ a tsu e he ni ngɛ masu mi. Saneyo ɔ 
daa si ngɛ ni sɛɛmi kɛ tsakpa nɛ ngɛ sukpojeli ɔmɛ a kpɛti ɔ nɔ.. Sukpojeli a he 
hiaa wawɛɛ ngɛ saneyo ɔ mi nɛ a loɔ saneyo ɔ kɛ woɔ sukpojelɔ oti ɔ he. Sukpojeli 
nɔhyɛ ni ji sukpojelɔ oti nɛ saneyo ɔ kɔɔ e he; sukpojelɔ kolisilɔ nɛ teɔ si woɔ 
sukpojelɔ oti ɔ ngɛ saneyo ɔ mi; sukpojelɔ nɛ tsakee we e juɛmi ngɛ saneyo ɔ mi 
kɛ sukpojelɔ nɛ tsakeɔ e juɛmi ke nihi tsake ngɛ saneyo ɔ mi ɔ.
Yi mi tomi oti: Enɛ ɔ peeɔ yi mi tomi pɔtɛɛ nɛ ngɛ saneyo ɔ mi kaa bua si tami 
aloo tsui si tomi. Nɔ bumi aloo bua jɔmi nami. Saneyo ma nyɛ hɛɛ yi mi tomi 
sɛtsɔ nɛ waa yi mi tomi oti ɔ sisi numi.
Jehe/bahe/he: Enɛ ɔ ji saneyo ɔ se kpo. E tsɔɔ he nɛ saneyo ɔ ya nɔ ngɛ, be mi nɛ 
saneyo ɔ ya nɔ kɛ nɔ he nɛ saneyo ɔ kɔɔ (wa he nihi, blema sanehi, kusumi aloo 
nihi nɛ bɔle wɔ)
Lomibɔ: Enɛ ɔ tsɔɔ bɔ nɛ a loɔ saneyo ɔ ha. E jeɔ juɛmihi kɛ ni peemihi kpo ngɛ 
saneyo ɔ mi. E tsuɔ kolisimi he ni; nimli a kolisimi kɛ nyagbahi. E ma nyɛ pee 
nya sami nɛ juɛmi ngɛ mi nɛ a to nya aloo nyakpɛ nɔ ko nɛ woɔ tsakemi kɛ baa.
Susumi/dahe: Enɛ ɔ ji munyutso he juɛmi hyɛmi ngɛ saneyo ɔ mi. Susumi ɔ tsɔɔ 
nɔ nɛ nɔ nɛ a da kɛ ngma saneyo ɔ. E ma nyɛ pee delɔ (saneyo delɔ ɔ piɛɛ saneyo 
ɔ he) aloo adeha (a ngmaa saneyo ɔ ngɛ sukpojeli a he se pi mɛ nitsɛmɛ. Delɔ 
biɛnamemidali ekomɛ ji: i, ami/imi kɛ ye. Adeha biɛnanemidali ɔmɛ ji: lɛ, a, mɛ 
kɛ e.

Mumi mi: Enɛ ɔ ji he numi nɛ saneyo ngmalɔ ɔ ngɛ hlae nɛ e je kpo kɛ ha kaneli. 
E ji blɔ nɔ nɛ a guɔ kɛ tsuɔ munyungu komɛ, ni komɛ, nihi, juɛmi aloo nihi nɛ ya 
nɔ kɛ be, he nɛ nɔ ko ya nɔ ngɛ he ni, kɛ gblaa tue buli aloo kaneli a juɛmi kɛ woɔ 
saneyo ɔ mi. E ma nyɛ pee mɔbɔ, buajɔ, buajɔ kɛ be nɔ, hɛ kɛ nɔ fɔmi, nyagba nɔ 
ko kɛ ekpa komɛ.
Ni tsumi 8.12
Nyɛɛ nuu nyɛ he enyɔɔnyɔ nɛ nyɛɛ sɛsɛ nihi eywiɛ nɛ ngɛ saneyo nyatsɔɔ he. 
Nyɛɛ kane nyɛ heto ɔmɛ kɛ ha nyɛ tsu mi bi ɔmɛ.
Ni tsumi 8.13
Nyɛ bi nyɛ tsɔɔlɔ ɔ nɛ ha nyɛ saneyo nyatsɔɔ ko. Nyɛɛ nuu nyɛ he nɛ nyɛɛ 
kane saneyo ɔ konɛ nyɛ yɔse nihi nɛ ngɛ saneyo nyatsɔɔ ngmami mi ɔ ngɛ mi. 
Nyɛ je oti ko kpo ngɛ saneyo ɔ mi kɛ ma nyɛ heto ɔ nɔ mi. Nyɛɛ kɛ nyɛ tsu mi 
bi ɔmɛ nɛ sɛsɛ nyɛ heto ɔmɛ a he.

Phonology (Speech sounds of a Ghanaian language)
INTRODUCTION
Dear learner, you are welcome to this section which discusses the foundation 
of language (speech sounds). You will be introduced to the concepts of vowels 
and consonants of your language of study and how speech sounds are described 
(parametre). It will focus on where the speech sounds occur in words of a Ghanaian 
language. For example, where vowels and consonants can occur in a word of a 
Ghanaian language such as initial position, medial position, or final position of 
a word. Again, Dear learner you will be introduced to the distribution of vowels 
and consonants in their language, aiding them to form meaningful words and 
facilitate effective speaking and reading in the language. This section is essential 
for learners not only in the context of Ghanaian language studies but also to 
establish links with related subjects such as English and other languages. This 
section equips you with foundational knowledge and functional understanding 
of speech sounds and their role in language learning. In summary, you should be 
able to identify, explain, produce, and label vowel charts and consonant tables of 
your language of study.
At the end of this section, you should be able to:
1. Describe the vowels of a Ghanaian language using the right parameters 
(e.g., lip posture, tongue height and part of the tongue).
2. Describe the consonants of the Ghanaian language using the right 
parameters (e.g., voicing, place of articulation and manner of articulation).
3. Explain the distribution of vowels of the Ghanaian language (e.g., word 
initial, medial and final).
4. Explain the distribution of consonants of the Ghanaian language (e.g., 
word initial, medial and final).

SECTION 1 SOUNDS OF THE LANGUAGE
Key ideas
• Production refers to the making or saying of a speech sound in language. 
Speech sound is a sound used in the formation of words for human 
communication. The production of speech sound involves obstruction 
which is the interruption of free flow of air during production of speech 
sounds. Sounds are distributed in languages and this refers to the place 
or position in a word where a sound can appear. Sound involves airflow 
which is a mass movement of air that is meant for the production of 
speech sounds. Another term for it is airstream.
TYPES OF SPEECH SOUNDS
Speech sounds can be grouped into two main types, namely vowels and consonants. 
It is the combination of these two types of sounds that produces words. In other 
words, all words are made up of individual speech sounds. For examples, the word 
pan consists of three individual speech sounds, that is, /p/, /a/, /n/. The sound /a/ 
is a vowel, whereas the sounds /p/ and /n/ are consonants. In the following topics 
we discuss both vowels and consonants focusing on how each is produced in a 
Ghanaian language.
The concept of vowel
The concept vowel refers as a speech sound in which production there is a little or 
no obstruction of the flow of air in the oral cavity. In other words, a speech sound 
which when being produced the air is not obstructed or it is minimally obstructed 
in the oral cavity is referred to as a vowel. Since in their production there is no 
or very little obstruction of airflow, vowels are comparatively heard louder when 
they are produced. Vowels are very important part of words. There cannot be a 
word without a vowel or vowel-like sound. This important role vowel plays in a 
word will later on in your second year be discussed when we are talking about the 
syllable.
Description of vowels
Dear learner, in describing vowels of a Ghanaian language, there are certain 
properties we use. These properties are often termed parametres. Parametres 
simply refer to the characteristics that a vowel possesses. The main parametres 
used in describing vowels are the tongue height, lip posture, and part of the tongue 
4

used during the production of the vowel sound. In addition to the three, there 
is a fourth parameter called advancement of the tongue root in some Ghanaian 
languages such as Akan. Let us begin the discussions of these parametres.
Lip position/posture:
The parametre lip posture is used to determine the position your lips assume when 
you are producing a vowel. So, at this level, the lips assume two main postures 
or positions, namely rounded or unrounded. That is, whether the lips are rounded 
or they are not rounded when a vowel sound is being produced. Based on this 
posture of the lips, we can divide vowels of a Ghanaian language into two, namely 
‘rounded’ and ‘spread/unrounded.’ Some examples of rounded vowels are /u, 
o, ɔ/. examples of unrounded vowels, on the other hand, are /i, e, a/.
Activity
At this point, produce rounded and unrounded/spread vowels of your Ghanaian 
language of study.
Tongue height/Height of the tongue:
This refers to the position of the tongue in reference to the root of the mouth when 
producing vowel sounds. It is assumed that when we are producing vowels, the 
mouth opens when we drop the jaw. This can be high, mid, or low. When we 
drop our jaws to the lowest possible position, the vowels produced in this way are 
referred to as low vowels. Examples of low vowel is /a/, and in some Ghanaian 
languages [æ]. When we open our mouth wide enough but not as low as when 
producing low vowels, then the vowels we produced are termed mid vowels. 
Some examples of mid vowels in a Ghanaian language are /e, o/. In producing 
high vowels, on the other hand, the mouth is significantly opened but not as wide 
as mid vowels, thereby allowing enough air to flow through the oral cavity. Some 
examples of high vowels in a Ghanaian language are /i, u/.
Activity
Begin practicing the production of vowels in your language of study focusing 
on how high or how low you raise your jaws or open your mouth.
5
SECTION 1 SOUNDS OF THE LANGUAGE
Part of the tongue:
This parametre refers to the area of the tongue where the vowel sound is produced. 
It is assumed that when we are producing vowels, some parts of the tongue 
move. We cannot easily feel this movement though. Three parts of the tongue 
are assumed to be involved when a vowel sounds is being produced. These parts 
are the front part, middle part, and back part. Based on that, the parametre gives 
us three classes of vowels, namely front, mid, and back vowels. In producing 
front vowels, it is the front part of the tongue that moves. Some examples of front 
vowels of a Ghanaian language are /i, e, ɛ/. For the production of mid vowels, 
the middle of the tongue is assumed to move. Therefore, the following vowel is 
an example of a mid-vowel: /a/. For back vowels, on the other hand, as the name 
suggests, it is the back of the tongue that is involved in their production. Some 
examples of back vowels of a Ghanaian language are: /u, o, ɔ/.
Activity
Practice how to produce vowels of your language of study with focus on the 
part of the tongue.
Having finished discussing the main parametres we use in describing vowels of 
a Ghanaian language, there is a fourth parametre as mentioned earlier in this 
sub-strand which is not common among Ghanaian languages. This parametre is 
advancement of the tongue.
Advancement of the tongue root (ATR): (Please, discuss only if applicable in 
your language). This parametre, which is prominent in a few Ghanaian languages 
including Akan, Dagbani, etc. It is used to determine the position the tongue root 
assumes when a vowel is being produced. By this parametre, we try to find out 
if there is tension or pressure on the tongue or not during production of vowels. 
When a vowel is produced with pressure on the tongue thereby causing the tongue 
root to draw back, we say that vowel is produced with Advanced Tongue Root 
(ATR) i.e. (+ATR) vowels. When vowels are produced with the tongue root in its 
natural neutral position, we label those vowels are Unadvanced Tongue Root i.e. 
(-ATR) vowels. Some examples of (+ATR) vowels are: /i, e, u, o/, and examples 
of (-ATR) vowels are /ɪ, ɛ, ɔ/.

Having discussed the nature of vowel sounds and the parametres used in 
describing the vowel sounds of your language, we now focus our attention on 
the production of consonants.
The concept of consonant
As was mentioned earlier in the section, consonant is another type of speech sounds 
apart from vowel. The concept consonant refers to a speech sound in which during 
production the breath, which we have termed airflow, is at least obstructed. Based 
on this explanation, we can contrast vowel and consonant by saying that while in 
the production of vowel there is very minimal or no obstruction of airflow, there 
is significant obstruction of airflow when producing consonants. We combined 
vowels and consonants form a word.

Consonant Distribution
The concept consonant distribution simply refers to the position in a word where 
a consonant can occur in a particular Ghanaian language. A consonant that 
occurs at the beginning of a word is referred to as word initial consonant. When a 
consonant occurs at the middle of a word, we refer to it as word medial consonant. 
When a consonant occurs at the end of a word, we refer to refer to it as word final 
consonant. Let us note that some consonants can occur in all positions of a word. 
For example, in some Ghanaian languages, the consonant /m/ can occur in the 
three positions in a word.

INTRODUCTION
This section discusses identification of key ideas in texts and discourse. It 
always gives information on specific ideas or knowledge to the reader or hearer. 
The information given may come from all perspectives such as education, 
industrialisation, mining among others. It may also indicate some cultural values 
such as respect, tolerance and patience. Identifying key ideas gives you a better 
understanding of the discourse. It also enhances your critical thinking skills and 
interpretation abilities. There are types of reading techniques namely skimming 
and scanning and the application of any of the type enables you to get the right 
information demanded at any time. Knowledge of the types is therefore essential 
in our everyday life. The concept of oral interpretation will also be discussed. We 
shall discuss the skills needed for effective interpretation. Interpretation plays 
important roles in facilitating communication across language barriers.
At the end of this section, you should be able to
• Identify key ideas from appropriate discourse. E.g., cultural values 
(respect, kindness, tolerance and others), education, child trafficking, 
environment, industrialisation in Ghana, mining, GESI etc.,
• Discuss ideas and relevant opinions from selected discourse. E.g., 
cultural values (respect, kindness, tolerance and others), education, 
child trafficking, environment, industrialisation in Ghana, mining, GESI, 
STEM, etc.
Key Ideas
 Key ideas are the main messages that is relevant in any discourse. Some 
of the key ideas may center on cultural values such as respect, kindness, 
tolerance, patience, etc. In any discourse you can share relevant opinions 
on any discourse appropriately and interpret any discourse in your own 
understanding.

 Dear learner, before leaving home for your present school, what are the 
main points from the conversation you had with your parent/guardian? 
Share with peers.
 The main points you shared with your peers are known to as key ideas. 
Key ideas are the essential ideas that the author or speaker wants to give 
to the reader or hearer/listener respectively. The ideas may include the 
claims, the reasons, conclusions, definitions, classifications, comparisons, 
evaluations, recommendations, etc. Key ideas can be expressed explicitly 
or implicitly.
 For you to identify the key ideas in discourse there is the need for you 
to understand the main concepts, arguments, and the points made. Note 
that the discourse could deal with any topic such as mining, teenage 
pregnancy, natural disaster, educational issues among others. It must also 
be pointed out that it could also come in a text form, video or picture or 
all the forms mentioned.
 In summary, my dear learner to identify the key ideas in a discourse which 
may be written or oral or visual, you may need to answer the following 
questions
• Find who or what the passage discusses: Does this passage discuss a 
person, group of people or an entity?
• Ask when the event took place: Does the information contain a reference 
to time?
• Find where the event took place: Does the text name a place?
• Ask why the event took place: Do you find a reason or explanation for 
something that happened?
• Ask how the event took place: Does this information indicate a method 
or a theory?
 NB: In a text, key ideas are sometimes italicised, boldened, or underlined. 
You can also find it in the topic sentence.

Reading
By the end of the sub-strand you should be able to:

2. Discuss scanning using the strategies (e.g., movement of eyes or finger,

Key ideas
 Skimming is going through a text rapidly to get the general information 
in the text while scanning involves looking for a specific information in 
a text. Scanning is a process of reading in which your eyes quickly run 
through a piece of text to find a piece of relevant information. Scanning 
and skimming are two different concepts of reading.
TYPES OF READING
There are types of reading skill or technique namely skimming, scanning, 
intensive reading and extensive reading. Dear learner, in this lesson you shall 
learn skimming and scanning techniques of reading.
Skimming
Skimming is a reading technique used to quickly identify the main ideas or key 
points in a text. It is the action of reading something quickly so as to note only the 
important points. Basically, skimming is reading rapidly in order to get a general 
overview of the material read. It is used to find specific facts in texts. It involves 
glancing over the material, focusing on headings, subheadings, bold text and key 
phrases to get a general understanding of the content. Skimming is useful when; 
time is limited, looking for specific information, you want to get an overview 
8
SECTION 2 SHARING IDEAS AND ORAL INTERPRETATION
before reading in-depth and you are dealing with a large amount of text. Below 
are the skimming types.
Preview: An opportunity to view something before it is acquired or becomes 
generally available. Preview is done in an effort to learn about the ideas presented 
and the structure of their development.
Overview: Used to sample the reading material more thoroughly. A general review 
or summary of a subject.
Review: The review is done to re-familiarise yourself with the material you have 
previously read thoroughly or skimmed. A formal assessment of something with 
the intention of instituting a change if necessary.
Learner, in skimming, you can follow these steps
- Read the title
- Read the headings and sub-headings as well as topic sentences in each 
paragraph
- Look for important information such as date, names and unusual words.
- Read the conclusion

In summary you have learnt skimming and the steps as well as the types of 
skimming which you can apply. Dear learner, let us examine what is scanning.
Scanning
Scanning is reading rapidly in order to find facts without reading everything. 
Scanning helps you locate a particular fact while skimming tells you what general 
information is within a section.
Scanning involves looking for a specific information in a text. It can also be said 
to be a process of reading in which your eyes quickly run through a piece of text 
to find a piece of relevant information. In scanning the reader looks for a piece 
of specific information. An example of scanning is searching for the meaning 
of a word in a dictionary. Scanning helps the reader to locate particular facts in 
an entire text quickly. Students often use scanning when solving their reading 
comprehension questions.
It is important to know the purpose for scanning. You should know what you are 
searching for, eg title of a book, a website, a reference material, a particular word 
or phrase and a particular story you want to read etc. You should know how the 
10

material is structures either alphabetically, non-alphabetically, chronologically, 
by category, by titles /headings, by textual sense, by numbers among others.
Scanning helps a learner to read more and to develop love for reading.
When to scan
1. Scan before reading
2. Scan a number of questions to identify the one which you are most 
comfortable answering
3. When searching for particular information such as date, keywords etc.
The following shows how to do scanning after getting overview of a text and 
identifying the sections of the text you want to read.
1. Start scanning the text by moving your eyes and fingers quickly over it
2. When you have identified the information, word or the phrase you are 
searching for, read the information surrounding the word carefully
3. When you identified the information that requires attention, you read it 
thoroughly slowly.

Oral Interpretation and translation
At the end of the sub-strand the learner should be able to:
 Discuss oral interpretation focusing on effective listening, encoding and

Key Ideas
 Oral interpretation is reframing the meaning of a speech most often orally 
into another language. The original language is the source language 
and the language in which it is rendered is the target language. In oral 
interpretation you must note the cultural differences and be accurate in 
giving the meaning of what you are to render in the language orally.
CONTENT
Interpretation is listening to a message in one language and rendering it orally 
in another language maintaining the original meaning, tone and context. It 
is the stylistic representation of a creative work or dramatic role. It is the act 
of explaining, reframing, or otherwise showing your own understanding of 
something. In interpretation you first have to understand the text or the piece 
given to you and then explain in your own words. In broader terms it is rendering 
a spoken or signed message into another spoken or signed language preserving 
the register and meaning of the source language content.
Dear learner, it must be noted that before you can do any interpretation, you must 
be well versed in the source and target language. Interpretation can be performed 
either simultaneously or consecutively between users of different languages.
Dear learner, know that in interpreting you do not embellish or over-exaggerate. 
State the ideas clearly. In interpreting you need to listen carefully, decode and 
encode as they serve as the process of communication and interpreting.

Akpa A: Dɔwɔnyawo
1. Aleke dɔwɔnya siwo ɖe nuwɔna fia kple dɔwɔnya siwo ɖe nuwɔƒemenɔla ƒe 
nɔnɔme fia la to vovo tso wo nɔewo gbɔe?
2. De dzesi dɔwɔnyawo katã le nuŋlɔɖi si gbɔna la me eye nàtsɔ wò ŋuɖoɖo la 
asɔ kple xɔ̃wò tɔ.
Esi mezɔ kabakaba ɖo ƒua ta la, meƒu du, ti kpo, eye meɖu ɣe le 
ƒutsotsoewo me. Ŋdɔ ʋu nyuie hede dzo lãme nam eye ŋusẽ gaɖo ŋunye. 
Meƒu tsi, hl ẽ tsi eye mefe fefe le tsia me heko alɔgbɔnu kple dzidzɔ. 
Tɔkɔtsalɛwo dzo va yi, xlɔ̃, heƒo woƒe aʋalawo papapa. Metsɔ ke tu xɔ 
nyui aɖe eye metsɔ adzato kple kpekuiwo ɖo atsy ɔ̃ nɛ. Metsa le ƒua ta 
hede dzesi nu nyui geɖe siwo nyemekpɔ kpɔ o la le ƒua ta. Nyemaŋlɔ 
nuteƒekpɔkpɔ sia be kpɔ o.
3. Ma dɔwɔnya siwo nède dzesii le nuŋlɔɖi si va yi me la ɖe woƒe hatsotso etɔ̃ 
siwo nèsrɔ̃ la me.
Akpa B: Dɔwɔnyaɖɔnyawo
1. Ŋlɔ nu siwo nèwɔna gbe sia gbe la da ɖi eye nàgblɔ ale si nèwɔa wo, 
ɣeyiɣi si me nèwɔa wo, teƒe siwo nèwɔa wo le kple susu siwo ta nèwɔa 
wo ɖo la na xɔ̃wò.
2. Ŋlɔ dɔwɔnyaɖɔnya siwo katã xɔ̃wò la zã le nuwɔnaawo ɖɔɖɔ me la da 
ɖi eye nàma wo ɖe woƒe hatsotsowo me.
3. Tso nyadu si anɔ abe nya blaatɔ̃ (50) ene la tso yame ƒe tɔtrɔ kple ame 
siwo le teƒe si nèle la ŋu. Dɔwɔnyaɖɔnya 10 teti nènɔ wò nyadu la me.

Numenyaduwo Kple Nyadu Ŋlɔɖiwo
NUƲUƲU
Akpa sia dzro nyati vovovo siwo numenyadu kple nyadu ŋlɔɖiwo lɔ ɖe 
eme la me. Le akpa sia la, àsrɔ̃ nu tso nu si tsiƒoɖi si nye numenyaduwo 
dometɔ ɖeka la  ŋu. Nusɔsrɔ̃ la ku ɖe tsiƒoɖi ƒe vevinyenyewo kple ale 
si woƒoa tsi ɖi la ŋu. Edzro gbedodoɖa ƒe vevinyenye kple susu siwo ta 
míedoa gbe ɖa ɖo la me. Ele be nàku nu gɔme tso susu si ta tsiƒoɖi le 
vevie le mia de la ŋu. Akpa sia le vevie na wò elabena edo ka kple nusɔsrɔ̃ 
bubuwo abe Subɔsubɔŋutinusɔsrɔ̃ ene. Akpa sia ana aɖaŋu si awɔe be 
nàte ŋu ade dzesi mia de kɔnuwo ƒe vevinyenye kple ame bubuwo tɔ la 
wò.
Le akpa sia ke la, àgasrɔ̃ nu ku ɖe avihɛwo ŋu le Ghana dukɔa me. Le esia 
me la, àlé ŋku ɖe avihɛwo ŋu le Eʋeawo dome. Àdzro avihɛ aɖewo me. 
Numedzodzro sia aku ɖe avihɛwo ƒe vevinyenyewo ŋu koŋ.
Tsɔ kpe ɖe eŋu la, akpa sia gaƒo nu tso ŋutinya kple nu siwo wòlɔ ɖe eme 
la ŋu. Miaƒe nufiala akpe ɖe mia ŋu be miadzro nu siwo ŋutinya lɔ ɖe eme 
abe nuwɔla, nyati, ŋutinya ƒe zɔzɔme, teƒe kple ɣeyiɣi, nyagblɔmɔnu kple 
bubuawo ene la me.
Le nusɔsrɔ̃ sia ƒe nuwuwu la, ele be:
• Nàƒlɔ ŋku ɖe tsiƒoɖi ƒe tutuɖo le Eʋeawo dome me (tɔgbeawo kple 
mawuawo yɔyɔ kple woƒe ŋkɔwo ƒoƒo ɖo, gbedeasi, kple taƒoƒo)
• Nàdzro avihɛwo me (wɔƒewo kple vevinyenyewo)
• Nàdzro nu siwo ŋutinya lɔ ɖe eme la me (kpɔɖeŋu: nuwɔla, nyati, 
ŋutinya ƒe zɔzɔme, teƒe kple ɣeyiɣi, nyagblɔmɔnu kple bubuawo)
• Nàdzro ŋutinyawo me (tanya, nyati, gbezazã, gbeɖaŋuwo kple 
bubuawo)

AKPA 8LIA  NYADUWO
Nyati Veviwo
• Tsiƒoɖi nye dekɔnugbedodoɖa.
• Ɖoƒe vevi etɔ̃e le tsiƒoɖi me. Esiawoe nye: Tɔgbeawo kple mawuawo 
yɔyɔ kple woƒe ŋkɔwo ƒoƒo ɖo (nuʋuʋu), gbedeasi (tsia ŋutɔ ƒoƒo 
ɖi), taƒoƒo.
• Nyatie nye susu vevitɔ si le ŋutinya la me.
• Ŋutinya ƒe zɔzɔmee nye ɖoɖo si nu nudzɔdzɔwo yi edzi le le 
ŋutinya la me la.
• Teƒe kple ɣeyiɣi ƒoa nu tso teƒe kple ɣeyiɣi si nudzɔdzɔwo yi edzi 
le la ŋu.
• Nyagblɔmɔnu nye ale si nuŋlɔla la gblɔ eƒe ŋutinya lae la. Le 
kpɔɖeŋu me, nuŋlɔla la tea ŋu gblɔa ŋutinya la abe ɖe wòle eteƒe 
kpɔ nuawo wodzɔ alo ɖe eya ŋutɔ kpɔ gome le nudzɔdzɔwo me 
ene. Nyagblɔmɔnu tea ŋu nyea ame gbãtɔ (si me nuƒola la nyea 
nuwɔlawo dometɔ ɖeka le la) alo ame etɔ̃lia.
• Avihɛwo ɖea ame aɖe ƒe dodo le agbagbeawo dome yi kukuawo 
dome  fiana; enye konyifafa ɖe ale si wobu ame aɖee la ŋu; enye 
seselelãmeɖeɖe fia.
TSIƑOƉI
Numedzodzro sia lé ŋku ɖe tsiƒoɖi ƒe ɖoƒe vevi etɔ̃awo ŋu. Eƒo nu tso 
nuʋuʋu/tɔgbeawo kple mawuawo yɔyɔ kple woƒe ŋkɔwo ƒoƒo ɖo, gbedeasi/
tsia ƒoƒo ɖi kple taƒoƒo ŋu.
Nu kae nye tsiƒoɖi?
Tsiƒoɖi nye gbedodoɖa na Mawugã to tɔgbeawo dzi. Enye mɔnu si dzi 
woƒoa dzatsi kple aha sesẽ ɖi na mawuawo kple tɔgbeawo le la. Le Ayim-
Aboagye (1993) ƒe nya nu la, tsiƒoɖi nye nuwɔna si me woƒoa tsi, aha sesẽ 
alo aha vivi abe wain ene ɖi na tɔgbeawo le be woatsɔ abia kpekpeɖeŋu 
tso wo gbɔ. Le teƒe aɖewo la, wozãa kuinuwo abe mɔlu ene le tsiƒoɖi me. 
Tsiƒoɖi wɔa wɔƒe vevi aɖe le Afrika dukɔwo dome. Le tsiƒoɖi me la, wokpea 
tɔgbeawo, ame siwo wobu be woƒe wɔƒe le vevie la le dutoƒotakpekpewo 
wɔwɔ me. Le Ghana dukɔa me la, ƒometatɔwo kple dekɔnudziɖulawo

Nu siwo tsiƒoɖi ƒe tutuɖo lɔ ɖe eme la woe nye: nuʋuʋu/tɔgbeawo kple

Mawuawo kple tɔgbeawo yɔyɔ kple woƒe ŋkɔwo ƒoƒo ɖo
Le ɖoƒe sia la, woyɔa mawuawo heƒoa woƒe ŋkɔwo ɖo. Tsiƒola la yɔa 
Mawugã gbã, emegbe la, eyɔa dutrɔ̃wo, mawuawo kple tɔgbeawo. Ɖoƒe 
sia nye ʋɔƒoƒo alo agododo na Mawugã kple mawuawo. Kpɔɖeŋu si gbɔna

M ba Sibiri, yiɣisi deegi a kom. Father Sibiri, wake up and take your water.
A yi neei nyin neei a ba Danaa. If you wake up, wake your father Danaa.
Ka o gba neei ti yaba Bidira. And he will wake up our grandfather Bidira.
Yi saa kom m-bɔŋɔ This is your rainwater

Gbedeasi la/tsia ŋutɔ ƒoƒo ɖi
Le tsiƒoɖi me la, gbedeasie nye susu si ta wole tsia ƒom ɖi ɖo la. Esia ate 
ŋu anye nubiabia alo akpedada. Le ɖoƒe sia la, tsiƒoɖila la gblɔa susu si ta 
wòyɔ wo ɖo la na wo eye wòbiaa woƒe amegbɔnɔnɔ le wɔna blibo la katã 
me. Afi siae wòbiana tso tɔgbeawo si le be woakpɔ yewo ta le.
Taƒoƒo
Le tsiƒoɖi ƒe ɖoƒe sia la, tsiƒoɖila la daa akpe na mawuawo. Ɣe aɖewo ɣi la, 
wotea ŋu ɖea adzɔgbe na tɔgbeawo alo mawuawo be ne wowɔ nu si dim 
yewole la, yewoana esi kple ekemɛ wo. Tsiƒoɖila la biana tso mawuawo 
si be woakpɔ yewo ta eye ne ame aɖe di vɔ̃e na yewo la, vɔ̃ la nadze wo 
ŋutɔ dzi. Egadia ɖagbe tso mawuawo gbɔ na ame siwo le nu nyuiwo wɔm 
na dua la. Le go aɖewo me nenye be tsilelekɔnu ƒe tsiƒoɖie la, wosaa vɔ le 
ɖoƒe sia. Nɔnɔmetata siwo gbɔna la ɖe tsiƒoɖi le ameha vovovowo dome 
le Ghana la fia.

iv. Enye degbenɔnɔ kple blemanyawo ŋuti nunya ɖeɖe fia.
v. Enye bubudede ƒometɔ alo xɔlɔ̃ siwo yi nugbe la ŋu.
vi. Enana be wosrɔ̃a nya yeyewo.
vii. Enana be amewo ƒoa nu nyuie.

AVIHƐWO
Ŋugbledede: Seselelãme kae vana na wò nenye be miaƒe ƒometɔ aɖe ku?
Nu kae nye avihɛ?
Enye ha si yɔ fũu kple konyifafa kple vevesese. Le go bubu me la, enye 
konyifaha si wodzina le kuteƒewo kple ŋkuɖodziwɔnawo wɔƒewo. Eganye 
nublanuiha si wodzina blewuu si ɖea fu lãme na ame la. Wogadzia 
avihɛwo tsɔna kafua ameyinugbewo alo dea bubu wo ŋu. Enye kɔnu si 
wowɔna na ame si ku la.
Avihɛwo ƒe wɔƒewo
Le Afrika dukɔwo dome la, wɔƒe geɖewo le avihɛwo si. Wo dometɔ aɖewoe 
nye esiwo gbɔna:
1. Wodzinɛ tsɔna faa konyi ɖe ameyinugbewo ŋu.
2. Wodzinɛ tsɔna doa hedenyui na ameyinugbe la.
3. Wodzinɛ tsɔna naa gbedeasi vevi aɖe.
4. Wodzinɛ tsɔna dia ɖagbe na ameyinugbe la le tsiẽƒe.
5. Wodzinɛ tsɔna ɖea seselelãme fiana.
Avihɛwo ƒe vevinyenye
Avihɛwo ƒe vevinyenye aɖewo nye esiwo gbɔna:
1. Enyea kafukafu kple bubu na ameyinugbe la.
2. Eɖea kadodo si le tsã kple fifiɣeyiɣi alo kukuawo kple agbagbewo 
dome la fiana.
3. Eɖea kadodo mavɔ si le ameyinugbea kple eƒe ƒometɔwo dome la 
fiana.
4. Eɖea vevesese ɖe ameyiku la ŋu fiana.

NU SIWO ŊUTINYA LƆ ƉE EME
Ŋutinya
Ŋutinya nye nyadu ŋlɔɖiwo dometɔ ɖeka. Enye nyadu si zɔna ɖe nuƒoƒo 
kple gbezazã ƒe ɖoɖowo nu. Ezɔna ɖe gbeŋutise kple gbegbɔgblɔ ƒe tutuɖo 
ƒe ɖoɖowo nu abe ale si míeƒoa nu ene. Mezɔna ɖe hakpanya ƒe tutuɖo 
nu o. Enye nyadu si wozãna tsɔna ɖea tamesusuwo gblɔna na nuxlẽla la.
Nuwɔna 8.11
Ɖe nu si ŋutinyanyadu nye la me le wò gɔmesese nu eye nàtsɔ wò 
ŋuɖoɖo la asɔ kple wò nusrɔ̃hati aɖe tɔ.
Nu siwo ŋutinya lɔ ɖe eme
1. Nuwɔlawo: Wonye ame, lã, alo nu bubu aɖe si wɔ nane le nyadu 
me la. Nuwɔlawo tea ŋu nyea amewo alo lãwo. Ŋutinya la kuna 
ɖe kadodo si le nu siwo yi edzi le nuwɔla vovovowo dome la ŋu. 
Nuwɔlawo le vevie le ŋutinya la ƒe zɔzɔme eye nuwɔla vevitɔwo ƒe 
wɔƒewo wɔa dɔ ɖe ŋutinya la ƒe zɔzɔme dzi. Wonyea ame siwo ŋu 
nudzɔdzɔwo ƒo nu tsoe wu le ŋutinya la me. Nuwɔla vevitɔ siawo 
dometɔ aɖewoe nye nuwɔla gã nu nyui wɔla; nuwɔla gã vɔ̃ ɖitɔ si 
tsia tsitre ɖe nuwɔla gã la ŋu hehea kuxi geɖewo vaa ŋutinya la me 
la; nuwɔla si ƒe nɔnɔme metrɔna o kple nuwɔla si ƒe nɔnɔme trɔna ɖe 
nudzɔdzɔwo ŋu nɔa ŋutinya la me.
2. Nyati: Esia nye gbedeasi si le ŋutinya aɖe me la. Zi geɖe la, gbedeasi 
la dzena to nuwɔlawo ƒe nuwɔnawo kple kadodo si le wo dome la 
me. Nyati vivivi siwo tua nyati vevitɔ ɖo la tea ŋu nɔa ŋutinyawo 
me.
3. Teƒe kple Ɣeyiɣi: Esia nye gɔmeɖokpe na ŋutinya la. Elɔ nutsotso tso 
teƒe kple ɣeyiɣi si me ŋutinya la dzɔ le la ɖe eme (hadomegbenɔnyawo/
hamenuwɔnawo, blemanyatotowo, degbenɔnɔ kple teƒe tɔxɛaɖe)
4. Ŋutinya ƒe Zɔzɔme: Esia nye ɖoɖo si nu nudzɔdzɔwo le le ŋutinya 
la me la. Eɖea ale si nuwɔnawo zɔ le ŋutinya la me la fiana. Ewɔa 
dɔ ɖe adika, tsitretsitsi ɖe ame nɔewo ŋu kple kuxi siwo do mo ɖa 
la dzi. Ate ŋu anye nu siwo dzɔna alo nu wɔnuku si amewo mele 
mɔkpɔkpɔ me na o la.
11
AKPA 8LIA  NYADUWO
5. Nyagblɔmɔnu: Esia nye nukpɔsusu si nuwɔla aɖe tsɔ le ŋutinya la 
gblɔm la. Etea ŋu nyea ame gbãtɔ (si me nuƒola la nyea nuwɔlawo 
dometɔ ɖeka le la) alo ame etɔ̃lia.
6. Seselelãme: Enye seselelãme si nuŋlɔla la di be wòava na nuxlẽla 
la. Enye seselelãme si nuŋlɔla la di be nesu nuxlẽla la si to 
susumenukpɔkpɔ, nɔnɔmewo, nuwo, susuwo, alo nudzɔdzɔwo kple 
nu bubu siwo ku ɖe teƒe kple ɣeyiɣi siwo ŋu nuŋlɔla la ƒo nu tso 
la ŋu. Etea ŋu nyea blanuiléle, dziɖuɖu, dzidzɔkpɔkpɔ, mɔkpɔkpɔ, 
dzɔgbevɔ̃e kple bubuawo ƒe seselelãmewo.
Nuwɔna 8.12
Minɔ eveve miaƒo nu tso nu siwo ŋutinya lɔ ɖe eme la dometɔ ene ŋu. 
Migblɔ nu siwo ŋu mieke ɖo la na klase la katã.
Nuwɔna 8.13
Bia miaƒe nufiala wòatsɔ ŋutinyanyadu aɖe na wò. Mi kple wò 
nusrɔ̃hati mixlẽ ŋutinyanyadu la eye mialé ŋku ɖe nu siwo ŋutinya 
lɔ ɖe eme la ƒe vevinyenyewo ŋu. Miɖo kpe miaƒe ŋuɖoɖo la dzi kple 
kpɔɖeŋu siwo tso nyadu la me la.

 AMEGAXI KPLE GBƆ̃VI LA
 Gbɔ̃vi aɖe nɔ anyi gbe aɖe gbe. Esi eƒe dzowo nɔ tsitsim ta la, esusu 
be yenye gbɔ̃tsu tsitsi si ate ŋu anɔ eɖokui si la. Eya ta gbe ɖeka ɣetrɔ, 
esi woɖu gbe vɔ henɔ dzodzom eye dadaa yɔe la, gbɔ̃vi la meke nu de 
dadaa o, ke boŋ eganɔ gbe fɛ̃ aɖewo ɖum. Eteƒe medidi o la, efɔ ta 
dzi eye wòkpɔ be gbɔ̃ mamlɛawo katã le ye gbɔ.
 Eya ɖeka koe susɔ ɖe afi ma. Ɣe yina ɖe to ɖo ge. Nuwo ƒe vɔvɔli 
legbewo le zɔ ɖem le anyigba. Ya fafɛ aɖe ƒo ɖo gbewo me eye hoowɔwɔ 
ɖo wo dome ŋɔdzitɔe. Vɔvɔ̃ ɖo gbɔ̃vi la esi wòɖo ŋku amegaxi vɔ̃ɖi 
aɖe dzi. Emegbe la, edze xɔxlɔ̃ gɔme henɔ dadaa dim le gbeɖuƒe la. 
Gake hafi wòaɖo ative aɖe me la, kasia amegaxi lae nye esi!
 Gbɔ̃vi la kpɔe dze sii be yeƒe agbe le xaxa me.
 Ede asi ƒoƒo me hegblɔ be, “Aƒetɔ Amegaxi, meɖe kuku, menya be èle 
ɖuye ge. Gake gbã la, meɖe kuku dzi ha nam, elabena medi be maɖu 
ɣe ahakpɔ dzidzɔ abe ale si mate ŋui la ene.”
 Edo dzidzɔ na amegaxi la be yele ha vi aɖe dzi ge hafi aɖu nu, eya 
ta edzi ha vivi aɖe eye gbɔ̃vi la ti kpo heɖu ɣe dzidzɔtɔe.
 Le ɣeyiɣi sia me la, gbɔ̃ mamlɛawo nɔ zɔzɔm blewuu ɖo ta aƒe me. 
Ɣetrɔya fafɛ la ƒe ƒoƒo na amegaxi la ƒe hadzidzi la de didiƒewo ke. 
Hadzidzi la ge ɖe to me na avu siwo kplɔ gbɔ̃awo yi ɖe gbeɖuƒe la. 
Wode dzesii be ha siae amegaxi la dzina hafi ɖua nu. Kasia wotrɔ ɖo 
ta gbeɖuƒe la kple du. Amegaxi ƒe hadzidzi la tɔ enumake. Avuawo 
yɔe ɖe du nu. Esi avuawo gogo amegaxi la keŋ vɔ la, egblɔ na eɖokui 
be yedzɔ movi ŋutɔ be yewɔ gbɔ̃vi la ƒe lɔlɔ̃nu le esime wòle be yealée 
aɖu hafi.

SECTION 1 SOUNDS OF THE LANGUAGE
ORAL CONVERSATION
Phonology (Speech sounds of a Ghanaian language)
INTRODUCTION
Dear learner, you are welcome to this section which discusses the foundation 
of language (speech sounds). You will be introduced to the concepts of vowels 
and consonants of your language of study and how speech sounds are described 
(parametre). It will focus on where the speech sounds occur in words of a Ghanaian 
language. For example, where vowels and consonants can occur in a word of a 
Ghanaian language such as initial position, medial position, or final position of 
a word. Again, Dear learner you will be introduced to the distribution of vowels 
and consonants in their language, aiding them to form meaningful words and 
facilitate effective speaking and reading in the language. This section is essential 
for learners not only in the context of Ghanaian language studies but also to 
establish links with related subjects such as English and other languages. This 
section equips you with foundational knowledge and functional understanding 
of speech sounds and their role in language learning. In summary, you should be 
able to identify, explain, produce, and label vowel charts and consonant tables of 
your language of study.
At the end of this section, you should be able to:
By the end of the lesson, you should be able to:
1. Describe the vowels of a Ghanaian language using the right parameters 
(e.g., lip posture, tongue height and part of the tongue).
2. Describe the consonants of the Ghanaian language using the right 
parameters (e.g., voicing, place of articulation and manner of articulation).
3. Explain the distribution of vowels of the Ghanaian language (e.g., word 
initial, medial and final).

SECTION 1 SOUNDS OF THE LANGUAGE
Key ideas
• Production refers to the making or saying of a speech sound in language. 
Speech sound is a sound used in the formation of words for human 
communication. The production of speech sound involves obstruction 
which is the interruption of free flow of air during production of speech 
sounds. Sounds are distributed in languages and this refers to the place 
or position in a word where a sound can appear. Sound involves airflow 
which is a mass movement of air that is meant for the production of 
speech sounds. Another term for it is airstream.
TYPES OF SPEECH SOUNDS
Speech sounds can be grouped into two main types, namely vowels and consonants. 
It is the combination of these two types of sounds that produces words. In other 
words, all words are made up of individual speech sounds. For examples, the word 
pan consists of three individual speech sounds, that is, /p/, /a/, /n/. The sound /a/ 
is a vowel, whereas the sounds /p/ and /n/ are consonants. In the following topics 
we discuss both vowels and consonants focusing on how each is produced in a 
Ghanaian language.
The concept of vowel
The concept vowel refers as a speech sound in which production there is a little or 
no obstruction of the flow of air in the oral cavity. In other words, a speech sound 
which when being produced the air is not obstructed or it is minimally obstructed 
in the oral cavity is referred to as a vowel. Since in their production there is no 
or very little obstruction of airflow, vowels are comparatively heard louder when 
they are produced. Vowels are very important part of words. There cannot be a 
word without a vowel or vowel-like sound. This important role vowel plays in a 
word will later on in your second year be discussed when we are talking about the 
syllable.
Description of vowels
Dear learner, in describing vowels of a Ghanaian language, there are certain 
properties we use. These properties are often termed parametres. Parametres 
simply refer to the characteristics that a vowel possesses. The main parametres 
used in describing vowels are the tongue height, lip posture, and part of the tongue 
4
SECTION 1 SOUNDS OF THE LANGUAGE
used during the production of the vowel sound. In addition to the three, there 
is a fourth parameter called advancement of the tongue root in some Ghanaian 
languages such as Akan. Let us begin the discussions of these parametres.
Lip position/posture:
The parametre lip posture is used to determine the position your lips assume when 
you are producing a vowel. So, at this level, the lips assume two main postures 
or positions, namely rounded or unrounded. That is, whether the lips are rounded 
or they are not rounded when a vowel sound is being produced. Based on this 
posture of the lips, we can divide vowels of a Ghanaian language into two, namely 
‘rounded’ and ‘spread/unrounded.’ Some examples of rounded vowels are /u, 
o, ɔ/. examples of unrounded vowels, on the other hand, are /i, e, a/.
Activity
At this point, produce rounded and unrounded/spread vowels of your Ghanaian 
language of study.
Tongue height/Height of the tongue:
This refers to the position of the tongue in reference to the root of the mouth when 
producing vowel sounds. It is assumed that when we are producing vowels, the 
mouth opens when we drop the jaw. This can be high, mid, or low. When we 
drop our jaws to the lowest possible position, the vowels produced in this way are 
referred to as low vowels. Examples of low vowel is /a/, and in some Ghanaian 
languages [æ]. When we open our mouth wide enough but not as low as when 
producing low vowels, then the vowels we produced are termed mid vowels. 
Some examples of mid vowels in a Ghanaian language are /e, o/. In producing 
high vowels, on the other hand, the mouth is significantly opened but not as wide 
as mid vowels, thereby allowing enough air to flow through the oral cavity. Some 
examples of high vowels in a Ghanaian language are /i, u/.
Activity
Begin practicing the production of vowels in your language of study focusing

5
SECTION 1 SOUNDS OF THE LANGUAGE
Part of the tongue:
This parametre refers to the area of the tongue where the vowel sound is produced. 
It is assumed that when we are producing vowels, some parts of the tongue 
move. We cannot easily feel this movement though. Three parts of the tongue 
are assumed to be involved when a vowel sounds is being produced. These parts 
are the front part, middle part, and back part. Based on that, the parametre gives 
us three classes of vowels, namely front, mid, and back vowels. In producing 
front vowels, it is the front part of the tongue that moves. Some examples of front 
vowels of a Ghanaian language are /i, e, ɛ/. For the production of mid vowels, 
the middle of the tongue is assumed to move. Therefore, the following vowel is 
an example of a mid-vowel: /a/. For back vowels, on the other hand, as the name 
suggests, it is the back of the tongue that is involved in their production. Some 
examples of back vowels of a Ghanaian language are: /u, o, ɔ/.
Activity
Practice how to produce vowels of your language of study with focus on the 
part of the tongue.
Having finished discussing the main parametres we use in describing vowels of 
a Ghanaian language, there is a fourth parametre as mentioned earlier in this 
sub-strand which is not common among Ghanaian languages. This parametre is 
advancement of the tongue.
Advancement of the tongue root (ATR): (Please, discuss only if applicable in 
your language) This parametre, which is prominent in a few Ghanaian languages 
including Akan, Dagbani, etc. It is used to determine the position the tongue root 
assumes when a vowel is being produced. By this parametre, we try to find out 
if there is tension or pressure on the tongue or not during production of vowels. 
When a vowel is produced with pressure on the tongue thereby causing the tongue 
root to draw back, we say that vowel is produced with Advanced Tongue Root 
(ATR) i.e. (+ATR) vowels. When vowels are produced with the tongue root in its 
natural neutral position, we label those vowels are Unadvanced Tongue Root i.e. 
(-ATR) vowels. Some examples of (+ATR) vowels are: /i, e, u, o/, and examples 
of (-ATR) vowels are /ɪ, ɛ, ɔ/.

Having discussed the nature of vowel sounds and the parametres used in

The concept of consonant
As was mentioned earlier in the section, consonant is another type of speech sounds 
apart from vowel. The concept consonant refers to a speech sound in which during 
production the breath, which we have termed airflow, is at least obstructed. Based 
on this explanation, we can contrast vowel and consonant by saying that while in 
the production of vowel there is very minimal or no obstruction of airflow, there 
is significant obstruction of airflow when producing consonants. We combined 
vowels and consonants form a word.

Consonant Distribution
The concept consonant distribution simply refers to the position in a word where 
a consonant can occur in a particular Ghanaian language. A consonant that 
occurs at the beginning of a word is referred to as word initial consonant. When a 
consonant occurs at the middle of a word, we refer to it as word medial consonant. 
When a consonant occurs at the end of a word, we refer to refer to it as word final 
consonant. Let us note that some consonants can occur in all positions of a word. 
For example, in some Ghanaian languages, the consonant /m/ can occur in the 
three positions in a word.

INTRODUCTION
This section discusses identification of key ideas in texts and discourse. It 
always gives information on specific ideas or knowledge to the reader or hearer. 
The information given may come from all perspectives such as education, 
industrialisation, mining among others. It may also indicate some cultural values 
such as respect, tolerance and patience. Identifying key ideas gives you a better 
understanding of the discourse. It also enhances your critical thinking skills and 
interpretation abilities. There are types of reading techniques namely skimming 
and scanning and the application of any of the type enables you to get the right 
information demanded at any time. Knowledge of the types is therefore essential 
in our everyday life. The concept of oral interpretation will also be discussed. We 
shall discuss the skills needed for effective interpretation. Interpretation plays 
important roles in facilitating communication across language barriers.
AT the end of this section you should be able to:
• Identify key ideas from appropriate discourse. E.g., cultural values 
(respect, kindness, tolerance and others), education, child trafficking, 
environment, industrialisation in Ghana, mining, GESI etc.,
• Discuss ideas and relevant opinions from selected discourse. E.g., 
cultural values (respect, kindness, tolerance and others), education, 
child trafficking, environment, industrialisation in Ghana, mining, GESI, 
STEM, etc.

of the key ideas may center on cultural values such as respect, kindness,

WHAT IS DISCOURSE

Reading
At the end of the sub-strand you should be able to:
1. Discuss skimming using preview, overview and review.
2. Discuss scanning using the strategies (e.g., movement of eyes or finger, 
locating words and phrases)
3. Apply skimming and scanning to extract information or ideas from texts
Key ideas
 Skimming is going through a text rapidly to get the general information 
in the text while scanning involves looking for a specific information in 
a text. Scanning is a process of reading in which your eyes quickly run 
through a piece of text to find a piece of relevant information. Scanning 
and skimming are two different concepts of reading.
TYPES OF READING
There are types of reading skill or technique namely skimming, scanning, 
intensive reading and extensive reading. Dear learner, in this lesson you shall 
learn skimming and scanning techniques of reading.
Skimming
Skimming is a reading technique used to quickly identify the main ideas or key 
points in a text. It is the action of reading something quickly so as to note only the 
important points. Basically, skimming is reading rapidly in order to get a general 
overview of the material read. It is used to find specific facts in texts. It involves 
glancing over the material, focusing on headings, subheadings, bold text and key 
phrases to get a general understanding of the content. Skimming is useful when; 
time is limited, looking for specific information, you want to get an overview 
8
SECTION 2 SHARING IDEAS AND ORAL INTERPRETATION
before reading in-depth and you are dealing with a large amount of text. Below 
are the skimming types.
Preview: An opportunity to view something before it is acquired or becomes 
generally available. Preview is done in an effort to learn about the ideas presented 
and the structure of their development.
Overview: Used to sample the reading material more thoroughly. A general review 
or summary of a subject.
Review: The review is done to re-familiarise yourself with the material you have 
previously read thoroughly or skimmed. A formal assessment of something with 
the intention of instituting a change if necessary.
Learner, in skimming, you can follow these steps
- Read the title
- Read the headings and sub-headings as well as topic sentences in each 
paragraph
- Look for important information such as date, names and unusual words.
- Read the conclusion

In summary you have learnt skimming and the steps as well as the types of 
skimming which you can apply. Dear learner, let us examine what is scanning.
Scanning
Scanning is reading rapidly in order to find facts without reading everything. 
Scanning helps you locate a particular fact while skimming tells you what general 
information is within a section.
Scanning involves looking for a specific information in a text. It can also be said 
to be a process of reading in which your eyes quickly run through a piece of text 
to find a piece of relevant information. In scanning the reader looks for a piece 
of specific information. An example of scanning is searching for the meaning 
of a word in a dictionary. Scanning helps the reader to locate particular facts in 
an entire text quickly. Students often use scanning when solving their reading 
comprehension questions.
It is important to know the purpose for scanning. You should know what you are 
searching for, eg title of a book, a website, a reference material, a particular word 
or phrase and a particular story you want to read etc. You should know how the

material is structures either alphabetically, non-alphabetically, chronologically, 
by category, by titles /headings, by textual sense, by numbers among others.
Scanning helps a learner to read more and to develop love for reading.
When to scan
1. Scan before reading
2. Scan a number of questions to identify the one which you are most 
comfortable answering
3. When searching for particular information such as date, keywords etc.
The following shows how to do scanning after getting overview of a text and 
identifying the sections of the text you want to read.
1. Start scanning the text by moving your eyes and fingers quickly over it
2. When you have identified the information, word or the phrase you are 
searching for, read the information surrounding the word carefully
3. When you identified the information that requires attention, you read it 
thoroughly slowly.

Oral Interpretation and translation
At the end of the sub-strand, you should be able to:
 Discuss oral interpretation focusing on effective listening, encoding and 
decoding.
Key Ideas
 Oral interpretation is reframing the meaning of a speech most often orally 
into another language. The original language is the source language 
and the language in which it is rendered is the target language. In oral 
interpretation you must note the cultural differences and be accurate in 
giving the meaning of what you are to render in the language orally.
CONTENT
Interpretation is listening to a message in one language and rendering it orally 
in another language maintaining the original meaning, tone and context. It 
is the stylistic representation of a creative work or dramatic role. It is the act 
of explaining, reframing, or otherwise showing your own understanding of 
something. In interpretation you first have to understand the text or the piece 
given to you and then explain in your own words. In broader terms it is rendering 
a spoken or signed message into another spoken or signed language preserving 
the register and meaning of the source language content.
Dear learner, it must be noted that before you can do any interpretation, you must 
be well versed in the source and target language. Interpretation can be performed 
either simultaneously or consecutively between users of different languages.
Dear learner, know that in interpreting you do not embellish or over-exaggerate. 
State the ideas clearly. In interpreting you need to listen carefully, decode and 
encode as they serve as the process of communication and interpreting.

‘Encoding’ Eji gbɛjianɔtoo ni akɛtsakeɔ adafitswaa loo sane hiɛ kɛmajeɔ 
shweshweeshwe ni tsakemɔ ko baa mli. Ekɔɔ sane mli tsɔɔmɔ kɛ shishinumɔ 
shishi. Ekɔɔ nikanemɔ, wolo majemɔ he sane ni etsiɔ wiemɔkulibii, sanefa kɛ 
sanemuu ta.
‘Decoding’ Enɛ ji gbɛjianɔtoo ni akɛtsakeɔ niŋmaa ko hiɛ, ni gbalaa niŋmaa ko 
mli ni anuɔ shishi Enɛ haa mɛi nuɔ shishi ni amɛgbalaa mli. Enɛ ji gbɛ nɔ ni 
toibolɔi tsɔɔ nɔ kɛnuɔ loo kɛboɔ sane ko mli haa.
You need to know the following to do oral interpretation
1. Listen attentively.
2. You should be fluent in both languages.
3. Keep to the meaning of the test or speech in the original language.
4. Keep pace with the dialogue.
Dear learner, decoding is like sending message and encoding is similar to receiving 
and understanding the message.

Nitsumɔhei: Kɔlebu Helatsamɔhe, Jubilee House, University of Ghana, k.n.k.n..
Faa: Pra, Seŋtse, Densu, Ankobra, Kɔɔle, Ŋshɔ k.n.k.n..
Kwaamaŋgbɛi
Eji gbɛi ni akɛhaa nibii (gbɔmɔ, kooloo, atade, dade, susumɔ, gɔŋ, shika sikli, 
k.n.k.n.), nɔ ko ni jeee kɔsuaŋgbɛi ni. Enɛmɛi lɛ akɛ niŋmaa okadi agbo ejeee 
shishi bɛja eeeje sanemuu shishi. Nɔkwɛmɔnibii komɛi nɛ; niŋmaatso, shia, tsu, 
loo, ŋshɔ, tɔ, kpatashi, nikasemɔtsu mli.
Kɔɔyɔɔ/gbɛisisa
Enɛmɛi ji wiemɔkulibii ni damɔɔ shi haa susumɔi loo yiŋtoi, henumɔi loo nibii 
ni wɔnyɛɛɛ wɔna kɛ wɔhiŋmɛi shi amɛyɛ gbɛi. Nɔkwɛmɔnii; miishɛɛ, ŋkɔmɔ, 
suɔmɔ, mligbigblimɔ, anɔkwa, k.n.k.n.
4
SECTION 3 SANEMUU TSƐRƐMƆ
Gbɛi ni anyɛɔ ataa he
Enɛmɛi ji nibii ni yɔɔ jeŋ ni anaa ni anyɛɔ ataa he. Eji nibii ni adesa jwɛŋmɔi 
enumɔ lɛ eko kɛ nyɛɔ nuɔ he, taa he, naa, fuɔ kɛ saa naa. Nɔkwɛmɔnii: tɛ, okpɔlɔ, 
saatso, nu, kɔɔyɔɔ, su, saŋku, mi, shwuɔ, k.n.k.n.
Nitsumɔ 1
Jaramɔ gbɛiwiemɔi nɛɛ amli owo kɔsuaŋgbɛi, kwaamaŋgbɛi, kɔɔyɔŋ/gbɛisisa 
kɛ gbɛi ni anyɛɔ ataa he. Tsɔɔmɔ nɔ ni ha ofeɔ nakai yiŋtoi lɛ.
i. Tsɔɔlɔ
ii. Okpɔlɔ
iii. Suɔmɔ
iv. Araba
v. Abu
vi. Miishɛɛ
vii. Ekomefeemɔ
viii. Sɛi
ix. Kɔɔyɔɔ
x. Tɛ
Nitsumɔ 2
i. Yɛ kui amli lɛ, nyɛŋmalaa gbɛiwiemɔi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sanekuku nɛɛ mli.
ii. Buamɔ gbɛiwiemɔi nɛɛ anaa owo kui nɛɛ ashishi. Gbɛi ni anyɛɔ ataa 
he Kwaamaŋgbɛi Kɔsuaŋgbɛi kɔɔyɔɔŋgbɛi
iii. Okɛ nɔkwɛmɔnii ni ona lɛ awo sanemuji amli. N.k. Mimaŋ lɛ edaaa.
Yitso: Miikpa shi yɛ mimaŋ jara lɛ mli.
Yɛ mimaŋ lɛ mli lɛ, jara ko yɛ jɛmɛ ni be fɛɛ be lɛ nifeemɔi miiya nɔ waa. Eji 
miishɛɛ he ko ni mɛi buaa amɛhe naa kɛhɔɔ nii ni aheɔ nibii srɔtoi yɛ jɛmɛ. 
Kɛjɛ aduawai fɛfɛji kɛ yeli baji kɛyashi mamai, tsobii kɛ shiaŋ nibii, ni nɔ fɛɛ 
nɔ ni otaoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ.

SECTION 3 SANEMUU TSƐRƐMƆ
Daa otsi naagbee lɛ, mikɛ miweku lɛ yaa ni wɔyaheɔ nibii ni wɔtaoɔ lɛ yɛ 
jɛmɛ. Kɛji wɔbɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, wɔnuɔ sanegbaa ni miitsɔɔ nibii lɛ ajara kɛ mɛi 
ananeshi gbɛɛmɔ kɛmiiho.
Nɔ ni mihiŋmɛi gba nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ji aduawai ni ato fɛfɛo kɛ yeli baji ni jwere 
apaawa nɔ. Akutu kɛ ŋɔɔmɔŋɔɔmɔ, akwadu ni etsu hɛluu kɛ akpakpa fɛfɛji 
Ŋma ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli, ni eyi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ha mikɛ miishɛɛ kɔlɔ nibii 
ni mitaoɔ mahe lɛ.
Wɔtsa nɔ kɛshɛ shwapoi ni eto srɛnɛɛ ni miihɔɔ mama kɛ ehe nibii lɛ amli. 
Shɛɛtii kɛ sikɛɛti fɛfɛji kɛ jwinei fɛfɛji lɛ gbala mijwɛŋmɔ.Mibɔi nibii lɛ 
amligbɛlɛmɔ akɛ mana nɔ ko ni baasa mi mafata minibii ni mihe momo lɛ he 
lo.
Be ni wɔtsa nɔ kɛtee hiɛ yɛ jara lɛ nɔ lɛ, wɔyashɛ shwapoi komɛi ni miihɔɔ 
tsobii, jwinei ni jara waaa. Kɛjɛ fiifii kɛ ŋwɛi atadei fɛfɛji kɛyashi miishɛɛ 
shwɛmɔ tsobii, gbekɛ fɛɛ gbekɛ na nɔ ko ni baaha lɛ miishɛɛ.Mihiŋmɛi nyɛɛɛ 
aho he kɛkɛ akɛ ja miŋmɔ hɛoo ko be ni mina miishɛɛ ni yɔɔ gbekɛbii lɛ ahiɛ 
be mli ni amɛna tsobii ni jwere shi lɛ.
Naagbee lɛ, wɔyashɛ jara lɛ he ni ahɔɔ shiaŋ nibii yɛ lɛ. Biɛ lɛ wɔna kpatashi 
nibii, falefalefeemɔ nibii kɛyashi tsu mli saamɔ nibii. Mimami hala nibii lɛ 
amli jogbaŋŋ kɛtao nibii ni he hiaa wɔ lɛ be mli ni wɔwa kɛtere baagii lɛ.
Wɔbatsa nɔ kɛ gbɛiwiemɔ henɔi lɛ kwɛmɔ.
Gbɛikushao
Amɛ ji gbɛi ni akɛhaa nibii ni abua naa, ku loo efi tɛo. Eeenyɛ efee nibii, kooloi 
loo gbɔmɛi ni abua amɛnaa ekome. Nɔkwɛmɔnii: meelei pii, bɔɔlutswalɔi aku, 
kwayabii, ku, shao, duru, omɔ, sikli, gali, k.n.k.n. Akɔɔ ku lɛ akɛ nɔ kome ni 
akwɛɛɛ mɛi loo nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afalɛ akɛ mɛi pii koni akɛfee gbɛiwiemɔ lɛ pii.
Nitsumɔ 3
Yɛ mɛi enyɔ aku mli lɛ, mɔ fɛɛ mɔ aha wiemɔkulibii enumɔ yɛ gbɛikushao 
shishi.
Okɛ onaanyo agba ohetoo ni oha lɛ he sane.
Kwɛmɔ sanemuji ni baa nɛɛ koni otsɔɔ emli nɔ ni abaanyɛ akane kɛ nɔ ni 
anyɛɛɛ akane gbɛiwiemɔi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.
- Wɔ nyɔ gbekɛbii lɛ anɔ be ni akpa gbi lɛ mli shwɛmɔ kɛ tɔlɛ lɛ.

SECTION 3 SANEMUU TSƐRƐMƆ
MƐNI JI SUTSƆƆLƆI/KADILƆI?
Yɛ nyɛ kui amli lɛ, nyɛ kɛ wiemɔkulibii etɛ atsɔɔ wiemɔi ni baa nɛɛ anaa.
- Oklasi lɛ.
- Onaanyo kpakpa lɛ.
- Okpɔlɔ lɛ.
- Shihilɛ ni yɔɔ sukuu lɛ mli
Nilee ni yɔɔ kadilɔi/sutsɔɔlɔi amli miitsɔɔ wiemɔkulibii ni kadiɔ gbɛiwiemɔ ko. 
Sutsɔɔlɔi/kadilɔi miitsɔɔ wiemɔkulibii ni tsɔɔ nɔ ko pɔtɛɛ yɛ mɔ ko loo nɔ ko he. 
Nɔkwɛmɔ nibii; diŋ, tsuru, kpitio, kakadaŋŋ, agbo, bibioo, k.n k.n. Nɔkwɛmɔ 
nibii ni baa nɛɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni akɛ sutsɔɔlɔi/kadilɔi etsu nii yɛ sanemuu mli.
i. Misumɔɔ shia memeji.
ii. Gbekɛnuu lɛ kwɔ asaŋ eta loo.
iii. Aku he yɛ oya fe enyɛmi nuu lɛ.
Yɛ (i) lɛ, wiemɔ “momo” lɛ miisusu shia he nɔ ni wielɔ lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ he. Yɛ (ii) lɛ, 
wiemɔkulibii kwɔ kɛ eta loo miitsɔɔ hewalɛnamɔ mli ni gbekɛ nuu lɛ yɔɔ. Yɛ (iii) 
lɛ mli lɛ, wiemɔkulibii oya fe kɛ nibii enyɔ miito he, Aku kɛ enyɛmi nuu lɛ he oya 
yɛ nɔ ko feemɔ mli.
Kadilɔ/sutsɔɔlɔ henɔi
Ayɛ kadilɔ/sutsɔɔlɔ henɔi, otii ni yɔɔ mli ni wɔbaakwɛ lɛ ji;
- Mɔsɛɛgbɛ tsɔɔlɔ
- Kadilɔ
- Yifalɛ
Mɔsɛɛgbɛ tsɔɔlɔ
Yɛ enɛ mli lɛ, akɛ sɛɛgbɛtsɔɔlɔ najiaŋgbɛi ‘enɛ, no, enɛmɛi amɛ/nomɛi’tsuɔ nii 
akɛ kadilɔi ejaakɛ amɛtsɔɔ mɔ/nɔ ni amɛwieɔ ehe lɛ sɛɛgbɛ fitsofitso kɛkadiɔ 
gbɛiwiemɔ lɛ. Nɔkwɛmɔ nibii;
a. Nɛkɛ tsɔne nɛɛ yɛ ehee.
b. Nakai tsui lɛ, yoo lɛ nɔ ni.
c. Nɛkɛ tsu nɛɛ, mitsɛ ataa nɔ ni.
d. Aku miihe nɛkɛ tsui nɛɛ.
10
SECTION 3 SANEMUU TSƐRƐMƆ
Nii kɛ nii ahetoo kadilɔ
Akɛ susuɔ nibii loo mɛi enyɔ ni anaa srɔtoi ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ. Nomɛi ji; bibioo, agbo, 
grɔŋŋ, kpitioo, oya fe.
a. Niyenii nɛɛ jara waaa fe minɔ lɛ.
b. Ama he yɛ oya fe Kofi.
c. Lɔle yɛŋ lɛ joɔ foi fe lɔle tsuru lɛ.
d. Oshika lɛ shɛɛɛ minɔ lɛ.
Kadilɔ ni tsɔɔ Yifalɛ
Kadilɔi/sutsɔɔlɔi nɛɛ tswaa yifalɛ he adafi. Yifalɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ kadilɔ. Nɔkwɛmɔ 
nibii;
a. Mihe omɔ ko.
b. Ehoo wɔji enyɔ.
c. Eetao sikli fioo.
d. Woji babaoo yɛ mideka lɛ mli.
Mɔhewiemɔ kadilɔ (qualifier)
Eji wiemɔ ni tsɔɔ mɔ ko subaŋ, nifeemɔ loo jebɔ ko mli ni eyɔɔ. Amɛji kadilɔi ni 
tsɔɔ su ko mli ni gbɛiwiemɔ lɛ yɔɔ ni haa anaa mɔ he ni awieɔ lɛ. Kadilɔi titri fɛɛ 
hiɔ henɔ nɛɛ shishi. Kwɛmɔ henɔi ni baa nɛɛ:
a. Tsɔne lɛ egbɔ.
b. Miyɛ wolo bibioo ko..
c. Niyenii lɛ yɛ akɔnɔ.
d. Mina bɔɔsu agbo ko.
Nitsumɔ
1. Kuu sɛɛ oyakwɛ wiemɔkulibii ni wɔna yɛ shishijee nikasemɔi lɛ amli lɛ. 
Too amɛ owo (Mɔ wiemɔ kadilɔ (demonstrative): Nakai, nɛkɛ, nomɛi 
kɛ enɛmɛi, ekɔmɔ damɔɔ kɛji eewie mɔ kome loo mɛi pii ahe, ditɛmina 
loo gbɛiwiemɔ sɛɛgbɛ tsɔɔlɔ, yifalɛ kɛ (kadilɔi) ashishi. Ha nɔkwɛmɔnii 
krokomɛi ofata nɔ ni aha lɛ he.
2. Kanemɔ sane ni baa nɛɛ koni ohala kadilɔi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Too amɛ owo 
ditɛmina loo gbɛiwiemɔ sɛɛgbɛ tsɔɔlɔ, kɛ yifalɛ shishi koni okɛ klasi lɛ 
asusu he.
11
SECTION 3 SANEMUU TSƐRƐMƆ
Be ni wuɔ gbɛɛ shii etɛ nakai leebi lɛ, mɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Alata akrowa lɛ naa ekpe 
shi yɛ maŋtsɛwe lɛ. Maŋtsɛwe bii lɛ fɛɛ ewula amɛhe kɛ atade yɛŋ. Amɛkɛ 
kladuku efimɔ amɛyitsei ni amɛnyiɛ nane folo.
Amɛkpe kɛmiiye maŋtsɛ lɛ he odase. Kusum tsɔɔ akɛ afii babaoo ni eho lɛ, 
maŋtsɛ lɛ tsɛmɛi asisai lɛ ye bua akrowa lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ewa amɛ gbi ko shwane 
be mli ni akrowa lɛ ŋmɔji fɛɛ esha. Hɔmɔ ba akrowa lɛŋ. Hɔmɔ ba ni awerɛho 
mɔmɔ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ yɛ akrowa lɛŋ.
Maŋtsɛ lɛ tsɛmɛi ni ye bua akrowa lɛ mli bii fɛɛ kɛ niyenii babaoo. Akrowaŋbii 
lɛ tsɔ enɛ nɔ kɛwo lɛ maŋtsɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛhiɛsɔlɛ. Daa afi lɛ amɛbɔleɔ kutuu 
kɛkaiɔ nibii kpakpai ni etsɛmɛi efee kɛho lɛ.
Taakɛ onaa yɛ shishi nɔkwɛmɔnii lɛ amli lɛ abaanyɛ akɛ gbɛiwiemɔ sɛɛgbɛ tsɔɔlɔ 
atsu nii yɛ gbɛiwiemɔ lɛ sɛɛ kɛji ekɛ feemɔwiemɔ tsa.
a. Shia lɛ yɛ fɛo.
b. Watsi ni oŋmɔ lɛ yɛ fɛo
c. Maŋoi ni oyeɔ lɛ yɛ akɔnɔ.
d. Tso ni mina lɛ kwɔ grɔŋŋ.
Obaanyɛ okɛ nɛkɛ kadilɔi nɛɛ atsu nii kɛji enyiɛ gbɛiwiemɔ sɛɛ. Yɛ blɔfo mli lɛ 
amɛbaa dani gbɛiwiemɔ ni amɛkadiɔ lɛ baa, shi yɛ Ga wiemɔ lɛ mli lɛ amɛbaa yɛ 
gbɛiwiemɔ ni amɛkadiɔ lɛ sɛɛ taakɛ onaa yɛ nɔkwɛmɔ nibii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛ:
a. Enɛ lɛ shia fɛfɛo ni.
b. Mina tso grɔŋŋ ko.
c. Mimami he watsi fɛfɛo ko eha mi.
d. Miyeɔ maŋoi fɛfɛji daa.
12
SANEBIMƆ EKOŊŊ
1. Jaramɔ sutsɔɔlɔi/kadilɔi ni baa nɛɛ amli owo henɔi lɛ ashishi. Ku fɛɛ ku 
atsɔɔ nɔ hewɔ ni amɛjara mli nakai lɛ.
i. fɛfɛo
ii. kakadaŋŋ
iii. ŋɔɔmɔŋɔɔmɔ
iv. akɔnɔ
v. fa
vi. tsuru
vii. yitsoŋwalɛ
viii. akase
ix. hulutsoo
x. nakai
xi. nɛkɛ
xii. etɛ
xiii. eko
2. Kanemɔ sane ni baa nɛɛ koni oha sanebimɔi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ahetoi.

Feemɔ klalo akɛ okɛ oklasibii lɛ baagba oyiŋtoo lɛ he sane.
Feemɔwiemɔ tsɔɔ nifeemɔ ko ni yɔɔ sanemuu mli. Wiemɔkulibii kɛ sanekukuji 
hu fata feemɔwiemɔi ahe ni etsɔɔ bɔ ni nɔ ko tee nɔ ha (nu nɔ ko he, eda, nu nɔ ko

Feemɔwiemɔ nyɛɔ ehiɔ sane mli kɛ helɔ loo helɔ fataaa he. Helɔi ni onaa ni baa 
yɛ feemɔwiemɔ sɛɛ lɛ wɔtsɛɔ lɛ akɛ helɔ yigbelɔ.. Anyɛɔ adamɔɔ feemɔwiemɔ 
yigbelɔi anɔ kɛbuaa feemɔwiemɔi anaa awoɔ kui srɔtoi etɛ amli (nɔ ni eŋɔɔɔ

Feemɔwiemɔ ni ŋɔɔ yigbelɔ
Feemɔwiemɔi ni ŋɔɔ yigbelɔ baa kɛ helɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ yɛ sanemuu lɛ mli. Nɔkwɛmɔ 
nibii komɛi nɛ: hoo, nu, kudɔ, yɛ, to eat, ŋma, yi, k.n.k.n. Nɔkwɛmɔ nibii:

3. Kofi kɛ Adwoa ye jɔlɔfu .
4. Gbekɛ ko bu fai.
5. Gbɛfalɔi lɛ kɔ tsɔne lɛ.
Feeemɔwiemɔ ni akpa lɛ afa lɛ fɛɛ lɛ feemɔwiemɔi ni ŋɔɔ yigbelɔ ni. Yigbelɔi 
kɛ helɔi lɛ fɛɛ baa yɛ feemɔwiemɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔkwɛmɔnɔ. Yɛ (1) lɛ mli lɛ, helɔ lɛ ji

Mɛni ji Mligbalalɔ?
Kwɛmɔ mfoniri ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Mɛni amɛfeɔ lɛ? Mɛɛ beiaŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni? 
Nɛgbɛ nifeemɔ lɛ yaa nɔ yɛ? Mɛni hewɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ yaa nɔ?
Mligbalalɔi ji wiemɔkulibii loo sanekukuji ni haa anuɔ feemɔwiemɔ ko shishi 
jogbaŋŋ yɛ sanemuu ko mli. Mligbalalɔi komɛi susuɔ mligbalalɔi krokomɛi 
amɛtsɔɔ. Susumɔ bɔ ni onyiɛ kɛba sukuu ŋmɛnɛ he, ani onyiɛ blɛoo, waa loo 
ojo foi? Eko lɛ onyiɛ oyayaayai kɛtee sukuu. Wiemɔkuli oyayaayai miitsɔɔ bɔ 
ni onyiɛ kɛtee sukuu, hewɔ lɛ mligbalalɔ ni. Adamɔɔ bɔ ni mligbalalɔi tsakeɔ 
feemɔwiemɔ shishinumɔ nɔ kɛjaraa amɛmli. Henɔi amli ni ajaraa amɛ awoɔ lɛ ji: 
gbɛ nɔ ni atsɔ afee nɔ ko, he ni nɔ ko tee nɔ yɛ, be ni nɔ ko tee nɔ, shii abɔ ni afee 
nɔ ko, henumɔ loo bɔ ni nɔ ko tee nɔ ha, nɔ hewɔ ni afee nɔ ko.
Mligbalalɔ ni miitsɔɔ gbɛ nɔ ni atsɔ afee nɔ ko:
Mligbalalɔ nɛɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni loo gbɛ nɔ ni atsɔ  afee nɔ ko loo nifeemɔ lɛ tee nɔ.

Mlijaa A: Feemɔwiemɔ
1. Mɛɛ srɔto ka feemɔwiemɔ ni tsɔɔ nɔ ko feemɔ kɛ feemɔwiemɔ ni tsɔɔ

Be mli ni misha shi kɛtee ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ, mijo foi kɛtu kɛyanina ŋshɔ ke 
lɛ. Hulu ni gbɛ eda aŋ hatoo kɛ bɔi mi shaa lɛ ha miyɔse akɛ miyɛ wala 
mli. Mikɛ selemɔ kɛ shwɛmɔ gbɛ nu kɛ shwɛ yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli. Ŋshɔnaa 
loofɔji lɛ fliki kɛ yaafo kɛho. Mikɛ ŋshɔnaa shia shɔ tsui strɔtoi kɛ mɔɔ 
hu ni mikɛ ŋshɔnaa tɛ saa fɛɛ he fɛfɛo. Be ni shɛɔ jenamɔ lɛ, mikpa shi 
kɛnyiɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa kɛ miitao nibii ni eteetee yɛ ŋshɔnaa shia lɛ mli bɔ ni 
manyɛ makai nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni etee nɔ.
Jaramɔ feemɔwiemɔi ni oyɔse yɛ sane ni okane lɛ mli kɛwo feemɔwiemɔ 
henɔi etɛ ni okase lɛ mli.
Mlijaa B: Mligbalalɔi
1. Ŋmalamɔ nibii komɛi ni ofɔɔ feemɔ daa gbi koni ogba otsɔɔ onaanyo ko 
nɔ hewɔ, bei amli, he ni kɛ he ni ofɔɔ nɛkɛ nifeemɔ nɛɛ feemɔ yɛ.
2. Ŋmalamɔ mligbalalɔi fɛɛ ni onaanyo lɛ kɛtsɔ nii yɛ amɛsusumɔi ahe ko 
ni ojara mli.
3. Ŋmaa sane ni naa shɛɔ wiemɔkulibii nyɔŋmai enumɔ ni kɔɔ jeŋ kɛ mɛi 
ni okɛyɔɔ lɛ he. Kɛ hooo kwraa lɛ, okɛ mligbalalɔi nyɔŋma awo osane 
lɛ mli.

WIEMƆ KƐ NITSUMƆ
Ga wiemɔ lɛ ŋmaa mli mlai
HIƐGBELEMƆ
Mlijaa nɛɛ baatsɔɔ mlai ni yɔɔ Ga wiemɔ lɛ ŋmaa mli. Gbɛjianɔtoi nɛɛ baagba 
mlai ni yɔɔ gbɛiwiemɔi, feemɔwiemɔi, najiaŋgbɛi kɛ kadilɔi/sutsɔɔlɔi lɛ ahe 
sane.. Wɔbaakwɛ mlai ni yɔɔ gbɛiwiemɔi ahe klɛŋklɛŋ, ni najiaŋgbɛi baanyiɛ sɛɛ, 
no sɛɛ lɛ kadilɔi/sutsɔɔlɔi, kɛkɛ lɛ feemɔwiemɔi kɛ mligbalalɔi. Enɛ haa bo nilee 
yɛ mlai kɛ bɔ ni akɛ gbɛiwiemɔi, najiaŋgbɛi, kadilɔi/sutsɔɔlɔi, feemɔwiemɔi kɛ 
mligbalalɔi tsuɔ nii ahaa yɛ Ga wiemɔ ni okaseɔ lɛ mli. Obaanyɛ okɛ mlai lɛ ato 
wiemɔi krokomɛi tamɔ Blɔfo wiemɔ lɛ he.
Nikasemɔ lɛ mli Otii
1. Okɛ mlai ni yɔɔ gbɛiwiemɔi kɛ najiaŋgbɛi ahe aŋmalaa sanemuji/ 
wiemɔmuji.
2. Okɛ mlai ni yɔɔ kadilɔi kɛ sutsɔɔlɔi ahe aŋmalaa sanemuji.
3. Okɛ mlai ni yɔɔ feemɔwiemɔi kɛ mligbalalɔi ahe aŋmalaa sanemuji.
Susumɔ Otii
• Gbɛiwiemɔi damɔɔ shi akɛ feelɔi (subjects), feelɔ (direct) kɛ helɔ/nɔnalɔ
• Najiaŋgbɛi hu damɔɔ shi akɛ feelɔ aloo nɔnalɔ loo helɔ yɛ saneŋmaa mli.
• Kadilɔi loo sutsɔɔlɔi kadiɔ gbɛiwiemɔi. Yɛ Ga wiemɔ lɛ mli lɛ amɛfɔɔ 
gbɛiwiemɔi ni amɛkadiɔ lɛ asɛɛ nyiɛmɔ..
• Feemɔwiemɔi tsɔɔ nifeemɔi ni yɔɔ sanemuu mli loo be mli ni nifeemɔ lɛ 
tee nɔ. Ga wiemɔ lɛ etsiii feemɔwiemɔi abɔ ni okɛbaatsu nii yɛ sanemuu 
mli naa. Gbɛiwiemɔi kɛ feemɔwiemɔi damɔɔ shi ankroankro yɛ Ga wiemɔ 
lɛ mli, bɛja feemɔwiemɔ ni nyiɛ najiaŋgbɛi sɛɛ, no lɛ aŋmaa amɛ atsaa.
• Mligbalalɔi tsɔɔ bɔ ni nifeemɔ ko tee nɔ ha mli, ni enyɛɔ egbalaa 
mligbalalɔi krokomɛi hu amli etsɔɔ..

GBƐIWIEEMƆI
Wɔkwɛ gbɛiwiemɔi yɛ naagbee mlijaa lɛ mli. Wɔtsɛ gbɛiwiemɔi srɔtoi lɛ ni wɔha 
nɔkwɛmɔ nibii ni wɔgba he sane, kɛ kui amli ni eko fɛɛ eko yɔɔ.
Sanebimɔi ahesusumɔ: Ani okaiɔ gbɛiwiemɔ henɔi lɛ? Ŋmaa owo wolo mli.
Gbɛiwiemɔi ji gbɔmɛi agbɛi, hei, kooloi kɛ nibii. Efɔɔ kaa akɛ sanemuu hiɛɔ 
kɛhooo kwraa lɛ gbɛiwiemɔ kome. Ni efɔɔ kaa akɛ ekɛ ‘lɛ’, nɛ, ni, loo eko loo ko.
Najiaŋgbɛi
Akɛ najiaŋgbɛi lɛ, bo, mi, e, amɛ, wɔ, kɛ ekrokomɛi damɔɔ shi haa gbɛiwiemɔ yɛ 
sanemuu mli. Amɛnyɛɔ amɛdamɔɔ shi akɛ gbɛiwiemɔ sanekuku.
Kaimɔ akɛ: Yɛ Ga wiemɔ lɛ mli lɛ, abɛ najiaŋgbɛi ni damɔɔ shi haa yoo loo nuu 
ankroankro shi wiemɔkuli lɛ damɔɔ shi haa amɛ fɛɛ. Ani nakai ni yɛ owiemɔ ni 
okaseɔ lɛ mli? Okɛ onaanyo asusu he koni nyɛkɛ nyɛsanegbaa lɛ ayahaa tsɔɔlɔ lɛ.
Yɛ nikasemɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ wɔkwɛ niŋmaa mlai ni kɔɔ gbɛiwiemɔi kɛ najiaŋgbɛi 
kɛniŋmaa he.
Nifeemɔ
Nyɛkwɛa sini nɛɛ koni nyɛkɛ nyɛnanemɛi agbaa gbɛiwiemɔi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ 
anitsumɔi ahe sane kɛtsɔɔ nyɛjwɛŋmɔ.

Gbei
Gbei ji kooloi ni ale amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe gbɛi akɛ kooloo naanyo yɛ je lɛŋ he 
fɛɛ he. Anaa amɛ yɛ henɔi kɛ sui srɔtoi amli. Kooloi naji ejwɛ tsɛmɛi ji amɛ, ni 
amɛjɛ klaŋ weku lɛ mli. Be ko ni blema tsɛmɛi lɛ eko ŋɔ klaŋ kɛba shia kɛye abua 
gbɔbimɔ lɛ,amɛbɛŋkɛ gbɔmɛi akui ni amɛsumɔ gbɔmɛi asane. Amɛkase adesai 
ahe nii ni amɛyɔse gbɔmɛi ahenumɔ tamɔ sanesuɔmɔ, awuiyeli kɛ gbeyei, ni amɛ 
hu amɛto he nine pɛpɛɛpɛ.
Gbei nɛɛ yɛ nifuu henumɔ srɔto ko. Amɛnuɔ gbɛɛmɔi ahe kɛyaa shɔŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ. 
Nɔ ni haa gbei ahe baa sɛɛnamɔ jogbaŋŋ ji akɛ anyɛɔ atsɔseɔ amɛ yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi

ni atsɔɔ kɛkuraa wɔhewɔŋ ni emli atse. Bɔ ni wɔkwɛɛɛ loo wɔwaaa 
kɛ kuraaa wɔhewɔŋ lɛ miiha daa gbo kɛ gbiɛnaa lɛ wɔhewɔŋ miifite. 
Nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ; gbɛi gbohii anɔ ni atsɔɔ kɛtsiɔ jwɛi ashwieɔ, jwɛi tsimɔ kɛ 
shwiemɔ, hei ni esaaa ni akɛ rɔbai ashwie k.n k.n. Kɛji akwɛɛɛ ni agu 
subaŋi gbohii nɛɛ lɛ, ebaashɛ be ko lɛ, ebaatɔ yinɔbii ni baa lɛ yɛ nɛkɛ 
subaŋi nɛɛ ahe. Eji mi kɛ bo gbɛnaa akɛ bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni ji lɛ wɔwa kɛfee 
nɔ ni sa kɛwa kɛkura wɔhewɔŋ jogbaŋŋ. Eji wɔgbɛnaa akɛ wɔsusu gbɛi 
anɔ ni wɔbaatsɔ kɛkura shikpɔŋ ni Naa Nyɔŋmɔ kɛha wɔ lɛ. Toigbele

FEEMƆWIEMƆI
Feemɔwiemɔ kɛ mligbalalɔi kɛsanemuu feemɔ yɛ Ga mli kpaa mlai komɛi 
agbɛ kɛnitsumɔ
Mlai nɛɛ kɛnitsumɔ yeɔ buaa kɛŋmalaa saji lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni kanelɔ lɛ nuɔ nɔ ni oŋma 
lɛ shishi kɛ emlijelɛ. Mlai ni kɔɔ niŋmaa he yɛ wiemɔ ko mli lɛ kɛnitsumɔ yeɔ 
buaa ni oŋmaa nii ni shishinumɔ lɛ feɔ faŋŋ yɛ Ga wiemɔ lɛ mli
Dani wɔbaakwɛ mlai lɛ nyɛhaa wɔkaia nɔ ni feemɔwiemɔi ji. Naa nɔkwɛmɔ nibii 
komɛi. Feemɔwiemɔi ji wiemɔkulibii ni adiki mli lɛ.
1. Okwaafonyo lɛ huɔ koo kɛji humɔ bei shɛ.
2. Gbekɛbii lɛ nyiɛɔ kɛyaa sukuu daa Sohaa.
3. Wɔhuruɔ daa leebi kɛgbɔleɔ wɔkpɔiaŋ.
Feemɔwiemɔ ji wiemɔ ni tsɔɔ nifeemɔ ko, be ni nɔ ko tee nɔ loo ba lɛ ha. 
Feemɔwiemɔ ji nɔnalɔ loo helɔ lɛ yitso (predicate) yɛ sanemuu mli.
Mlai ni tsɔɔ feemɔwiemɔ kɛnitsumɔ yɛ sanemuu mli.
Wiemɔi titri yɛ mlai srɔtoi ni kuraa feemɔwiemɔi kɛnitsumɔ. Mlai lɛ ekomɛi nɛ:
1. Feemɔwiemɔi tsɔɔ nɔ ni feelɔ lɛ feɔ yɛ sanemuu lɛ mli. Nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ: Gbee 
lɛ bolɔɔ yɛ agbo lɛ naa daa.
 Yɛ biɛ lɛ feemɔwiemɔ 'bolɔɔ' lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ni feelɔ ‘gbee’ lɛ feɔ yɛ agbo lɛ naa.
a. Gbekɛbii lɛ taa okɔokpe kɛyaa sukuu daa leebi
 Feemɔwiemɔ taa lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ni feelɔ (kaselɔ) lɛ feɔ.
2. Feemɔwiemɔi tsɔɔ be ni feelɔ lɛ kɛfee nɔ ko. Nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ:
 Kojo na miishɛɛ be ni agbe kaa lɛ naa lɛ.
 Biɛ lɛ, feemɔwiemɔ “na” tsɔɔ nɔ ni mli ni feelɔ ‘Kojo’ yɔɔ be ni agbe kaa lɛ 
naa lɛ.
3. Feemɔwiemɔ lɛ ji feemɔwiemɔ sanekuku lɛ yitso. Nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ
a. Tsɔne bibioo lɛ hiɛ foi waa.
 Feemɔwiemɔ ‘foi’ ji feemɔwiemɔ sanekuku lɛ yitso, ‘hiɛ foi waa’’
b. Kaselɔi lɛ taa okɔokpe kɛyaa sukuu daa leebi.
 Biɛ hu lɛ feemɔwiemɔ ‘taa’ lɛ ji feemɔwiemɔ saanekuku lɛ yitso, ‘taa 
okɔokpe kɛyaa sukuu daa leebi.’

Mligbalalɔi
Wɔkwɛ feemɔwiemɔ mlai ni adamɔɔ nɔ kɛtsɛrɛɔ sanemuji momo. Agbɛnɛ nyɛhaa 
wɔkwɛa mligbalalɔi ahe mlai ni adamɔɔ nɔ kɛtsɛrɛɔ sanemuu.
Nyɛkaiɔ nɔ ni mligbalɔi ji?
Mligbalalɔi ji wiemɔkulibii loo sanekukuji ni haa anuɔ feemɔwiemɔ ko shishi 
jogbaŋŋ yɛ sanemuu ko mli kɛtsɔ he ni afee nɔ ko yɛ, be ni afee nɔ ko kɛ henumɔ 
ko ni teenɔ nɔ.
Mligbalalɔ nɔkwɛmɔ nibii yɛ sanemuu mli nɛ:
1. Amɛba biɛ. (he ni nɔ ko tee nɔ yɛ)

2. Wɔshɛ leebi ŋmɛji kpawo. (be ni nɔ ko tee nɔ)
3. Bɔɔlutswaa kuu lɛ tswa bɔɔlu lɛ kɛ miishɛɛ. (henumɔ yɛ nɔ ko ni tee nɔ he)
 Mligalalɔi ni yɔɔ sanemuji nɛɛ amli ji; biɛ, ŋmɛji kpawo kɛ miishɛɛ.
Mlai/bɔ ni amɛtsuɔ nii
Mlai ni adamɔɔ nɔ kɛtsɛrɛɔ mligbalalɔi sanekuku lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ wiemɔi srɔtoi amli.
Mlai/bɔ ni amɛtsuɔ nii yɛ wiemɔ mli komɛi nɛ:
1. Mligbalalɔi damɔɔ shi akɛ yitso yɛ mligbalalɔ sanekuku mli.
 Nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ:
a. Hii lɛ wie kɛ gbee ni naa wa.
b. Nifeemɔ lɛ ba naagbee trukaa.
 Mligbalalɔi ni ji gbee ni naa wa kɛ trukaa lɛ damɔɔ shi akɛ mligbalalɔ 
sanekuku ni amɛdamɔɔ shi hu akɛ mligbalalɔ sanekuku lɛ yitsei.
2. Amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ kadilɔi yɛ mligbalalɔ mli.
 Nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ;
a. Amɛshwɛ jogbaŋŋ.
b. Sukuubii lɛ bɔ amɛhe mɔdɛŋ kɛtɛke nɔ.
 Yɛ sanemuji ni wɔkwɛ momo lɛ mli lɛ, mligbalalɔ ‘jogbaŋŋ’ lɛ miikadi loo 
tsɔɔ bɔ ni shwɛmɔ lɛ tee eha, ni mligbalalɔ kɛtɛke nɔ hu miikadi loo miitsɔɔ 
bɔ ni amɛbɔ amɛhe mɔdɛŋ amɛha.

WIEMƆ KƐ NITSUMƆ
Mlai ni akɛŋmaa Ga wiemɔ lɛ
HIƐGBELEMƆ
Mlijaa nɛɛ tsɔɔ saneŋmaa henɔi srɔtoi ni yɔɔ. Ŋaagbɛi ahe hiaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ 
saneŋmaa mli, jeee yɛ Ga wiemɔ lɛ mli pɛ shi yɛ Blɔfo kɛ wiemɔi krokomɛi fɛɛ 
amli.
Be ni oti mlijaa nɛɛ baaba naagbee lɛ, obaanyɛ;
1. Oŋma gbaa sane
2. Oŋma susumɔkɛtsɔɔmɔ sane
3. Oŋma nɔ ko feemɔ sane
Susumɔ otii
• Eji niŋmaa ko loo nifeemɔi loo gbɛi anɔ ni akɛtsɔɔ jwɛŋmɔ yɛ yitsei 
komɛi ahe.
• Obaakase nibii srɔtoi etɛ ni kɔɔ saneŋmaa he:
o Gbaa saneŋmaa ji wojiaŋ saji ni susuɔ loo tsɔɔ mɔ ko hesalɛ kɛtsɔ 
ŋaagbɛ ko nɔ ni ekɛ dumɔ woji hiɛ.
o Susumɔkɛtsɔɔmɔ saneŋmaa ji gbɛ ko nɔ ni haa kaselɔi susuɔ nɔ ko, 
mɔ ko, he ko, nibii ni mɔ ko etsɔ mli, henumɔ ko k.n k.n.
o Nɔ ko feemɔ saneŋmaa ji saneŋmaa ni tsɔɔ bɔ ni afeɔ nɔ ko loo 
agbalaa nɔ ko mli atsɔɔ loo asusuɔ nɔ ko he atsɔɔ. Ehaa wɔnaa lɛ 
faŋŋ ni wɔnuɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ shishi faŋŋ.
• Saneŋmaa fɛɛ saneŋmaa hiɛ jebɔ kɛ gbɛjianɔtoo srɔto ko.

Mlijaa 5 WIEMƆ KƐ NITSUMƆ
MLINII
Wɔsusu yitso nɛɛ he fioo yɛ wɔnikasemɔ ni eho lɛ mli. Ani obaanyɛ okai nɔ ni 
sanemuu oti ji? Mɛni ji sanemuu oti walɔ?
Kɛ onanemɛi asusu he koni oŋma ohetoo lɛ.
Agbɛnɛ kwɛmɔ akɛ ohetoo lɛ kɛ hetoo nɛɛ ja pɛpɛɛpɛ lo.
SANEMUU OTI
Sanemuu oti ji sane ni jieɔ yiŋtoo oti ko kpo yɛ mlijaa mli. Sanemuu oti walɔi ji 
wiemɔi ni yeɔ buaa ni sanemuu oti lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ susumɔ oti ko he.
Saneŋmaa
Hesalɛ kpakpa ko he hiaa kɛji wɔmiiŋma sane. Adamɔɔ susumɔi lɛ anɔ kɛŋmaa lɛ 
jogbaŋŋ yɛ kukuji amli. Enɛmɛi fɛɛ baanyɛ aye emuu kɛjie shɛɛ wiemɔi ni yɔɔ mli 
lɛ kpo, atoɔ naa pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛyeɔ nibii ni he baahia lɛ he odase, k.n k.n.
Eji niŋmaa ko loo nifeemɔi loo gbɛi anɔ ni atsɔɔ kɛjieɔ jwɛŋmɔ kpo yɛ yitsei 
komɛi ahe. Saneŋmaa fɛɛ saneŋmaa hiɛ yitso pɔtɛɛ ko.
Wɔbaasusu saneŋma srɔtoi etɛ ahe yɛ mlijaa nɛɛ mli.
Gbaa saneŋmaa
Eji gbaa sane ni aŋma yɛ wojiaŋ. Edamɔɔ yitso ko nɔ, ni hesalɛ akɛwieɔ, koni 
mɔ ko atsɔɔ nibii amli ni etsɔmɔ hu. Esa ni ole gbaa sane jebɔ ni onyɛ okɛtsu nii. 
Abaanyɛ adamɔ afoata loo anɔkwale saji agbɛjianɔtoo nɔ. Gbaa sane gbɛkpamɔ 
ji akɛ akɛ gbɛjianɔtoo kpakpa ni ato aha adesatamɔ atsu nii, tamɔ sane lɛ yitso, 
hekɛhɛlɛmɔ, Ga sɛɛsɛɛ, kn. Yɛ gbɛ nɛɛ nɔ lɛ kanelɔ lɛ jwɛŋmɔ baanyiɛ sane lɛ sɛɛ 
jogbaŋŋ. Akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ mɔ najiaŋgbɛi”mi” ni fɔɔ ŋmaa koni ŋmalɔ lɛ loo kanelɔ 
lɛ ana ehe loo toiboloi ana lɛ akɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe sane ni. Ehaa anaa nɔmimaa ahaa 
sanebimɔi ni jeɔ kpo lɛ, asɔɔ wiemɔi lɛ, ni aŋmaa yɛ eho be mli. Esa akɛ atoɔ 
nifeemɔ bei lɛ anaa taakɛ eba lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni sane lɛ amɔ toibolɔi ajwɛŋmɔ be ni 
eyaa hiɛ lɛ.Wielɔ lɛ wiemɔi lɛ asha jwɛŋmɔŋ mfoniri yɛ toibolɔi ajwɛŋmɔ mli, ni 
enyɛ ekɛ fɔŋwiemɔi atsu nii kɛgbala toibolɔi ajwɛŋmɔ kɛba sane lɛ nɔ.
Gbaa saneŋmaa yitsei komɛi:
• Ŋmaa sane yɛ oklɛŋklɛŋ gbi yɛ sukuu he.
• Gbɛhamɔ ko ni mihiɛ kpaŋ nɔ.

Hiɛgbelemɔ
Sane ni tsɛɔ jwɛŋmɔ sɛɛ kɛ sanebimɔi jeɔ sane lɛ shishi. Egbalaa loo etsɛɔ 
jwɛŋmɔ loo nɔ ko ni he miihia toibolɔi. Enyɛɔ ekɛ shigbɛlɛmɔ sane ko ni jieɔ 
yitso lɛ kpo tsuɔ nii.
Sanetso Mlijaa
Nibii ni tee nɔ fɛɛ lɛ amligbalamɔi loo nibii ni otsɔmɔ mli ni maa sane lɛ nɔ 
mi lɛ nɛ.
Onaa bei abɔ ni eshwɛ, ni osaa otsimɔɔ kpɔi loo nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ.

Naagbee

Susumɔkɛtsɔɔmɔ saneŋmaa
Mɛni ji Susumɔkɛtsɔɔmɔ saneŋmaa?
Eji saneŋmaa henɔ ko ni tsɔɔ bɔ ni afeɔ nɔ ko ahaa tamɔ; gbɔmɔ, he, hesalɛ, 
henumɔ loo sane ko he kn., ni aŋmaa kɛ hesalɛ ko bɔ ni afee ni ejie nɔ fɛɛ nɔ he 
ni awieɔ lɛ ŋmiiŋmi atsɔɔ. Saneŋmaa hiɛ sui ni jieɔ henumɔ ko kpo yɛ nibii pɔtɛɛ 
he ni awieɔ lɛ he etsɔɔ.
Susumɔkɛtsɔɔmɔ saneŋmaa jebɔ
Susumɔkɛtsɔɔmɔ saneŋmaa jebɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni wɔkase momo lɛ.
Hiɛgbelemɔ: Enɛ gbalaa mɔ jwɛŋmɔ kɛbaa sane pɔtɛɛ he ni awieɔ lɛ. Anyɛɔ ajeɔ 
shishi kɛ sanebimɔ ni he ehiaaa hetoo.
Sanetso: Enɛ gbalaa sane pɔtɛɛ ni awieɔ he lɛ mli. Kuku fɛɛ kuku hiɛ sanemuu 
oti ko ni ewieɔ he ni no tsɛɔ kanelɔ lɛ toi sɛɛ yɛ nibii ni amɛkpaa gbɛ lɛ he. Ehaa 
anaa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni sa akɛ ana kɛ nɔkwɛmɔ nibii ni sa akɛ ana.
Naagbee: Ewieɔ loo emaa sanetso ni yɔɔ sane kuku kome lɛ nɔ mi yɛ nibii pɔtɛɛ 
hewɔ ni agbaa sane lɛ.
Susumɔkɛtsɔɔmɔ saneŋmaa yitsei komɛi.
• Gbaa sini loo niyenii ni osumɔɔ waa he sane otsɔɔ.
• Susumɔ maŋ henɔyeli yiŋtoo ko he.
• Susumɔ wolo ko ni osumɔɔ kanemɔ he sane.
• Susumɔ maŋsɛɛ gbɛ ko ni ofa he.

HIƐGBELEMƆ
Mlijaa nɛɛ gbalaa jwɛŋmɔ lɛ kɛyaa hei ni obaana jemawɔji agbɛii yɛ yɛ wɔkutso 
lɛ mli yɛ Ghana, ni ehaa onaa hei ni kusumnaa gbɛii lɛ jɛ. Ebaagbele gbɛ eha bo 
kɛna he ni gbɛii lɛ jɛ kɛ nɔ ni kɛ gbɛi lɛ ba. Nikasemɔ nɛɛ haa onuɔ gbɛi ni awoɔ lɛ 
shishi ni anyaa he ni asaa akɛ bulɛ haa kusumii ni afeɔ lɛ. Ehaa anuɔ gbɛi srɔtoi ni 
awoɔ lɛ shishi ni ayoɔ nakai gbɛi kɛ mɛi ni woɔ lɛ akɛ Ghana bii ni akɛ nakai woo 
lɛ haa amɛ Mlijaa nɛɛ saa egbaa kpokuafoiaŋ hetsuumɔ kusum ni kpeɔ mɛi floŋŋ 
kɛjɛɔ gbekɛbii ajeŋ kɛyaa onukpai amli lɛ he sane. Sanegbaa lɛ baadamɔ gbɛi anɔ 
ni atsɔɔ akɛfeɔ kusumii nɛɛ, dani abaafee, be ni aafee kusumi lɛ, kɛ ni afee agbe 
naa lɛ sɛɛ Obaakwɛ sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ kusum nɛɛ feemɔ he kɛha kpokuafoi ni atsuɔ 
amɛkusum lɛ, amɛwekumɛi kɛ akutso muu lɛ fɛɛ. Obaanyɛ otsɔɔ srɔtoi ni yɔɔ 
kusum nɛɛ feemɔ yɛ akutso ko kɛ ekroko teŋ kɛ nifeemɔi ni je amɛhe yɛ Ghana 
nɛɛ.
Be ni mlijaa nɛɛ baaba naagbee lɛ, kaselɔ anyɛ:
• Atao jemawɔji ni yɔɔ kpɔ lɛ mli lɛ agbɛi, atao he ni amɛjɛ kɛ amnitsumɔ 
pɔtɛɛ.
• Atsɔɔ gbɛjianɔtoi anɔ ni atsɔɔ kɛtsuɔ kpokuafoi ahetsuumɔ kusum kɛkpeɔ 
amɛ awoɔ onukpai ateŋ lɛ (kpokuafoi ahetsuumɔ:: dani abaafee, be ni 
afeɔ kusum lɛ kɛkusum lɛ sɛɛ nifeemɔi
• Akɛ hetsuumɔ kusumi srɔtoi lɛ atotoi he yɛ akutsei srɔtoi lɛ amli yɛ 
Ghana.
Susumɔi oti
• Wɔŋgbɛi naa amɛshishifa kɛjɛɔ wɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ko deŋ
• Tsakpaa ko yɛ amɛkɛ mumɔŋ hewalɔ ko tɛŋ.
• Amɛtsɔɔ amɛsɛɛ nyiɛlɔi he ni amɛnaa amɛhewalɛi lɛ kɛjɛɔ

• Kpokuafoiaŋ hetsuumɔ ji be ko ni akɛkpeɔ kpokuafoi kɛboteɔ onukpa 
tsɔmɔ mli ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛwoɔ shwiei.
• Hetsuumɔ kusum nɛɛ tsɔɔ kpeemɔ ni afeɔ nɔ kɛgbalaa mɔ ko awoɔ ku ko 
mli.
• Kpeemɔ kusum nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ mɔ ko miiwo ku ko mli
• Afeɔ hetsuumɔ kusum nɛɛ ahaa gbekɛbii hii kɛ yei fɛɛ.
JEMAWƆJI AGBƐI
Gbɛi komɛi yɛ ni wɔnuɔ kɛji wɔkɛ Jemawɔji kɛ mumɔi shara. Wɔnaa gbɛii nɛɛ 
akɛ wɔji agbɛi. Dani wɔbaakase nii yɛ wɔji agbɛii ahe lɛ, esa akɛ wɔle nɔ ni wɔji 
ji.
Mɛni ji wɔji?
Jemawɔji lɛ ji mumɔi ni kuraa maji kɛ akutsei lɛ. Amɛji mumɔŋbii ni maŋbii 
heɔ amɛ ayeɔ ni anaa amɛ akɛ amɛ ni amɛbuɔ maŋbii lɛ ahe. Maŋbii lɛ jaa amɛ. 
Maŋbii naa amɛ akɛ hewalɛtsɛmɛi ni kuraa maŋbii ajeŋshihilɛ. Jemawɔji nɛɛ hiɛ 
hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni amɛtaoɔ. Ajaa amɛ ni afeɔ amɛsuɔmɔnaa nii. Anaa 
amɛ akɛ nuu aloo yoo. Jeŋ maji amli jamɔ wɔji lɛ ekomɛi: Zeus, Apollo, Athena, 
Aphrodite, Artemis, k.n.k.n. Yɛ Ghana nɛɛ kpokpai fɛɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwɔji. 
Jemawɔji wuji ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ ekomɛi nɛ:
Ga: Dantu, Nae, Klote, La Kpa, k.n.k.n..
Akan: Kune, Tegare, Nyamaa, k.n.k.n..
Dagomba: Tambo, etc.

Jemawɔji
Adamɔɔ hemɔkɛyeli ni ayɔɔ yɛ jemawɔŋ ko mli kɛ bɔ ni ajaa amɛ ahaa ni akɛ 
amɛgbɛi woɔ mɔ ko. Jemawɔji yɛ gbɛi pɔtɛɛ ni maŋbii, weku ko loo shiai woɔ kɛji 
amɛkɛ nakai jemawɔŋ lɛ sharaa.

Ani ole he ni ogbɛi lɛ jɛ?
Nɔ ni kɛ jemawɔji agbɛi lɛ baa
Mɛi yɛ nɔ hewɔ ni amɛnaa jemawɔji agbɛi. Ahaa mɛi jemawɔŋ gbɛi kɛtsɔɔ gbɛnaa 
nitsumɔ ni jemawɔŋ lɛ tsu, ekomɛi naa kɛtsɔ mumɔŋ nitsumɔ ni jemawɔŋ lɛ tsu 
eha mɔ ni akɛwo lɛ lɛ. Ekomɛi tsɔɔ ekaawoo ni ana kɛjɛ jemawɔŋ lɛ dɛŋ. Ni 
ekomɛi tsɔɔ kusum ni afeɔ yɛ nakai akutso loo maŋ lɛ nɔ.
Kɛfata he lɛ kɛji fɔlɔi komɛi yɛ ni amɛnaa bi lɛ amɛyanaa jemawɔŋ ko kɛha 
yelikɛbuamɔ. Amɛwoɔ shi ni kɛji amɛna bi lɛ akɛ jemawɔŋ lɛ gbɛi woɔ bi lɛ.
Jemawɔji agbɛi ahe sɛɛnamɔ
Jemawɔji agbɛi tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ jalɔi ashihilɛ mli.
Nɔ ni baa yɛ shishi nɛɛ ji sɛɛnamɔi ni mɛi ni hiɛ gbɛi lɛ naa:
1. Ayoɔ mɔ ni oji mra. Anaa jamɔ mli ni oyɔɔ ni anaa he ni ojɛ.
2. Etsɔɔ tsakpaa ni yɔɔ mɔ ni hiɛ gbɛi lɛ kɛ jemawɔŋ lɛ teŋ.
3. Jemawɔji agbɛi hiɔ shi yɛ yinɔi fɛɛ mli ni ehaa anaa kusum kɛ jamɔ nifeemɔi.
4. Ehaa anaa hemɔkɛyeli ni fɔlɔi lɛ yɔɔ.
5. Yɛ hemɔkɛyelii komɛi amli lɛ, jemawɔŋ gbɛi ni mɔ ko hiɛ haa lɛ nɔmimaa 
akɛ gbɛi ni ehiɛ lɛ haa lɛ hewalɛ srɔto ko, efoɔ ehe afabaŋ loo haa lɛ mumɔŋ 
hewalɛ ko.

2. Yɛ mɛi enyɔnyɔɔnyɔ akui amli lɛ nyɛŋmalaa ghanabii agbɛi nyɔŋma ko 
ni nyɛkwɛ jemawɔji agbɛi ni yɔɔ mli.

Eji be ko yɛ walashihilɛ mli ni nuu loo yoo ko naa akɛ eshɛ shwiewoo ni ebaanyɛ 
efɔ. Efɔɔ kaa kɛjɛ afii 10-14 kɛji gbekɛ yoo ni, ni kɛjɛ afii 12-16 kɛji gbekɛ nuu ni

Gbɔmɔtsoŋ tsakemɔi yɛ gbekɛbii yei ahe
Enɛmɛi fata tsakemɔi komɛi ni anaa yɛ yei ahe
• Hɛtso lɛ mli gbeleɔ
• Shwuɔji lɛ daraa agboi
• Dukuii lɛ feɔ kokloo
• Nakai bei amli nɔŋŋ lɛ amɛbɔi tsuiasɛɛ yaa
• Amɛjeɔ fufɔ loo fufɔ feɔ agboi
• Amɛshi kɛ ŋaashi hu tsaa tswɛi
Gbɔmɔtsoŋ tsakemɔi yɛ gbekɛbii hii ahe
Yɛ gbekɛbii hii amli lɛ anaa tsakemɔi ni baa nɛɛ:
• Hamɔ kɛ dɔlɔ feɔ agboi
• Amɛshi kɛ ŋaashi hu tsaa tswɛi
• Amɛtsitsi kɛ kɔɔji hu lɛɔ ni efeɔ agboi
• Kpɔiaŋ tuaa lɛ
• Gbee mli kwɔɔ
• Egbɔmɔtso kwɔɔ ni efeɔ gojoo fe tsutsu
• Tswɛi tsaa yɛ amɛhiɛ
Nɛkɛ okadii nɛɛ haa anaa akɛ mɔ ko eshɛ kpokuafonyo.

Kpokuafonyo hetsuumɔ
Kpokuafoiaŋ hetsuumɔ ji jeŋ kusum ko ni afeɔ ahaa kpokuafoi kɛjieɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ 
gbekɛbii ajeŋ kɛyaa onukpai amli. Enɛ ji kusum ni ji enyɔ nɔ ni afeɔ ahaa gbekɛ 
fɛɛ gbekɛ yɛ kpojiemɔ kusum sɛɛ ahaa mɔ ko, ni enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ gbekɛ nuu loo yoo 
ni afeɔ ahaa lɛ etsɔ onukpa.
Okpɔlɔ 6.1 ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ gbɛii srɔtoi ni akɛhaa kusum nɛɛ yɛ Ghana wiemɔi 
srɔtoi lɛ amli. Mɛni ji.

Te atsɛɔ kpokuafoiaŋ hetsuumɔ kusum lɛ tɛŋŋ yɛ Ga? Ani gbekɛbii hii kɛ yei fɛɛ

Hetsuumɔ ji nifeemɔi ni akɛ mɔ ko tsɔɔ mli kɛjieɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋɛlɛ ko nɔ kɛyaa 
ekroko nɔ. Ni no nɔŋŋ ji kpokuafoiaŋ hetsuumɔ kusum lɛ. Abaanyɛ akɛ mɔ 
ko awo mumɔŋ nifeemɔi loo kui loo asɔle mɔ ko awo jamɔ ko amli Fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, 
kpokuafoiaŋ hetsuumɔ he ji nɔ ni wɔwieɔ nɛɛ.
Hetsuumɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ
Gbɛjianɔtoi srɔtoi ni wɔnaa yɛ kpokuafoiaŋ hetsuumɔ mli lɛ jɛɔ maji kɛ kui kɛ 
amɛkusumi srɔtoi ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. Hesaamɔ dani abaabote kusumfeemɔ lɛ mli, 
kusum lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feemɔ kɛ agbɛnɛ hu kɛji agbe kusum lɛ naa nifeemɔi ahe sane 
he wɔbaawie yɛ biɛ nɛɛ.

2. Kpokuafoiaŋ hetsuumɔ kusum lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mli
 Yɛ hetsuumɔ kusum lɛ mli lɛ, wɔŋtsɛ/wɔyoo/yoo nukpa tsuɔ kusumi nɛɛ 
ehaa kpokoafonyo lɛ.
 Onukpai ni tsuɔ kusum lɛ yeɔ ŋkpai ni amɛtuɔ kpokuafoi lɛ amɛwoɔ mumɔŋbii 
lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛbu kpokuafoi nɛɛ ahe shweshweeshwe yɛ kusumfeemɔ nɛɛ 
mli. Ŋkpaiyeli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ akɛ amɛ tsɔmɔɔ mumɔŋ nibii amli ni ekomɛi nɛ:
a. Akwɛɔ mumɔŋ akɛ kpokoafonyo lɛ yɛ krɔŋŋ ni ehe tse lo. Ahaa eyataa 
mumɔŋ tɛ diŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ejuɔ ehe yɛ faa loo ŋshɔ loo koo mli, k.n.k.n.
b. Wɔŋtsɛ/wɔyoo/naa yoomo shɛɔ kpokoafonyo nɛɛ yitsɔi. Yɛ kusum nɛɛ 
feemɔ mli lɛ kpokuafoi nɛɛ taraa sɛsɛgwai loo shia sɛii anɔ
c. Aakpa gbɛ akɛ kpokuafoi nɛɛ baatara sɛsɛgwai anɔ be mli ni atsuɔ kusum 
nɛɛ.
d. Awoɔ amɛnaa niyenii tamɔ wuɔwɔlɔ kɛ Otɔ, k.n.k.n.

Akwɛ srɔtoi kɛ hegbɔyelii
Jɛ nibii ni yeɔ hegbɔi lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ekomɛi ni hiɛ amɛhe kwraa ji nibii ni agba he saji 
yɛ shishi lɛ.
Ayigbemɛi
1. Akutsei kɛ kui srɔtoi lɛ akusumi lɛ ye bei srɔtoi. Ekomɛi yeɔ otsi loo nyɔŋ 
kome.
2. Atsiɔ kpokuafoi nɛɛ anaa yɛ shia lɛ mli ni ahaa amɛnanemɛi yawoɔ amɛhe 
sɔlɛ nɛkɛ be mli fɛɛ
3. Anaa wuɔ wɔlɔ ni ahoɔ ahaa kpokuafoi ni amɛyeɔ lɛ akɛ ebaanyɛ eha ni 
amɛfɔ.
