Krɔbɔbii
1. Krɔbɔbii tsuɔ amɛkpokuafoi ahetsuumɔ kusum lɛ kɛji aha Nene Klɔweki 
(Shikpɔŋ wɔyoo lɛ) adafitswaa lɛ je kpo yɛ Oflɔ nyɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eyeɔ gbii 
enumɔ.
2. Dani abaatsu kusum nɛɛ fɔlɔi ni amɛbii baatsɔ kusum nɛɛ mli lɛ kɛ amɛbii 
lɛ yahaa amɛweku tɔkpaa wɔyoo ni kwɛɔ Dipo kusum nɛɛ nɔ lɛ.
3.  Yɛ kusum lɛ tsumɔ mli tuuŋtu lɛ, wɔŋtsɛ loo wɔyoo lɛ yeɔ ŋkpai ni etsuɔ 
mumɔŋ nitsumɔi krokomɛi ehaa kpokuafoi lɛ, ni ekomɛi ji eshɛɔ amɛyitsei 
ahe ehaa amɛ kɛ nifeemɔi krokomɛi.
Gamɛi
1. Gamɛi tsuɔ kpokuafoiaŋ hetsuumɔ kusum nɛɛ mra mli amɛhaa gbekɛbii ni 
amɛdrako tsɔ aloo kɛji ehe miihia
• Kɛji ana gbekɛ yoo ko akɛ eda ni eshɛ hetsuumɔ kusum lɛ mli lɛ efɔlɔi 
buaa amɛhe ni amɛyakɛɔ wulɔmɔ lɛ amɛyiŋtoo lɛ.
• Lɛ hu ewoɔ yeimeji aloo wɔyei ni tsuɔ kusum nɛɛ atoi nɔ..
• Ayatuɔ nibii ni akɛbaatsu kusum lɛ, nomɛi ji shinapu, ashinao, krɔbɔɔ, 
ayilɔɔ, bosao, taakotsa, boi, duku kɛ mamai
• No sɛɛ lɛ awoɔ baa ni amɛkɛjuɔ amɛhe. No ji bonsoŋmɛɛ lɛ. Anyɛɔ atsuɔ 
kusum nɛɛ yɛ gbekɛ yoo lɛ fɔlɔi loo weku shia lɛ.
• Kɛji aju amɛhe agbe naa lɛ abuuu amɛ mama dɔŋŋ shi awoɔ amɛ ashinao 
ni atsɛɔ amɛ boi. Amɛjoɔ yɛ wɔŋ lɛ naa. Nɛkɛ be mli fɛɛ lɛ ŋmɛmu ji nɔ 
ni amɛkpaa
• No sɛɛ lɛ awoɔ amɛ tsuŋ.
• Otofo yeimeji lɛ tsɔseɔ amɛ yɛ gblashihilɛ mli, bɔ ni akuraa shia ahaa
• Otii etɛ ni he hiaa waa ji Ŋshɔŋmɛɛ, tɛkɔmɔ kɛ shitɔwoo, jemawɔŋtɛtuu.. 
Enɛmɛi kɛ nibii krokomɛi ji nibii ni afeɔ ahaa kpokuafoi ni miitsɔ 
hetsuumɔ kusum lɛ mli.
• Naagbee nɔ kwraa ji shidaa.
Akanbii
1. Kusum nɛɛ tsumɔ yeɔ gbii kpaanyɔ ni ajeɔ shishi Ju loo Jufɔ
2. Dani kusum nɛɛ baaba nɔ lɛ maŋnyɛ lɛ kpaa kpokuafoi lɛ amli yɛ helooŋ 
kɛ mumɔŋ fɛɛ ekwɛɔ akɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ hi akɛ yoo floŋŋ ni ehiɛɛɛ hɔ lo.

Fioo ko ni atsuɔ he nii lɛ Ayigbemɛi tsɛɔ lɛ “Tudedeasi. Sisala tsɛɔ lɛ Baala” 
Gamɛi tsɛɔ nɛkɛkusum nɛɛ akɛ, Butrumwɔɔ/Deŋtuwoo ni Vaglabii tsɛɔ lɛ Pellaa. 
Kpokuafoiŋ Hetsuumɔ kɛha hii lɛ ejeee hetsuumɔ kusum nifeemɔ. Nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ: 
Yɛ Ayigbemɛi ateŋ lɛ, tu ni akɛwoɔ gbekɛ nuu dɛŋ lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ ‘Tudedeasi’. Ekɛ tu 
lɛ baafa lɛ kɛ eweku lɛ he.
Gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ ekomɛi ji enɛmɛi;
1. Abuaa nɛkɛ kpokuafoi nɛɛ anaa
2. Ahaa amɛ tsɔsemɔ yɛ nuufeemɔ mli, gbɛnaa nitsumɔ kɛ bɔlɛnamɔ mli.
3. Gbekɛbii hii lɛ atuumɔ kɛbote onukpai akui amli
4. Helooŋ kɛ mumɔŋ hesaamɔ
5. Atsɔɔ amɛ kusumi kɛ subaŋi kpakpai.
Gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ aaanyɛ afee srɔtoi yɛ akutsei kɛ maji srɔtoi lɛ amli, enɛ damɔ akutso 
lɛ hemɔkɛyeli nɔ.
Sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ kpokuafoiaŋ hetsuumɔ he
1. Ehaa onukpatsɔmɔ yeɔ emuu..
2. Ehaa kpokuafoi nilee jwɛŋmɔ ni akɛhiɛɔ gbɛnaa kroko.
3. Ehaa anaa akɛ kpokuafoi nɛɛ efee klalo kɛha gblamlibotemɔ.
4. Esaa mɛi ni atsuu amɛhe lɛ yɛ mumɔŋ kɛ helooŋ fɛɛ kɛha gblamlibotemɔ..
5. Ehaa kpokuafoi nɛɛ kaseɔ subaŋ kpakpai.
6. Etsɔɔ kpokuafoi kusum kɛ kusumnaa nifeemɔi kpakpai .
7. Ekuɔ subaŋi kɛ bɔlɛnamɔ gbohii anaa. .
8. Kpokuafoiaŋ hetsuumɔ haa yei ni tsɔɔ kusum lɛ mli naa jwetri kɛtsuɔ nii .

Mlijaa 7 Kusum nifeemɔi kɛ maŋkuramɔ gbɛjianɔto.
KUSUM NIFEEMƆI KƐ MAŊKURAMƆ 
GBƐJIANƆTO.
Kusumnaa Maŋkuramɔ
HIƐGBELEMƆ
Mlijaa nɛɛ gbeleɔ kusumnaa maŋkuramɔ gbɛjianɔtoo yɛ Ghana lɛ hiɛ etsɔɔ bo. 
Ewieɔ maŋkuralɔi kɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ nitsumɔ ni etsuɔ lɛ he etsɔɔ, ni anaa nibii ni sa akɛ 
gbɛhehiɛlɔi atsu, kɛ amɛhe sɛɛnamɔi. Mlijaa nɛɛ haa bo nilee ni onuɔ kusumnaa 
maŋkuramɔ kɛ nɔyeli nifeemɔi ashishi yɛ okusum lɛ mli. Obaale mlai ni kudɔɔ 
maŋlumɛi anifeemɔi kɛ sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ amɛnifeemɔi lɛ ahe.kɛ nɔyaa ni ekɛbahaa 
maŋbii kɛ akutso lɛ.
Be ni nikasemɔ lɛ baaya naagbee lɛ, kaselɔi anyɛ:
i. Atao kusumnaa nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli (tsɛ, weku yitso, wekutɔkpaa 
yitso, knkn)
ii Atao kusumnaa maŋkuralɔi agbɛjianɔtoi lɛ mli (kpokpaa bibii anɔ 
maŋtsɛmɛi, akrowai kɛ maji bibii anɔ maŋtsɛmɛi, maŋtsɛwolɔi, knkn)
Nikasemɔ mli otii
• Tsɛ Ataa loo Papa ji weku kɔklɔɔ ni ayeɔ tsɛsɛɛ nii yɛ mli lɛ yitso.
• Yɛ weku ni ayeɔ nyɛsɛɛ nii yɛ mli lɛ Yoo nyɛɔ feɔ weku lɛ yitso.
• Weku tɔkpaa yitsei ji majiatsɛmɛi nukpai ni kamɔ kpokpa wuji anaa ni 
aje gbɛ ahala amɛ ni ato amɛ akɛ kpokpa wuji anɔ majiatsɛmɛi.
3
Mlijaa 7 Kusum nifeemɔi kɛ maŋkuramɔ gbɛjianɔto.
KUSUMNAA MAŊKURAMƆ GBƐJIANƆTOO 
LƐ SHIKAMƆ
Atao kusumnaa nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli ( Tsɛ Ataa/Papa, weku yitso, wekutɔkpaa 
yitso).
Kusumnaa Maŋkuramɔ
Kusumnaa Maŋkuramɔ ji maŋkuramɔ ko ni shikwɛɛbii kɛ jeŋ kusum kɛ jeŋ 
nilee ni akɛkuraa. Shikwɛɛbii lɛ hiɛ maŋkuramɔ gbɛjianɔtoo kpakpai ni ato yɛ 
wɔkutsei lɛ amli ni akɛkuraa maji lɛ. Ehiɛ nɔyeli naatoo ni tsɔɔ lumɔ fɛɛ lumɔ kɛ 
mɔ ni shishi ni eyɔɔ. Srɔtoi baa yɛ nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoi nɛɛ amli yɛ wiemɔi srɔtoi lɛ 
amli shi akutsei lɛ titri hiɛ gbɛjianɔtoo kome.
Kusumnaa maŋkuramɔ gbɛjianɔtoo yɛ weku 
kɔklɔɔ mli
Yɛ wɔGhana lɛ weku nyɛɔ efeɔ weku kɔklɔɔ ni tsɛ, nyɛ kɛ bii yɔɔ mli, loo weku 
gbajaa ni tsɛkwɛ, nyɛkwɛ, tsɛnukpa loo tsɛfio loo nyɛnukpa loo nyɛfio, Nii, 
Naa knkn fata he. Koni ohiɛ aka bo shi lɛ kusumnaa nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoo ŋɔɔ tsɛ, 
wekuyitso, weku tɔkpaa yitso, majiatsɛmɛi, maŋtsɛmɛi bibii, maŋtsɛwolɔi kɛ 
kpokpa wuji anɔ maŋtsɛmɛi kɛ ekrokomɛi.
Nitsumɔ
Mɛni ji shikwɛɛ maŋkuramɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ni yɔɔ oshia lɛ mli? Namɔ ji hiɛnyiɛlɔ 
yɛ oweku kɔklɔɔ lɛ mli? Namɔ ji hiɛnyiɛlɔ yɛ oweku gbajaa lɛ mli? Ani oshi 
weku tɔkpaa ko nɔ?
Nɔyeli shidaamɔ tso ji gbɛnaa hiɛlɔi ashidaamɔ tso ni atɛŋ ni tsɔɔ gbɛnaahiɛlɔi 
ayelihe yɛ gbɛnaahiɛlɔi ateŋ yɛ ku ko mli. Etsɔɔ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ yelihe yɛ ku loo 
nitsumɔ ko mli, kɛjɛ onukpa ni fe fɛɛ nɔ kɛyashi gbɛnaa bibioo ni fe fɛɛ nɔ, ni no 
tsɔɔ mɔ shishi ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ko hɔ.
4
Mlijaa 7 Kusum nifeemɔi kɛ maŋkuramɔ gbɛjianɔto.
Yɛ kusumnaa nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoo mli lɛ, nɛkɛ ji bɔ ni wɔbaana nɔyeli tso lɛ.
Fig7.1: Nɔyeli tso yɛ akutso mli
1. Weku tɔkpaa yitso:
 Weku tɔkpaa ji ku mli bii ni jɛ tɔkpaa kome mli, ni niimɛi lɛ jɛ la kome mli 
loo gbala mli loo niimɛi aseshi bii. Eji wekui srɔtoi amli bii ni jɛ nii kome 
mli ni hiɛ gbɛi tso kome, ni amɛkɛwoo haa hiɛnyiɛlɔ kome kɛ blema tsɛ 
kome. Ayɔseɔ amɛ kɛ subaŋ kome, susumɔ kome kɛ tsuishwee nii kome. Mɔ 
ni ku lɛ woɔ akɛ amɛhiɛnyiɛlɔ lɛ ji mɔ ni amɛtsɛɔ lɛ weku tɔkpaa yitso lɛ. 
Akutsei komɛi yɛ subaŋi ni amɛtaoɔ amɛna yɛ mɔ ni abaawo lɛ tɔkpaa yitso 
he. Subaŋi agbɛ ni akpaa lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ akutsei krokomɛi amli. Yɛ kui komɛi 
amli lɛ weku yitsei lɛ ji mɛi ni woɔ ni yɛ ekrokomɛi amli lɛ akɛhaa mɔ ni 
eshɛ enɔ yɛ yinɔi lɛ amli.
2. Weku yitso lɛ:
 Weku yitso ji mɔ ko ni weku mli onukpai lɛ ekɔ lɛ akɛ amɛhiɛnyiɛlɔ. 
Amɛnitsumɔ oti ji, amɛkura weku lɛ koni amɛye saji fɛɛ ni baa wekumɛi lɛ 
ateŋ, koni amɛbaa weku nibii fɛɛ yi. Esa akɛ ana hiɛnyiɛlɔi asubaŋi kɛ nilee 
komɛi yɛ emli. Efɔɔ kaa akɛ akɛ weku yitso gbɛnaa nɛɛ haa hii.
3. Tsɛ Ataa loo Papa:
 Tsɛ Ataa loo Papa ji shia loo weku kɔklɔɔ ni lɛ kɛ eŋa kɛ ebii lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ 
yitso. Tsɛ Ataa ji mɔ ni taoɔ weku kɔklɔɔ nɛɛ mli hiamɔi nibii fɛɛ.
Nitsumɔ:
Yɛ nɔkwɔlɛ mli lɛ namɔ ji mɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, weku tɔkpaa yitso, weku yitso 
kɛ tsɛ ataa? Yɛ kusumnaa lɛ tsɔɔmɔ nɔkwɔlɛi ni yɔɔ nɔyelii lɛ amli hewalɛtsɛ.
5
Mlijaa 7 Kusum nifeemɔi kɛ maŋkuramɔ gbɛjianɔto.
Sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ gbɛnaahiɛlɔi agbɛnaahiɛmɔi lɛ ahe yɛ kusumnaa nɔyeli mli.
1. Weku tɔkpaa yitso
 Weku tɔkpaa yitso nifeemɔi komɛi nɛ:
a. Etsuɔ enii akɛ kojolɔnukpa yɛ tɔkpaa lɛ mli.
b. Ebaa blema saji ni yɔɔ tɔkpaa lɛ he lɛ yi.
c. Ekwɛɔ ni tɔkpaa lɛ kusumi ni yɔɔ lɛ akalaaje.
d. Efoɔ tɔkpaa lɛ gboshi nibii (shikpɔji kɛ nibii krokomɛi) ahe afabaŋ.
e. Ekwɛɔ ni akpaleɔ gboshi nii lɛ ahaa, kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kɛyaa yinɔ ni baa lɛ.
2. Weku yitso
 Weku yitso gbɛnaa nitsumɔi lɛ ekomɛi nɛ:
a. Efaa weku lɛ he kɛjeɔ haomɔi kɛ oshrai amli.
b. Ekɛ nɔyaa baa wekumɛi abii ashihilɛ mli.
c. Ekwɛɔ ni toiŋjɔlɛ baa weku lɛ mli.
d. Ekuraa weku lɛ nibii ni eyɔɔ, tamɔ shikpɔji, shiai, tsɔji knkn
e. Ekwɛɔ saji ni teɔ shi yɛ shia mli kɛ agbonaa nɔi fɛɛ.
f. Enyiɛɔ hiɛ ni eyeɔ weku lɛ najiaŋ yɛ maŋ kɛ akutsei kɛsharamɔ saji amli.
g. Ewoɔ wekumɛi abii ahewalɛ kɛ ekaa yɛ hiamɔ beiaŋ.
h. Ekɔɔ jwɛŋmɔ ni sa yɛ weku lɛ najiaŋ.
3. Tsɛ Ataa
 Gbɛnaa nitsumɔi pii yɛ ha tsɛ ataa yɛ weku kɔklɔɔ lɛ mli. Ekomɛi nɛ:
a. Ewoɔ mlai ni ekwɛɔ akɛ aye nɔ
b. Ehaa eshia lɛ naa he afabaŋfoo
c. Ehaa eshia lɛ naa shifimɔ kɛ ekaa yɛ shihilɛ mli
d. Etsuɔ enii akɛ tsɔselɔ
e. Ehaa eshia mli bii lɛ amɛhiamɔ nibii
Nitsumɔ 7.1:
Kɛhooo kwraa lɛ gbalamɔ weku tɔkpaa hiɛnyiɛlɔ nitsumɔ otii etɛ mli otsɔɔ, 
Okɛ onaanyo asusu he.

Nitsumɔ 7.2
Taomɔ kusumnaa nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoo ni yɔɔ okutso lɛ mli lɛ, ogbala sɛɛnamɔi 
ni yɔɔ mli lɛ otsɔɔ.
Nitsumɔ 7.3
Daamɔ shi akɛ weku yitso koni osaa wekumɛiabii enyɔ ni miibe yɛ nyɔmɔ ko 
ni mɔ kome hiɛ mɔ kroko lɛ he. Mɛi komɛi baadamɔ shi akɛ mɛi ni mli ewo la 
yɛ nɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ he. Abo toi ni akwɛ weku yitso lɛ nitsumɔi ni sa lɛ.
Nitsumɔ 7.4
Yɛ osusumɔ naa lɛ ani kusumnaa maŋkuramɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ he miihia 
ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ? Bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni otsɔɔ nɔ hewɔŋ ni osusuɔ nakai lɛ.
KUSUMNAA MAŊKURAMƆ GBƐJIANƆTOO
Nɔkwɔlɔmɔi ni yɔɔ kusumnaa nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ mli lɛ, nyiɛ nibii ni baa nɛɛ 
aŋɛlɛ nɔ:
1. Maŋtsɛ nukpa/Maŋtsɛ wulu.
2. Kpokpaa bibii anɔ maŋtsɛmɛi/maji bibii anɔ maŋtsɛmɛi.
3. Maŋnyɛmɛi.
4. Mantsɛwolɔi.
Kɛfata nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he lɛ ayɛ lumɛi tamɔ tatsɛ, wolɛiatsɛ loo okwaafoiatsɛ kɛ 
weku tɔkpaa yitsei, weku yitsei knkn.
1. Maŋtsɛ nukpa
 Maŋtsɛmɛi wuji kɛ onukpai ji jaku hiɛnyiɛlɔi aloo wiemɔkui wuji ahiɛnyiɛlɔi. 
Amɛji hewalɛtsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ amɛkui lɛ amli ni mɔ ko bɛ amɛsɛɛ dɔŋŋ yɛ 
amɛkpokpai lɛ anɔ. Akwɔɔ kɛyaa gbɛhe nɛɛ kɛji odehe ji bo, ni bei komɛi lɛ 
anaa gbɛhe nɛɛ kɛtsɔɔ nyɛsɛɛ loo tsɛsɛɛ gboshi niyeli nɔ kɛji ablade ji ofɔlɔi 
(tsɛ loo nyɛ) ni edamɔɔ ku mli ni ojɛ hu nɔ. Maŋtsɛ nukpa loo Maŋtsɛ wulu 
yɛ woogbɛi ni akɛhaa. Nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ. Ayigbemɛi (Ewe) hiɛ Fiaga, Akanbii 
hiɛ Osagyefuo, Dagombabii hiɛ Yaa-Naa knkn.
 Maŋtsɛ nukpa/ Maŋtsɛ wuli nifeemɔi/gbɛnaa nitsumɔi nɛ:
7
Mlijaa 7 Kusum nifeemɔi kɛ maŋkuramɔ gbɛjianɔto.
a. Hiɛnyiɛlɔ kɛha kpokpa wulu ni hiɛ akutsei kɛ akrowai babaoo.
b. Adamɔ shi kɛtsu kusumi kɛ nifeemɔi krokomɛi.
c. Ekura sɛi shikpɔji ni yɔɔ ekpokpa lɛ nɔ lɛ.
d. Akura ni eye saji yɛ ekpokpa lɛ nɔ.
e. Awo mla ni ekwɛ akɛ aye mla lɛ nɔ.
f. Ekwɛ ni nɔyaa aba ekpokpa lɛ nɔ.
g. Ekwɛ ni toiŋjɔlɛ kɛ ekomefeemɔ ahi ewebii lɛ ateŋ.
h. Etsu enii akɛ mɔ ni sumɔɔ ekomefeemɔ koni eye ekpokpa lɛ najiaŋ yɛ 
gwabɔɔ shishi.
2. Kpokpa bibii kɛ maji bibii anɔ maŋtsɛmɛi
 Kpokpa bibii kɛ maji bibii anɔ maŋtsɛmɛi hɔlɔ kpokpa wuji anɔ maŋtsɛmɛi 
ashishi. Amɛyɛ hewalɛ yɛ maji bibii kɛ akrowai lɛ anɔ. Eji gboshinii ni ashiɔ 
ahaa, ajɛɔ odehei aweku mli ni ayeɔ maŋtsɛ.
 Kpokpa bibii/maji bibii anɔ maŋtsɛmɛi agbɛnaa nitsumɔi:
a. Amɛtsuɔ nii kɛji maŋtsɛ nukpa lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ.
b. Amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa shweshweeshwenamɔ yɛ amɛmaji lɛ amli.
c. Amyeɔ saji yɛ amɛmaji lɛ amli
d. Amɛkwɛɔ koni toiŋjɔlɛ atsu nii yɛ amɛmaji lɛ amli.
e. Amɛtsuɔ kusumi ni yɔɔ amɛsɛii lɛ ahe lɛ.
3. Maŋnyɛ
 Maŋnyɛmɛi lɛ tsuɔ amɛnii akɛ mumɔ mli yitsei kɛha yei ni yɔɔ maji lɛ amli 
lɛ, ni amɛkɛ blema saji ni kɔɔ yinɔbii ahe lɛ toɔ. Amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ kɛtsuɔ nii 
kɛbaa yei kɛ gbekɛbii ashihilɛ yi, yɛ amɛmaji lɛ amli. Yɛ jakui ni yeɔ nyɛsɛɛ 
nii lɛ amli lɛ, eji maŋnyɛmɛi lɛ agbɛnaa akɛ amɛ amɛjieɔ mɔ ni sa ni awo lɛ 
maŋtsɛ lɛ. Maŋnyɛ lɛ ni hiɛ hewalɛ ni akɛtsɔɔ mɔ ni sa akɛ awo kɛji abladei 
awekui lɛ efamɔ mɛi fɛɛ ni sa kɛjɛ amɛwekui lɛ amli amɛha sɛi lɛ he onukpai 
lɛ. Amɛyɛ hegbɛ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfamɔɔ maŋnyɛmɛi bibii ni baasɔmɔ 
amɛ.
 Maŋnyɛmɛi agbɛnaa nitsumɔi lɛ ekomɛi ji:
a. Aye abua gbɛnaa nitsumɔi ni maŋtsɛmɛi tsuɔ yɛ maŋkuramɔ gbɛjianɔtoo 
mli lɛ.
b. Akwɛ ni eye saji ni gbaa yei anaa yɛ amɛkutsei lɛ amli.

c. Amɛ ni amɛfaa yei ahegbɛi ahe.
d. Amɛbaa yinɔi lɛ ahe saji ayi koni amɛkɛtsɔse yinɔi ni baa yɛ amɛkutsei 
lɛ amli lɛ.
4. Maŋtsɛwolɔi
 Maŋtsɛwolɔ loo wolɔi ji mɛi ni bɛŋkɛ ni amɛyɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ odehe ko ni sa 
maŋtsɛ ko nɔ, tsɛbelɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ amɛyeee emuu kɛha maŋtsɛyeli. Ku nɛɛ 
kpeɔ ni amɛkwɛɔ mɔ ni sa akɛ awo lɛ maŋtsɛ.
 Maŋtsɛwolɔi anitsumɔi nɛ:
a. Amɛwo maŋtsɛ hee kɛji gbɛ ba sɛi lɛ he.
b. Amɛtsuɔ kusum kɛji maŋtsɛ lɛ gbo.
c. Amɛdamɔɔ shi kɛkpaa maŋtsɛ kɛji gbɛ ba maŋtsɛ lɛ he.
d. Amɛkɛ maŋtsɛ hee lɛ tsɔɔ maŋbii lɛ.
e. Amɛwoɔ maŋtsɛ lɛ ŋaa.

1. Namɔ ji oweku kɔklɔɔ lɛ yitso?
2. Taomɔ nibii enyɔ ni okpaa gbɛ akɛ opapa afee ni no bɛ gbɛnaa nitsumɔi

3. Kanemɔ sane ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ koni otɛŋ nɔyelitso yɛ kusumnaa maŋkuramɔ

maji bibii an maŋtsɛmɛi, maŋtsɛwolɔi) Okɛ nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ ni ona yɛ

 Sane A
 Ghanabii akusumnaa nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoo
 Dani wɔbaabote “kɛɛmɔ makɛɛ eko” nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoo mli lɛ, 
kusumnaa nɔyeli ji maŋkuramɔ gtbɛjianɔtoo ni yɔɔ Ghana nɛɛ. Atoɔ 
gbɛjianɔi nɛɛ kɛbɔleɔ maŋtsɛmɛi kɛ amɛhewɔŋ onukpai ahe yɛ nɔkwɔlɛi 
amli Yɛ akrowai kɛ akutsei amli lɛ maŋtsɛmɛi ji mɛi ni nyiɛ akrowai 
lɛ ahiɛ kɛ amɛhewɔŋ onukpai, ni maŋtsɛwolɔi lɛ hu fata he, ni amɛ 
amɛtoɔ gbɛjianɔi amɛhaa akutso lɛ. Ahalaa onukpai nɛɛ yɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ 
mlikwɔlɛi, afii ni amɛye kɛ hesalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ yɛ maŋkuramɔ mli. Yɛ 
akrowaiaŋ maŋtsɛmɛi nɛɛ ayiteŋ lɛ, maŋtsɛmɛi onukpai ji mɛi ni kuraa 
jɛmɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ akrowai babaoo ni amɛkwɛɔ akɛ aye gbɛjianɔtoi anɔ, 
aye saji koni mla atsu nii ni toiŋjɔlɛ aba maji lɛ amli. Maŋtsɛmɛi aku 
ni yɔɔ eshishi lɛ ji mɛi ni woɔ lɛ ŋaa ni akpaa gbɛ akɛ ekɔ jwɛŋmɔi 
ni baaye abua mɔ fɛɛ mɔ yɛ kpokpa lɛ nɔ. He ni maŋtsɛ wulu bɛ lɛ 
Maŋtsɛnukpa ji mɔ ni da fe fɛɛ Maŋtsɛnukpa lɛ yɛ mumɔŋ kɛ heloo mli 
hewalɛ fe enukpai lɛ fɛɛ. Nɛkɛ kusumnaa maŋkuramɔ nɛɛ kpaa gbɛ akɛ 
mɛi atsɔɔ amɛjwɛŋmɔi yɛ susumɔi srɔtoi lɛ amli, ekɛ bulɛ haa onukpa 
ni ehaa anaa sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ akutso mli onukpai ayelikɛbuamɔ.
4. Nyɛgbaa gbɛnaa nitsumɔi 3 ni lumɛi nɛɛ tsuɔ yɛ kusumnaa maŋkuramɔ 
gbɛjianɔtoo mli, kɛ amɛhe sɛɛnamɔi yɛ akutso lɛ mli.

JEŊNILEE
Ŋaaŋ saji kɛ wojiaŋ saji
HIƐGBELEMƆ
Mlijaa nɛɛ miitsɔɔ ŋaaŋ saji kɛ wojiaŋ saji yɛ Ga nikasemɔ mli. Abaagbele 
ŋkpaiyeli nɔ hiɛ yɛ ŋaaŋ saji amli atsɔɔ nyɛ. Abaatsɔɔ sɛɛnamɔi kɛ gbɛjianɔtoo nɔ 
ni atsɔɔ kɛtsuɔ kusumii nɛɛ. Abaasusu ŋkpaiyeli he sɛɛnamɔi hu he kɛ nɔ hewɔ ni 
asɔleɔ atsɔɔ nyɛ. Abaawo nyɛ hewalɛ koni nyɛ kɛ nyɛ he awo nikasemɔ lɛ mli bɔ 
ni afee ni nyɛna nɔ hewɔ ni ŋkpaiyeli sɔlemɔ he hiaa yɛ Gamɛi asateŋ. Nɛkɛ mlijaa 
nɛɛ he hiaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ga nikasemɔ mli ni ekɛ tsakpaa ko baa nikasemɔ kroko 
he tamɔ Jamɔ he nikasemɔ. Mlijaa nɛɛ baaha bo nilee ni baaha onya okusum lɛ 
kɛ kusumii krokomɛi ahe. Mlijaa nɛɛ hu gbeleɔ yarawoo lalai ni yɔɔ Ghana hiɛ 
kɛtsɔɔ bo. Akɛ nyɛ baasusu yarawoo lalai yɛ Ga mli he. Nyɛ baakwɛ saji komɛi 
ni kɔɔ yarawoo lalai ahe. Susumɔi lɛ baakɔ yarawoo lalai anitsumɔ he. Kɛfata he 
lɛ, mlijaa nɛɛ gbeleɔ afoata mli otui ahiɛ kɛtsɔɔ bo. Otsɔɔlɔ lɛ baanyiɛ ohiɛ kɛsusu 
otui ni yɔɔ afoata mli tamɔ shwɛlɔi, oti he ni awieɔ, he ni sane lɛ ba yɛ, naatoo, 
mɔ ko susumɔ/jwɛŋmɔ kɛ ekrokomɛi.
Yɛ nikasemɔ nɛɛ naagbee lɛ, esa akɛ:
• ole gbɛjianɔtoo ni akwɛɔ kɛyeɔ ŋkpai;
• osusu yarawoo lalai ahe;
• asusu afoata mli otui ahe (n.k, shwɛlɔi, oti he ni awieɔ, he ni sane lɛ ba 
yɛ, naatoo k.n k.n);
• anya afoata sane he (yitso, oti he ni awieɔ, wiemɔ ni akɛŋmaa, 
heŋɔɔmɔwolɔi, k.n, k.n.).
Otii ahe susumɔ:
• Ŋkpaiyeli ji kusum sɔlemɔ.
• Gbɛjianɔtoi ni adamɔɔ nɔ kɛyeɔ ŋkpai; agboshimɔ, jaomɔ, amaniɛbɔɔ kɛ 
naamuu.
• Sane yitso ji wiemɔ ni kɔɔ nɔ ni sane lɛ wieɔ he lɛ.

• He ni sane lɛ ba yɛ lɛ ji adesa lɛ sɛɛtso. No tsɔɔ maŋ loo akrowa loo

ŊKPAIYELI
Wɔbaasusu gbɛjianɔtoo ni adamɔɔ kɛyeɔ ŋkpai. Wɔbaakwɛ agboshimɔ, jaomɔ, 
amaniɛbɔɔ kɛ naamu ni yɔɔ ŋkpaiyeli mli.
Ŋkpaiyeli
Eji nifeemɔ ko ni akɛ daa, akpɛtɛshi, weŋ, ŋmadaa, nu, tɛŋdaa loo nɔ ko ni hiɛ 
nu su, ni akɛshwieɔ shi ahaa mumɔŋ bii (sisai, jemawɔŋ, wɔji) koni amɛtsu nɔ ko 
pɔtɛɛ ko amɛha. Akɛ daa tamɔ shinapu, weŋ, akpɛtɛshi, ŋmadaa, kɛ ekrokomɛi lɛ 
shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni ajaoɔ kɛwoɔ mumɔi lɛ atoii anɔ ni afaa amɛ koni amɛfee nɔ ko 
pɔtɛɛ amɛha yɛ nɔ hewɔ ni ayeɔ ŋkpai lɛ he. Yɛ hei komɛi lɛ, akɛ yibii tamɔ abele 
loo omɔ woɔ nu lɛ mli kɛyeɔ ŋkpai lɛ. Ŋkpaiyeli yeɔ he eko jogbaŋŋ yɛ Afrika bii 
ashihilɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ ŋkpaiyeli lɛ nɔ lɛ, akɛtsɛɔ blema tsɛmɛi kɛ mumɔi lɛ atoi sɛɛ 
ni akɛfɔɔ amɛ nine kɛbaa nifeemɔi ashishi hu.

Ŋkpaiyeli mli tso
• Agboshimɔ:
 Aboɔ agoo kɛshiɔ agbo kɛbiɔ gbɛ yɛ gbi ni afeɔ nii lɛ mli hewalɛ koni 
tsɛmɛi kɛ mumɔi lɛ ahɛle shi yɛ nifeemɔ ni baa lɛ he ni amɛye amɛbua.
• Jaomɔ:
 Atsɛɔ Tsɛ Ofe lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ, ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ, jemawɔji, sisai, kɛ mumɔi 
krokomɛi fɛɛ ni ole koni amɛbaye amɛbua nifeemɔ lɛ. Akwɛɔ amɛtsiimɔ kɛ 
hewalɛ kɛtoɔ naa ni atsɛɔ
• Amaniɛbɔɔ:
 Mɔ ni yeɔ ŋkpai lɛ bɔɔ mumɔi lɛ amaniɛ kɛtsɔɔ nɔ hewɔ ni nifeemɔ lɛ yaa 
nɔ lɛ. Ebiɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ abapia nifeemɔ lɛ kɛyashi naagbee.
• Naamuu:
 Yɛ nɛkɛ ŋɛlɛ nɛɛ nɔ lɛ ebiɔ jɔɔmɔ ehaa mɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ, kɛ mɛi ni hiɛ

kulɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni afeɔ lɛ afite lɛ koni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ wɔteiaŋ.

YARAWOO LALA
Susumɔ sanebimɔ:
Mɛni henumɔ onaa kɛji owekunyo ko tsɔ esɛɛ?
Mɛni ji Yarawoo lala?
Eji nyanyɔji ashishikpemɔ kɛ awerɛho lala ni akɛfoɔ mɛi ni egboi. Eji lala ni alaa 
lɛ blɛoo kɛtsɔɔ dɔlɛ kɛ awerɛho, ni alaa yɛ yara kɛ gbele sɔɔmɔ feemɔ nɔ. Bei 
komɛi lɛ akɛjieɔ mɔ ni egbo lɛ yi .
Yarawoo lalai ahesɛɛnamɔ
1. Akɛfoɔ mɔ ni egbo lɛ.
2. Etsɔɔ tsakpaa ni kaa mɔ ni egbo lɛ wala beiaŋ kɛ be ni egbo nɛɛ.
3. Akɛgbeleɔ sane ko ni he miihia jogbaŋŋ hiɛ.
4. Akɛhaa mɔ ni egbo lɛ yaawɔ jogbaŋŋ.
5. Akɛtsɔɔ ŋmɛɛmɔ ni nɔ ko kpakpa eŋmɛɛ wɔ he.
6. Aatao atsɔɔ akɛ mɔ lɛ egbo moŋ shi hiɛnɔkamɔ ji akɛ eyɛ.
7. Yɛ maji komɛi amli lɛ anaa yarawoo lalai nɛɛ akɛ faafoo kusum kɛha mɔ ni 
egbo lɛ.

naatoo yɔɔ. Shwɛlɔi ahenɔi ji shwɛlɔ oti kɛ najiaŋwolɔ. Shwɛlɔ oti lɛ ji mɔ ni anuɔ

ehaa lɛ naagbai srɔtoi. Shwɛlɔ kroko hu ji Tsuisalɔ, lɛ lɛ etsakee eyiŋtoo, nɔ ni

Oyiŋ-etsɛɛɛ-tsɔmɔ, shwɛlɔ nɛɛ nyɛɛɛ edamɔ yiŋtoo kome nɔ. Edamɔɔ ŋaa fɛɛ ŋaa

INTRODUCTION
This section discusses identification of key ideas in texts and discourse. It always gives 
information on specific ideas or knowledge to the reader or hearer. The information given 
may come from all perspectives such as education, industrialisation, mining among others. 
It may also indicate some cultural values such as respect, tolerance and patience. Identifying 
key ideas gives you a better understanding of the discourse. It also enhances your critical 
thinking skills and interpretation abilities. There are types of reading techniques namely 
skimming and scanning and the application of any of the type enables you to get the right 
information demanded at any time. Knowledge of the types is therefore essential in our 
everyday life. The concept of oral interpretation will also be discussed. We shall discuss the 
skills needed for effective interpretation. Interpretation plays important roles in facilitating 
communication across language barriers.
At the end of the section, you should be able to:
• Identify key ideas from appropriate discourse. E.g., cultural values (respect, kindness, 
tolerance and others), education, child trafficking, environment, industrialisation in Ghana, 
mining, GESI etc.,
• Discuss ideas and relevant opinions from selected discourse. E.g., cultural values (respect, 
kindness, tolerance and others), education, child trafficking, environment, industrialisation in 
Ghana, mining, GESI, STEM, etc.
• Discuss skimming using preview, overview and review.
• Discuss scanning using the strategies (e.g., movement of eyes or finger, locating words and 
phrases)
• Apply skimming and scanning to extract information or ideas from texts
• Discuss oral interpretation focusing on effective listening, encoding and decoding,
Key Ideas
• In text, key ideas are the main messages that are relevant in any discourse. 
• Some of the key ideas may centre on cultural values such as respect, kindness, tolerance, 
patience, etc. 
• In any discourse you can share relevant opinions on any discourse appropriately and interpret 
any discourse in your own understanding.

Identification of Key Ideas in Text
Dear learner, before leaving home for your present school, what are the main points from 
the conversation you had with your parent/guardian? Share with peers.
The main points you shared with your peers are known to as key ideas. Key ideas are 
the essential ideas that the author or speaker wants to give to the reader or hearer/listener 
respectively. The ideas may include the claims, the reasons, conclusions, definitions, 
classifications, comparisons, evaluations, recommendations, etc. Key ideas can be expressed 
explicitly or implicitly.
For you to identify the key ideas in discourse there is the need for you to understand the 
main concepts, arguments, and the points made. Note that the discourse could deal with any 
topic such as mining, teenage pregnancy, natural disaster, educational issues among others. 
It must also be pointed out that it could also come in a text form, video or picture or all the 
forms mentioned.
In summary, my dear learner to identify the key ideas in a discourse which may be written 
or oral or visual, you may need to answer the following questions
• Find who or what the passage discusses: Does this passage discuss a person, 
group of people or an entity?
• Ask when the event took place: Does the information contain a reference to time?
• Find where the event took place: Does the text name a place?
• Ask why the event took place: Do you find a reason or explanation for something 
that happened?
• Ask how the event took place: Does this information indicate a method or a 
theory?
NB: In a text, key ideas are sometimes italicised, boldened, or underlined. You can also 
find it in the topic sentence.
What is discourse
Generally, discourse refers to communication, conversation or discussion between 
individuals or groups either in spoken form or written form. It involves the exchange of 
ideas, opinions and information. Note that the definition of discourse could be defined also 
from different angles such as linguistics, social science and philosophy. The general meaning 
is appropriate for us. Go online to read the other definitions to broaden your knowledge.

Key Ideas

Types of Reading
There are types of reading skill or technique namely skimming, scanning, intensive reading 
and extensive reading. Dear learner, in this lesson you shall learn skimming and scanning 
techniques of reading.
Skimming
Skimming is a reading technique used to quickly identify the main ideas or key points in a 
text. It is the action of reading something quickly so as to note only the important points. 
Basically, skimming is reading rapidly in order to get a general overview of the material 
read. It is used to find specific facts in texts. It involves glancing over the material, focusing 
on headings, subheadings, bold text and key phrases to get a general understanding of the 
content. Skimming is useful when; time is limited, looking for specific information, you 
want to get an overview before reading in-depth and you are dealing with a large amount of 
text. Below are the skimming types.
Preview: An opportunity to view something before it is acquired or becomes generally 
available. Preview is done in an effort to learn about the ideas presented and the structure 
of their development.
Overview: Used to sample the reading material more thoroughly. A general review or 
summary of a subject.
Review: The review is done to re-familiarise yourself with the material you have previously 
read thoroughly or skimmed. A formal assessment of something with the intention of 
instituting a change if necessary.

LANGUAGE USAGE
Oral Interpretation and translation
Key Ideas
• Oral interpretation is reframing the meaning of a speech most often orally into another 
language. 
• The original language is the source language and the language in which it is rendered is the 
target language. 
• In oral interpretation you must note the cultural differences and be accurate in giving the 
meaning of what you are to render in the language orally.
Oral Interpretation
Interpretation is listening to a message in one language and rendering it orally in another 
language maintaining the original meaning, tone and context. It is the stylistic representation 
of a creative work or dramatic role. It is the act of explaining, reframing, or otherwise 
showing your own understanding of something. In interpretation you first have to understand 
the text or the piece given to you and then explain in your own words. In broader terms it is 
rendering a spoken or signed message into another spoken or signed language preserving 
the register and meaning of the source language content.
Dear learner, it must be noted that before you can do any interpretation, you must be 
well versed in the source and target language. Interpretation can be performed either 
simultaneously or consecutively between users of different languages.
Dear learner, know that in interpreting you do not embellish or over-exaggerate. State the 
ideas clearly. In interpreting you need to listen carefully, decode and encode as they serve 
as the process of communication and interpreting.
What is encoding?
Encoding is the process of translating information into a form that can be transmitted to 
another person or system. It involves interpreting and understanding a text or message. It 
involves reading or receiving the text, recognize the words, phrases and sentences, interpret 
the meaning, context and intent behind the text and understand the cultural, linguistic and 
semantic nuances.
Decoding
This is the process of creating a text or message. It involves the interpretation and translation 
of coded information into a comprehensible form. This is how an audience is able to 
understand and interpret the message. Decoding can also be explained as transforming 
ideas, thoughts, or messages into spoken text.

INTRODUCTION
This section discusses identification of key ideas in texts and discourse. It always gives 
information on specific ideas or knowledge to the reader or hearer. The information given 
may come from all perspectives such as education, industrialisation, mining among others. 
It may also indicate some cultural values such as respect, tolerance and patience. Identifying 
key ideas gives you a better understanding of the discourse. It also enhances your critical 
thinking skills and interpretation abilities. There are types of reading techniques namely 
skimming and scanning and the application of any of the type enables you to get the right 
information demanded at any time. Knowledge of the types is therefore essential in our 
everyday life. The concept of oral interpretation will also be discussed. We shall discuss the 
skills needed for effective interpretation. Interpretation plays important roles in facilitating 
communication across language barriers.
At the end of the section, you should be able to:
• Identify key ideas from appropriate discourse. E.g., cultural values (respect, kindness, 
tolerance and others), education, child trafficking, environment, industrialisation in Ghana, 
mining, GESI etc.,
• Discuss ideas and relevant opinions from selected discourse. E.g., cultural values (respect, 
kindness, tolerance and others), education, child trafficking, environment, industrialisation in 
Ghana, mining, GESI, STEM, etc.
• Discuss skimming using preview, overview and review.
• Discuss scanning using the strategies (e.g., movement of eyes or finger, locating words and 
phrases)
• Apply skimming and scanning to extract information or ideas from texts
• Discuss oral interpretation focusing on effective listening, encoding and decoding,
Key Ideas
• In text, key ideas are the main messages that are relevant in any discourse. 
• Some of the key ideas may centre on cultural values such as respect, kindness, tolerance, 
patience, etc. 
• In any discourse you can share relevant opinions on any discourse appropriately and interpret 
any discourse in your own understanding.

Identification of Key Ideas in Text
Dear learner, before leaving home for your present school, what are the main points from 
the conversation you had with your parent/guardian? Share with peers.
The main points you shared with your peers are known to as key ideas. Key ideas are 
the essential ideas that the author or speaker wants to give to the reader or hearer/listener 
respectively. The ideas may include the claims, the reasons, conclusions, definitions, 
classifications, comparisons, evaluations, recommendations, etc. Key ideas can be expressed 
explicitly or implicitly.
For you to identify the key ideas in discourse there is the need for you to understand the 
main concepts, arguments, and the points made. Note that the discourse could deal with any 
topic such as mining, teenage pregnancy, natural disaster, educational issues among others. 
It must also be pointed out that it could also come in a text form, video or picture or all the 
forms mentioned.
In summary, my dear learner to identify the key ideas in a discourse which may be written 
or oral or visual, you may need to answer the following questions
• Find who or what the passage discusses: Does this passage discuss a person, 
group of people or an entity?
• Ask when the event took place: Does the information contain a reference to time?
• Find where the event took place: Does the text name a place?
• Ask why the event took place: Do you find a reason or explanation for something 
that happened?
• Ask how the event took place: Does this information indicate a method or a 
theory?
NB: In a text, key ideas are sometimes italicised, boldened, or underlined. You can also 
find it in the topic sentence.
What is discourse
Generally, discourse refers to communication, conversation or discussion between 
individuals or groups either in spoken form or written form. It involves the exchange of 
ideas, opinions and information. Note that the definition of discourse could be defined also 
from different angles such as linguistics, social science and philosophy. The general meaning 
is appropriate for us. Go online to read the other definitions to broaden your knowledge.

Identification of Key Ideas in Text
Dear learner, before leaving home for your present school, what are the main points from 
the conversation you had with your parent/guardian? Share with peers.
The main points you shared with your peers are known to as key ideas. Key ideas are 
the essential ideas that the author or speaker wants to give to the reader or hearer/listener 
respectively. The ideas may include the claims, the reasons, conclusions, definitions, 
classifications, comparisons, evaluations, recommendations, etc. Key ideas can be expressed 
explicitly or implicitly.
For you to identify the key ideas in discourse there is the need for you to understand the 
main concepts, arguments, and the points made. Note that the discourse could deal with any 
topic such as mining, teenage pregnancy, natural disaster, educational issues among others. 
It must also be pointed out that it could also come in a text form, video or picture or all the 
forms mentioned.
In summary, my dear learner to identify the key ideas in a discourse which may be written 
or oral or visual, you may need to answer the following questions
• Find who or what the passage discusses: Does this passage discuss a person, 
group of people or an entity?
• Ask when the event took place: Does the information contain a reference to time?
• Find where the event took place: Does the text name a place?
• Ask why the event took place: Do you find a reason or explanation for something 
that happened?
• Ask how the event took place: Does this information indicate a method or a 
theory?
NB: In a text, key ideas are sometimes italicised, boldened, or underlined. You can also 
find it in the topic sentence.
What is discourse
Generally, discourse refers to communication, conversation or discussion between 
individuals or groups either in spoken form or written form. It involves the exchange of 
ideas, opinions and information. Note that the definition of discourse could be defined also 
from different angles such as linguistics, social science and philosophy. The general meaning 
is appropriate for us. Go online to read the other definitions to broaden your knowledge.

Reading
Key Ideas
• Skimming is going through a text rapidly to get the general information in the text while 
scanning involves looking for a specific information in a text. 
• Scanning is a process of reading in which your eyes quickly run through a piece of text to find 
a piece of relevant information. 
• Scanning and skimming are two different concepts of reading.
Types of Reading
There are types of reading skill or technique namely skimming, scanning, intensive reading 
and extensive reading. Dear learner, in this lesson you shall learn skimming and scanning 
techniques of reading.
Skimming
Skimming is a reading technique used to quickly identify the main ideas or key points in a 
text. It is the action of reading something quickly so as to note only the important points. 
Basically, skimming is reading rapidly in order to get a general overview of the material 
read. It is used to find specific facts in texts. It involves glancing over the material, focusing 
on headings, subheadings, bold text and key phrases to get a general understanding of the 
content. Skimming is useful when; time is limited, looking for specific information, you 
want to get an overview before reading in-depth and you are dealing with a large amount of 
text. Below are the skimming types.
Preview: An opportunity to view something before it is acquired or becomes generally 
available. Preview is done in an effort to learn about the ideas presented and the structure 
of their development.
Overview: Used to sample the reading material more thoroughly. A general review or 
summary of a subject.
Review: The review is done to re-familiarise yourself with the material you have previously 
read thoroughly or skimmed. A formal assessment of something with the intention of 
instituting a change if necessary.
Learner, in skimming, you can follow these steps
• Read the title
• Read the headings and sub-headings as well as topic sentences in each paragraph
• Look for important information such as date, names and unusual words.

Scanning involves looking for a specific information in a text. It can also be said to be a 
process of reading in which your eyes quickly run through a piece of text to find a piece of 
relevant information. In scanning the reader looks for a piece of specific information. An 
example of scanning is searching for the meaning of a word in a dictionary. Scanning helps 
the reader to locate particular facts in an entire text quickly. Students often use scanning 
when solving their reading comprehension questions.
It is important to know the purpose for scanning. You should know what you are searching 
for, eg title of a book, a website, a reference material, a particular word or phrase and 
a particular story you want to read etc. You should know how the material is structures 
either alphabetically, non-alphabetically, chronologically, by category, by titles /headings, 
by textual sense, by numbers among others.
Scanning helps a learner to read more and to develop love for reading.
When to scan
1. Scan before reading
2. Scan a number of questions to identify the one which you are most comfortable 
answering
3. When searching for particular information such as date, keywords etc.
The following shows how to do scanning after getting overview of a text and identifying the 
sections of the text you want to read.
1. Start scanning the text by moving your eyes and fingers quickly over it
2. When you have identified the information, word or the phrase you are searching for, 
read the information surrounding the word carefully
3. When you identified the information that requires attention, you read it thoroughly 
slowly.

LANGUAGE USAGE
Oral Interpretation and translation
Key Ideas
• Oral interpretation is reframing the meaning of a speech most often orally into another 
language. 
• The original language is the source language and the language in which it is rendered is the 
target language. 
• In oral interpretation you must note the cultural differences and be accurate in giving the 
meaning of what you are to render in the language orally.
Oral Interpretation
Interpretation is listening to a message in one language and rendering it orally in another 
language maintaining the original meaning, tone and context. It is the stylistic representation 
of a creative work or dramatic role. It is the act of explaining, reframing, or otherwise 
showing your own understanding of something. In interpretation you first have to understand 
the text or the piece given to you and then explain in your own words. In broader terms it is 
rendering a spoken or signed message into another spoken or signed language preserving 
the register and meaning of the source language content.
Dear learner, it must be noted that before you can do any interpretation, you must be 
well versed in the source and target language. Interpretation can be performed either 
simultaneously or consecutively between users of different languages.
Dear learner, know that in interpreting you do not embellish or over-exaggerate. State the 
ideas clearly. In interpreting you need to listen carefully, decode and encode as they serve 
as the process of communication and interpreting.
What is encoding?
Encoding is the process of translating information into a form that can be transmitted to 
another person or system. It involves interpreting and understanding a text or message. It 
involves reading or receiving the text, recognize the words, phrases and sentences, interpret 
the meaning, context and intent behind the text and understand the cultural, linguistic and 
semantic nuances.
Decoding
This is the process of creating a text or message. It involves the interpretation and translation 
of coded information into a comprehensible form. This is how an audience is able to 
understand and interpret the message. Decoding can also be explained as transforming 
ideas, thoughts, or messages into spoken text.

Scanning involves looking for a specific information in a text. It can also be said to be a 
process of reading in which your eyes quickly run through a piece of text to find a piece of 
relevant information. In scanning the reader looks for a piece of specific information. An 
example of scanning is searching for the meaning of a word in a dictionary. Scanning helps 
the reader to locate particular facts in an entire text quickly. Students often use scanning 
when solving their reading comprehension questions.
It is important to know the purpose for scanning. You should know what you are searching 
for, eg title of a book, a website, a reference material, a particular word or phrase and 
a particular story you want to read etc. You should know how the material is structures 
either alphabetically, non-alphabetically, chronologically, by category, by titles /headings, 
by textual sense, by numbers among others.
Scanning helps a learner to read more and to develop love for reading.
When to scan
1. Scan before reading
2. Scan a number of questions to identify the one which you are most comfortable 
answering
3. When searching for particular information such as date, keywords etc.
The following shows how to do scanning after getting overview of a text and identifying the 
sections of the text you want to read.
1. Start scanning the text by moving your eyes and fingers quickly over it
2. When you have identified the information, word or the phrase you are searching for, 
read the information surrounding the word carefully
3. When you identified the information that requires attention, you read it thoroughly 
slowly.

LANGUAGE USAGE
Oral Interpretation and translation
Key Ideas
• Oral interpretation is reframing the meaning of a speech most often orally into another 
language. 
• The original language is the source language and the language in which it is rendered is the 
target language. 
• In oral interpretation you must note the cultural differences and be accurate in giving the 
meaning of what you are to render in the language orally.
Oral Interpretation
Interpretation is listening to a message in one language and rendering it orally in another 
language maintaining the original meaning, tone and context. It is the stylistic representation 
of a creative work or dramatic role. It is the act of explaining, reframing, or otherwise 
showing your own understanding of something. In interpretation you first have to understand 
the text or the piece given to you and then explain in your own words. In broader terms it is 
rendering a spoken or signed message into another spoken or signed language preserving 
the register and meaning of the source language content.
Dear learner, it must be noted that before you can do any interpretation, you must be 
well versed in the source and target language. Interpretation can be performed either 
simultaneously or consecutively between users of different languages.
Dear learner, know that in interpreting you do not embellish or over-exaggerate. State the 
ideas clearly. In interpreting you need to listen carefully, decode and encode as they serve 
as the process of communication and interpreting.
What is encoding?
Encoding is the process of translating information into a form that can be transmitted to 
another person or system. It involves interpreting and understanding a text or message. It 
involves reading or receiving the text, recognize the words, phrases and sentences, interpret 
the meaning, context and intent behind the text and understand the cultural, linguistic and 
semantic nuances.
Decoding
This is the process of creating a text or message. It involves the interpretation and translation 
of coded information into a comprehensible form. This is how an audience is able to 
understand and interpret the message. Decoding can also be explained as transforming 
ideas, thoughts, or messages into spoken text.

INTRODUCTION
This section discusses identification of key ideas in texts and discourse. It always gives 
information on specific ideas or knowledge to the reader or hearer. The information given 
may come from all perspectives such as education, industrialisation, mining among others. 
It may also indicate some cultural values such as respect, tolerance and patience. Identifying 
key ideas gives you a better understanding of the discourse. It also enhances your critical 
thinking skills and interpretation abilities. There are types of reading techniques namely 
skimming and scanning and the application of any of the type enables you to get the right 
information demanded at any time. Knowledge of the types is therefore essential in our 
everyday life. The concept of oral interpretation will also be discussed. We shall discuss the 
skills needed for effective interpretation. Interpretation plays important roles in facilitating 
communication across language barriers.
At the end of the section, you should be able to:
• Identify key ideas from appropriate discourse. E.g., cultural values (respect, kindness, 
tolerance and others), education, child trafficking, environment, industrialisation in Ghana, 
mining, GESI etc.,
• Discuss ideas and relevant opinions from selected discourse. E.g., cultural values (respect, 
kindness, tolerance and others), education, child trafficking, environment, industrialisation in 
Ghana, mining, GESI, STEM, etc.
• Discuss skimming using preview, overview and review.
• Discuss scanning using the strategies (e.g., movement of eyes or finger, locating words and 
phrases)
• Apply skimming and scanning to extract information or ideas from texts
• Discuss oral interpretation focusing on effective listening, encoding and decoding,
Key Ideas
• In text, key ideas are the main messages that are relevant in any discourse. 
• Some of the key ideas may centre on cultural values such as respect, kindness, tolerance, 
patience, etc. 
• In any discourse you can share relevant opinions on any discourse appropriately and interpret 
any discourse in your own understanding.

Identification of Key Ideas in Text
Dear learner, before leaving home for your present school, what are the main points from 
the conversation you had with your parent/guardian? Share with peers.
The main points you shared with your peers are known to as key ideas. Key ideas are 
the essential ideas that the author or speaker wants to give to the reader or hearer/listener 
respectively. The ideas may include the claims, the reasons, conclusions, definitions, 
classifications, comparisons, evaluations, recommendations, etc. Key ideas can be expressed 
explicitly or implicitly.
For you to identify the key ideas in discourse there is the need for you to understand the 
main concepts, arguments, and the points made. Note that the discourse could deal with any 
topic such as mining, teenage pregnancy, natural disaster, educational issues among others. 
It must also be pointed out that it could also come in a text form, video or picture or all the 
forms mentioned.
In summary, my dear learner to identify the key ideas in a discourse which may be written 
or oral or visual, you may need to answer the following questions
• Find who or what the passage discusses: Does this passage discuss a person, 
group of people or an entity?
• Ask when the event took place: Does the information contain a reference to time?
• Find where the event took place: Does the text name a place?
• Ask why the event took place: Do you find a reason or explanation for something 
that happened?
• Ask how the event took place: Does this information indicate a method or a 
theory?
NB: In a text, key ideas are sometimes italicised, boldened, or underlined. You can also 
find it in the topic sentence.
What is discourse
Generally, discourse refers to communication, conversation or discussion between 
individuals or groups either in spoken form or written form. It involves the exchange of 
ideas, opinions and information. Note that the definition of discourse could be defined also 
from different angles such as linguistics, social science and philosophy. The general meaning 
is appropriate for us. Go online to read the other definitions to broaden your knowledge.

Reading
Key Ideas
• Skimming is going through a text rapidly to get the general information in the text while 
scanning involves looking for a specific information in a text. 
• Scanning is a process of reading in which your eyes quickly run through a piece of text to find 
a piece of relevant information. 
• Scanning and skimming are two different concepts of reading.
Types of Reading
There are types of reading skill or technique namely skimming, scanning, intensive reading 
and extensive reading. Dear learner, in this lesson you shall learn skimming and scanning 
techniques of reading.
Skimming
Skimming is a reading technique used to quickly identify the main ideas or key points in a 
text. It is the action of reading something quickly so as to note only the important points. 
Basically, skimming is reading rapidly in order to get a general overview of the material 
read. It is used to find specific facts in texts. It involves glancing over the material, focusing 
on headings, subheadings, bold text and key phrases to get a general understanding of the 
content. Skimming is useful when; time is limited, looking for specific information, you 
want to get an overview before reading in-depth and you are dealing with a large amount of 
text. Below are the skimming types.
Preview: An opportunity to view something before it is acquired or becomes generally 
available. Preview is done in an effort to learn about the ideas presented and the structure 
of their development.
Overview: Used to sample the reading material more thoroughly. A general review or 
summary of a subject.
Review: The review is done to re-familiarise yourself with the material you have previously 
read thoroughly or skimmed. A formal assessment of something with the intention of 
instituting a change if necessary.
Learner, in skimming, you can follow these steps
• Read the title
• Read the headings and sub-headings as well as topic sentences in each paragraph
• Look for important information such as date, names and unusual words.

INTRODUCTION
This section discusses identification of key ideas in texts and discourse. It always gives 
information on specific ideas or knowledge to the reader or hearer. The information given 
may come from all perspectives such as education, industrialisation, mining among others. 
It may also indicate some cultural values such as respect, tolerance and patience. Identifying 
key ideas gives you a better understanding of the discourse. It also enhances your critical 
thinking skills and interpretation abilities. There are types of reading techniques namely 
skimming and scanning and the application of any of the type enables you to get the right 
information demanded at any time. Knowledge of the types is therefore essential in our 
everyday life. The concept of oral interpretation will also be discussed. We shall discuss the 
skills needed for effective interpretation. Interpretation plays important roles in facilitating 
communication across language barriers.
At the end of the section, you should be able to:
• Identify key ideas from appropriate discourse. E.g., cultural values (respect, kindness, 
tolerance and others), education, child trafficking, environment, industrialisation in Ghana, 
mining, GESI etc.,
• Discuss ideas and relevant opinions from selected discourse. E.g., cultural values (respect, 
kindness, tolerance and others), education, child trafficking, environment, industrialisation in 
Ghana, mining, GESI, STEM, etc.
• Discuss skimming using preview, overview and review.
• Discuss scanning using the strategies (e.g., movement of eyes or finger, locating words and 
phrases)
• Apply skimming and scanning to extract information or ideas from texts
• Discuss oral interpretation focusing on effective listening, encoding and decoding,
Key Ideas
• In text, key ideas are the main messages that are relevant in any discourse. 
• Some of the key ideas may centre on cultural values such as respect, kindness, tolerance, 
patience, etc. 
• In any discourse you can share relevant opinions on any discourse appropriately and interpret 
any discourse in your own understanding.

Identification of Key Ideas in Text
Dear learner, before leaving home for your present school, what are the main points from 
the conversation you had with your parent/guardian? Share with peers.
The main points you shared with your peers are known to as key ideas. Key ideas are 
the essential ideas that the author or speaker wants to give to the reader or hearer/listener 
respectively. The ideas may include the claims, the reasons, conclusions, definitions, 
classifications, comparisons, evaluations, recommendations, etc. Key ideas can be expressed 
explicitly or implicitly.
For you to identify the key ideas in discourse there is the need for you to understand the 
main concepts, arguments, and the points made. Note that the discourse could deal with any 
topic such as mining, teenage pregnancy, natural disaster, educational issues among others. 
It must also be pointed out that it could also come in a text form, video or picture or all the 
forms mentioned.
In summary, my dear learner to identify the key ideas in a discourse which may be written 
or oral or visual, you may need to answer the following questions
• Find who or what the passage discusses: Does this passage discuss a person, 
group of people or an entity?
• Ask when the event took place: Does the information contain a reference to time?
• Find where the event took place: Does the text name a place?
• Ask why the event took place: Do you find a reason or explanation for something 
that happened?
• Ask how the event took place: Does this information indicate a method or a 
theory?
NB: In a text, key ideas are sometimes italicised, boldened, or underlined. You can also 
find it in the topic sentence.
What is discourse
Generally, discourse refers to communication, conversation or discussion between 
individuals or groups either in spoken form or written form. It involves the exchange of 
ideas, opinions and information. Note that the definition of discourse could be defined also 
from different angles such as linguistics, social science and philosophy. The general meaning 
is appropriate for us. Go online to read the other definitions to broaden your knowledge.

Reading
Key Ideas
• Skimming is going through a text rapidly to get the general information in the text while 
scanning involves looking for a specific information in a text. 
• Scanning is a process of reading in which your eyes quickly run through a piece of text to find 
a piece of relevant information. 
• Scanning and skimming are two different concepts of reading.
Types of Reading
There are types of reading skill or technique namely skimming, scanning, intensive reading 
and extensive reading. Dear learner, in this lesson you shall learn skimming and scanning 
techniques of reading.
Skimming
Skimming is a reading technique used to quickly identify the main ideas or key points in a 
text. It is the action of reading something quickly so as to note only the important points. 
Basically, skimming is reading rapidly in order to get a general overview of the material 
read. It is used to find specific facts in texts. It involves glancing over the material, focusing 
on headings, subheadings, bold text and key phrases to get a general understanding of the 
content. Skimming is useful when; time is limited, looking for specific information, you 
want to get an overview before reading in-depth and you are dealing with a large amount of 
text. Below are the skimming types.
Preview: An opportunity to view something before it is acquired or becomes generally 
available. Preview is done in an effort to learn about the ideas presented and the structure 
of their development.
Overview: Used to sample the reading material more thoroughly. A general review or 
summary of a subject.
Review: The review is done to re-familiarise yourself with the material you have previously 
read thoroughly or skimmed. A formal assessment of something with the intention of 
instituting a change if necessary.
Learner, in skimming, you can follow these steps
• Read the title
• Read the headings and sub-headings as well as topic sentences in each paragraph
• Look for important information such as date, names and unusual words.

Scanning involves looking for a specific information in a text. It can also be said to be a 
process of reading in which your eyes quickly run through a piece of text to find a piece of 
relevant information. In scanning the reader looks for a piece of specific information. An 
example of scanning is searching for the meaning of a word in a dictionary. Scanning helps 
the reader to locate particular facts in an entire text quickly. Students often use scanning 
when solving their reading comprehension questions.
It is important to know the purpose for scanning. You should know what you are searching 
for, eg title of a book, a website, a reference material, a particular word or phrase and 
a particular story you want to read etc. You should know how the material is structures 
either alphabetically, non-alphabetically, chronologically, by category, by titles /headings, 
by textual sense, by numbers among others.
Scanning helps a learner to read more and to develop love for reading.
When to scan
1. Scan before reading
2. Scan a number of questions to identify the one which you are most comfortable 
answering
3. When searching for particular information such as date, keywords etc.
The following shows how to do scanning after getting overview of a text and identifying the 
sections of the text you want to read.
1. Start scanning the text by moving your eyes and fingers quickly over it
2. When you have identified the information, word or the phrase you are searching for, 
read the information surrounding the word carefully
3. When you identified the information that requires attention, you read it thoroughly 
slowly.

LANGUAGE USAGE
Oral Interpretation and translation
Key Ideas
• Oral interpretation is reframing the meaning of a speech most often orally into another 
language. 
• The original language is the source language and the language in which it is rendered is the 
target language. 
• In oral interpretation you must note the cultural differences and be accurate in giving the 
meaning of what you are to render in the language orally.
Oral Interpretation
Interpretation is listening to a message in one language and rendering it orally in another 
language maintaining the original meaning, tone and context. It is the stylistic representation 
of a creative work or dramatic role. It is the act of explaining, reframing, or otherwise 
showing your own understanding of something. In interpretation you first have to understand 
the text or the piece given to you and then explain in your own words. In broader terms it is 
rendering a spoken or signed message into another spoken or signed language preserving 
the register and meaning of the source language content.
Dear learner, it must be noted that before you can do any interpretation, you must be 
well versed in the source and target language. Interpretation can be performed either 
simultaneously or consecutively between users of different languages.
Dear learner, know that in interpreting you do not embellish or over-exaggerate. State the 
ideas clearly. In interpreting you need to listen carefully, decode and encode as they serve 
as the process of communication and interpreting.
What is encoding?
Encoding is the process of translating information into a form that can be transmitted to 
another person or system. It involves interpreting and understanding a text or message. It 
involves reading or receiving the text, recognize the words, phrases and sentences, interpret 
the meaning, context and intent behind the text and understand the cultural, linguistic and 
semantic nuances.
Decoding
This is the process of creating a text or message. It involves the interpretation and translation 
of coded information into a comprehensible form. This is how an audience is able to 
understand and interpret the message. Decoding can also be explained as transforming 
ideas, thoughts, or messages into spoken text.

the reader to locate particular facts in an entire text quickly. Students often use scanning

answering

Oral Interpretation and translation
Key Ideas
• Oral interpretation is reframing the meaning of a speech most often orally into another 
language. 
• The original language is the source language and the language in which it is rendered is the 
target language. 
• In oral interpretation you must note the cultural differences and be accurate in giving the 
meaning of what you are to render in the language orally.
Oral Interpretation
Interpretation is listening to a message in one language and rendering it orally in another 
language maintaining the original meaning, tone and context. It is the stylistic representation 
of a creative work or dramatic role. It is the act of explaining, reframing, or otherwise 
showing your own understanding of something. In interpretation you first have to understand 
the text or the piece given to you and then explain in your own words. In broader terms it is 
rendering a spoken or signed message into another spoken or signed language preserving 
the register and meaning of the source language content.
Dear learner, it must be noted that before you can do any interpretation, you must be 
well versed in the source and target language. Interpretation can be performed either 
simultaneously or consecutively between users of different languages.
Dear learner, know that in interpreting you do not embellish or over-exaggerate. State the 
ideas clearly. In interpreting you need to listen carefully, decode and encode as they serve 
as the process of communication and interpreting.
What is encoding?
Encoding is the process of translating information into a form that can be transmitted to 
another person or system. It involves interpreting and understanding a text or message. It 
involves reading or receiving the text, recognize the words, phrases and sentences, interpret 
the meaning, context and intent behind the text and understand the cultural, linguistic and 
semantic nuances.
Decoding
This is the process of creating a text or message. It involves the interpretation and translation 
of coded information into a comprehensible form. This is how an audience is able to 
understand and interpret the message. Decoding can also be explained as transforming 
ideas, thoughts, or messages into spoken text.

skills needed for effective interpretation. Interpretation plays important roles in facilitating 
communication across language barriers.

Identification of Key Ideas in Text
Dear learner, before leaving home for your present school, what are the main points from 
the conversation you had with your parent/guardian? Share with peers.
The main points you shared with your peers are known to as key ideas. Key ideas are 
the essential ideas that the author or speaker wants to give to the reader or hearer/listener 
respectively. The ideas may include the claims, the reasons, conclusions, definitions, 
classifications, comparisons, evaluations, recommendations, etc. Key ideas can be expressed 
explicitly or implicitly.
For you to identify the key ideas in discourse there is the need for you to understand the 
main concepts, arguments, and the points made. Note that the discourse could deal with any 
topic such as mining, teenage pregnancy, natural disaster, educational issues among others. 
It must also be pointed out that it could also come in a text form, video or picture or all the 
forms mentioned.
In summary, my dear learner to identify the key ideas in a discourse which may be written 
or oral or visual, you may need to answer the following questions
• Find who or what the passage discusses: Does this passage discuss a person, 
group of people or an entity?
• Ask when the event took place: Does the information contain a reference to time?
• Find where the event took place: Does the text name a place?
• Ask why the event took place: Do you find a reason or explanation for something 
that happened?
• Ask how the event took place: Does this information indicate a method or a 
theory?
NB: In a text, key ideas are sometimes italicised, boldened, or underlined. You can also 
find it in the topic sentence.
What is discourse
Generally, discourse refers to communication, conversation or discussion between 
individuals or groups either in spoken form or written form. It involves the exchange of 
ideas, opinions and information. Note that the definition of discourse could be defined also 
from different angles such as linguistics, social science and philosophy. The general meaning 
is appropriate for us. Go online to read the other definitions to broaden your knowledge.

Reading
Key Ideas
• Skimming is going through a text rapidly to get the general information in the text while 
scanning involves looking for a specific information in a text. 
• Scanning is a process of reading in which your eyes quickly run through a piece of text to find 
a piece of relevant information. 
• Scanning and skimming are two different concepts of reading.
Types of Reading
There are types of reading skill or technique namely skimming, scanning, intensive reading 
and extensive reading. Dear learner, in this lesson you shall learn skimming and scanning 
techniques of reading.
Skimming
Skimming is a reading technique used to quickly identify the main ideas or key points in a 
text. It is the action of reading something quickly so as to note only the important points. 
Basically, skimming is reading rapidly in order to get a general overview of the material 
read. It is used to find specific facts in texts. It involves glancing over the material, focusing 
on headings, subheadings, bold text and key phrases to get a general understanding of the 
content. Skimming is useful when; time is limited, looking for specific information, you 
want to get an overview before reading in-depth and you are dealing with a large amount of 
text. Below are the skimming types.
Preview: An opportunity to view something before it is acquired or becomes generally 
available. Preview is done in an effort to learn about the ideas presented and the structure 
of their development.
Overview: Used to sample the reading material more thoroughly. A general review or 
summary of a subject.
Review: The review is done to re-familiarise yourself with the material you have previously 
read thoroughly or skimmed. A formal assessment of something with the intention of 
instituting a change if necessary.
Learner, in skimming, you can follow these steps
• Read the title
• Read the headings and sub-headings as well as topic sentences in each paragraph
• Look for important information such as date, names and unusual words.

and extensive reading. Dear learner, in this lesson you shall learn skimming and scanning 
techniques of reading.
Skimming
Skimming is a reading technique used to quickly identify the main ideas or key points in a 
text. It is the action of reading something quickly so as to note only the important points. 
Basically, skimming is reading rapidly in order to get a general overview of the material 
read. It is used to find specific facts in texts. It involves glancing over the material, focusing 
on headings, subheadings, bold text and key phrases to get a general understanding of the 
content. Skimming is useful when; time is limited, looking for specific information, you 
want to get an overview before reading in-depth and you are dealing with a large amount of 
text. Below are the skimming types.
Preview: An opportunity to view something before it is acquired or becomes generally 
available. Preview is done in an effort to learn about the ideas presented and the structure 
of their development.
Overview: Used to sample the reading material more thoroughly. A general review or 
summary of a subject.
Review: The review is done to re-familiarise yourself with the material you have previously 
read thoroughly or skimmed. A formal assessment of something with the intention of 
instituting a change if necessary.

• Read the title
• Read the headings and sub-headings as well as topic sentences in each paragraph

Oral Interpretation and translation
Key Ideas
• Oral interpretation is reframing the meaning of a speech most often orally into another 
language. 
• The original language is the source language and the language in which it is rendered is the 
target language. 
• In oral interpretation you must note the cultural differences and be accurate in giving the 
meaning of what you are to render in the language orally.
Oral Interpretation
Interpretation is listening to a message in one language and rendering it orally in another 
language maintaining the original meaning, tone and context. It is the stylistic representation 
of a creative work or dramatic role. It is the act of explaining, reframing, or otherwise 
showing your own understanding of something. In interpretation you first have to understand 
the text or the piece given to you and then explain in your own words. In broader terms it is 
rendering a spoken or signed message into another spoken or signed language preserving 
the register and meaning of the source language content.
Dear learner, it must be noted that before you can do any interpretation, you must be 
well versed in the source and target language. Interpretation can be performed either 
simultaneously or consecutively between users of different languages.
Dear learner, know that in interpreting you do not embellish or over-exaggerate. State the 
ideas clearly. In interpreting you need to listen carefully, decode and encode as they serve 
as the process of communication and interpreting.
What is encoding?
Encoding is the process of translating information into a form that can be transmitted to 
another person or system. It involves interpreting and understanding a text or message. It 
involves reading or receiving the text, recognize the words, phrases and sentences, interpret 
the meaning, context and intent behind the text and understand the cultural, linguistic and 
semantic nuances.
Decoding
This is the process of creating a text or message. It involves the interpretation and translation 
of coded information into a comprehensible form. This is how an audience is able to 
understand and interpret the message. Decoding can also be explained as transforming 
ideas, thoughts, or messages into spoken text.

INTRODUCTION
This section discusses identification of key ideas in texts and discourse. It always gives 
information on specific ideas or knowledge to the reader or hearer. The information given 
may come from all perspectives such as education, industrialisation, mining among others. 
It may also indicate some cultural values such as respect, tolerance and patience. Identifying 
key ideas gives you a better understanding of the discourse. It also enhances your critical 
thinking skills and interpretation abilities. There are types of reading techniques namely 
skimming and scanning and the application of any of the type enables you to get the right 
information demanded at any time. Knowledge of the types is therefore essential in our 
everyday life. The concept of oral interpretation will also be discussed. We shall discuss the 
skills needed for effective interpretation. Interpretation plays important roles in facilitating 
communication across language barriers.
At the end of the section, you should be able to:
• Identify key ideas from appropriate discourse. E.g., cultural values (respect, kindness, 
tolerance and others), education, child trafficking, environment, industrialisation in Ghana, 
mining, GESI etc.,
• Discuss ideas and relevant opinions from selected discourse. E.g., cultural values (respect, 
kindness, tolerance and others), education, child trafficking, environment, industrialisation in 
Ghana, mining, GESI, STEM, etc.
• Discuss skimming using preview, overview and review.
• Discuss scanning using the strategies (e.g., movement of eyes or finger, locating words and 
phrases)
• Apply skimming and scanning to extract information or ideas from texts
• Discuss oral interpretation focusing on effective listening, encoding and decoding,

• In text, key ideas are the main messages that are relevant in any discourse. 
• Some of the key ideas may centre on cultural values such as respect, kindness, tolerance, 
patience, etc. 
• In any discourse you can share relevant opinions on any discourse appropriately and interpret 
any discourse in your own understanding.

LANGUAGE USAGE
Oral Interpretation and translation
Key Ideas
• Oral interpretation is reframing the meaning of a speech most often orally into another 
language. 
• The original language is the source language and the language in which it is rendered is the 
target language. 
• In oral interpretation you must note the cultural differences and be accurate in giving the 
meaning of what you are to render in the language orally.
Oral Interpretation
Interpretation is listening to a message in one language and rendering it orally in another 
language maintaining the original meaning, tone and context. It is the stylistic representation 
of a creative work or dramatic role. It is the act of explaining, reframing, or otherwise 
showing your own understanding of something. In interpretation you first have to understand 
the text or the piece given to you and then explain in your own words. In broader terms it is 
rendering a spoken or signed message into another spoken or signed language preserving 
the register and meaning of the source language content.
Dear learner, it must be noted that before you can do any interpretation, you must be 
well versed in the source and target language. Interpretation can be performed either 
simultaneously or consecutively between users of different languages.
Dear learner, know that in interpreting you do not embellish or over-exaggerate. State the 
ideas clearly. In interpreting you need to listen carefully, decode and encode as they serve 
as the process of communication and interpreting.
What is encoding?
Encoding is the process of translating information into a form that can be transmitted to 
another person or system. It involves interpreting and understanding a text or message. It 
involves reading or receiving the text, recognize the words, phrases and sentences, interpret 
the meaning, context and intent behind the text and understand the cultural, linguistic and 
semantic nuances.
Decoding
This is the process of creating a text or message. It involves the interpretation and translation 
of coded information into a comprehensible form. This is how an audience is able to 
understand and interpret the message. Decoding can also be explained as transforming 
ideas, thoughts, or messages into spoken text.

LANGUAGE AND USAGE
Lexis and Structure
INTRODUCTION
All words belong to specific word groups or classes. In this section, you will study the 
open (major) word classes, nouns, adjectives, verbs and adverbs. An understanding of word 
classes allows you to understand the function of any given word.
At the end of this section, you will be able to:
• Categorise nouns according to their types (e.g. proper, common, abstract, concrete, etc.)
• Classify adjectives into their types (e.g. demonstratives, quantifiers and qualifiers) and use 
them in sentences.
• Classify verbs into transitive, intransitive and ditransitive.
• Categorise adverbs into types (e.g. manner, place, time, degree).
Key Ideas
• Nouns are simply names of things in general. Nouns can be categorised as proper nouns, 
abstract nouns, common nouns, and concrete nouns.
• Quantifier is an adjective that provides information about nouns in terms of numbers or 
measurement.
• Qualifier, on the other hand, is an adjective that describes or qualifies a noun or pronoun.
• Predicate is an adjective that occurs after the nouns they modify.
• Verbs are words that express action or state of being. The three types of verbs are transitive, 
intransitive and ditransitive.
• Adverbs modify verbs, adjectives and other adverbs as well. Adverbs can be grouped into 
types, namely adverb of manner, adverb of place, adverb of time, adverb of frequency, adverb 
of purpose/ reason and adverb degree/intensity
Nouns and their Categories
Make a list of ten objects inside and outside your classroom in small groups. Then add two 
more words to your list of the feelings you have inside and outside the classroom. Does your 
group have the same ideas as other groups?
3

What are nouns?
A noun is a name of a person, a place, an animal, or a thing. Some nouns also refer to ideas, 
states or feelings.
Categories of nouns
Proper nouns
Proper nouns are nouns that serve as the name of a specific person, place or thing either 
natural or artificial. Proper nouns always begin with a capital letter no matter their position 
in a sentence. Some examples are:
1. People’s names: Esinam, Adole, Iddrisu, Wakil, Kofi, Akuba, Yeboah, etc.
2. Place names: Afadjato, Accra, Winneba, Tamale, Nungua, etc.
3. Days of the week: Sunday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Monday, etc.
4. Months of the year: April, May, June, August, October, December, etc.
5. Institutions: Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital, Jubilee House, University of Ghana, 
etc.
6. Names of water bodies: Pra, Volta, Densu, Ankonbra, Korle, etc.
Common nouns
These are names of ‘things’ (person, thing, place, name or concept), which are not proper 
nouns (see above). They are not capitalized except when they are found at the beginning of 
a sentence. They can be combined with determiners and other adjectives. Some examples 
include pen, book, pencil, house, building, fish, sea, bottle, kitchen, classroom.
Abstract nouns
These are words which denote concepts or states that we cannot see physically but are 
named in society. These represent ideas we do not see, smell, or touch. They usually describe 
emotions, ideas and feelings. Some examples are happiness, love, sadness, bitterness, truth, 
wisdom, etc.
Concrete nouns
These are real objects and things we can see or touch. They exist in the physical world and 
can be experienced directly. They refer to something or someone that can be perceived 
with the five senses (touching, hearing, seeing, smelling, and tasting). Some examples of 
concrete nouns are stone, table, bed, water, air, soil, piano, drum, elephant, etc.
Collective nouns
They are nouns that refer to a group. The group could be things, animals or people. Examples 
include fleet, team, choir, group, tribe, ream, library, etc. They are singular nouns despite 
referring to multiple people/things/ animals.

The concept of an adjective refers to a word that is used to modify or describe a noun. 
Adjectives refer to words that are used to provide information about the qualities that a 
person or something possesses. Some examples of adjectives are green, black, yellow, 
white, short, tall, beautiful, fluffy, big, small, slim, happy, sad, intelligent, true, etc. The 
following are examples of how some adjectives have been used in sentences.
a. I like old houses
b. The boy is tall and skinny
c. Aku is smarter than her brother
In example (a) above, the word old is describing the kind of house that the speaker likes. 
In (b) the words tall and skinny describe the physical attributes of the boy. In (c), the words 
smarter than are used in comparing Aku and her brother’s level of intelligence.
Types of adjectives
There are different types of adjectives, the principal categories you’ll study are:
1. Demonstrative adjectives
2. Comparative adjectives
3. Quantifiers
4. Descriptive or Qualifiers
Demonstrative adjectives
In this case, demonstrative pronouns (this, that, these, those) are used as adjectives because 
they specify the object being referred to (therefore modifying the noun). See the examples 
below:
a. This car is new.
b. The woman owns those houses.
c. That house belongs to my father.
d. Aku is buying these buildings.
Comparative adjectives
They are used to compare different persons or things to each other. These comparative 
adjectives include smaller, higher, bigger, smarter, more…than, less…than, etc. In the 
following examples, we have used these comparative adjectives.
a. This is a cheaper food.
b. Ama is smarter than Kofi.
c. The white car is faster than the blue one.
d. Your money is less than mine.
7
LEXIS AND STRUCTURESECTION 3
Year 1
Quantifier adjectives
These adjectives provide information about quantity. Quantifiers play the role of an adjective 
because they modify the noun by telling us how much or how many. See the following 
examples.
a. I bought some rice.
b. He cooked two eggs.
c. She needs a little sugar.
d. There are many books in my box.
Descriptive or qualifier adjectives
Descriptive or qualifier adjectives are adjectives that describe the characteristics, traits, 
or qualities that a noun possesses. They are simply adjectives that modify nouns. Most 
examples of adjectives fall under this type. See the examples below.
a. The car is old.
b. I have a small book.
c. The food is attractive.
d. I saw a big bus.
As you can see from the examples below, qualifier adjectives can be used after the noun if 
they are linked with a verb (often the verb ‘to be’)
a. The house is beautiful.
b. The watch you are wearing is nice.
c. The mangoes you are eating are fresh.
d. The tree I saw is tall.
These qualifier adjectives can also be used directly next to the nouns they modify. In 
English, they usually come before the nouns they modify, but in Ghanaian languages, they 
come after the nouns they modify as you can see in the examples below:
a. This is a beautiful house.
b. I saw a tall tree.
c. My mother bought me a nice watch.
d. I eat fresh mangoes every day.
